CounterStrike16.mp_summary:
SERVER: cs16-server, a systemd --user unit on 192.168.1.132. HLDS build 10211, protocol 48, 16 slots, YaPB 4.4.957 backfilling to 3 bots. Up on 2026-11-11 (de_cbble at 13:3x; the 16-map rotation changes every 20 min). hlds_linux holds 0.0.0.0:27018, and 'ip route get <box>' answers src 192.168.1.132.

THE ROUND: all eight XP boxes plus .186 join this one server at once, each with +connect 192.168.1.132:27018, the real HLDS port. :27015 is the a2s proxy in front of the same match and is the 'join' port in gameservers.py SERVERS. It is what the LAN browser lists, and it carried the 10/10 join on 2026-10-13, but through it every client reaches HLDS as 127.0.0.1. A direct join puts each box's own IP in rcon status and in the log's 'connected, address' line, so the IP identifies the box whatever name it arrives under. Only two machines have joined 27018 directly before: the XP Dell then at .145 (2026-08-29) and the Win7 Dell then at .246 (2026-08-31). Same client build, so it should work. If a box fails on 27018, relaunch it on :27015.

NAMES: this BCS16 repack ignores +name. On 2026-10-13 every box arrived under its cstrike\config.cfg name: '(n)Jucator - www.bcs16.ro', and .240 as 'RIAM - www.bcs16.ro'. On all nine boxes config.cfg ends with 'exec userconfig.cfg', and no box or library copy has a userconfig.cfg (checked case-insensitively, 2026-11-11). So the launcher writes name "{name}" there. This is not yet seen on hardware; if it fails, the IP still identifies the box.

MAPS: no downloads. The 16 rotation maps and de_dust2 (the unit's start map after a restart) are md5-identical in the staged client.

MENUS: at SELECT TEAM send UIKEY 5 (auto-assign), and the server logs 'joined team' at that step. Send UIKEY 6 (auto-select) only after that box's 'joined team' line appears, because on SELECT TEAM key 6 is SPECTATE. On 2026-10-13 key 5 took on 9 of 10 boxes, including .124 and the Win7 .197; .171 stayed at SELECT TEAM.

WITNESSES: A2S lists no LAN humans here. Use rcon status and the log.

.243 is excluded: the title is not deployed there (operator override).

OPTIONAL SECOND ROUND: the tree's other shortcut, Half-Life Deathmatch, can run on hldm-server. It has 12 slots, and its jk_botti bots backfill to 3 and give way to humans. The client's valve\ has no maps, so each box downloads them from the server over UDP. Use the same bat with -game valve, write valve\userconfig.cfg (valve\config.cfg also ends with exec userconfig.cfg), and connect to {host}:27021, or the 27020 proxy. That server runs 'log off', so its witness is rcon status.

launchers.bat:
@echo off
rem CounterStrike16 fleet round: join the host CS 1.6 server directly on 27018 as {name}
cd /d "C:\Games\CounterStrike16"
call "C:\Games\CounterStrike16\FLEETRES.BAT"
cd /d "C:\Games\CounterStrike16"
rem +name alone loses to cstrike\config.cfg - measured 2026-10-13 - and config.cfg ends with exec userconfig.cfg
> "C:\Games\CounterStrike16\cstrike\userconfig.cfg" echo name "{name}"
>> "C:\Games\CounterStrike16\cstrike\userconfig.cfg" echo alias fleetsb1 "+showscores; bind F6 fleetsb0"
>> "C:\Games\CounterStrike16\cstrike\userconfig.cfg" echo alias fleetsb0 "-showscores; bind F6 fleetsb1"
>> "C:\Games\CounterStrike16\cstrike\userconfig.cfg" echo bind F6 fleetsb1
set MESA_FORCE_SSE=1
start "" hl.exe -game cstrike -full -gl -w %FR_W% -h %FR_H% -condebug +name {name} +connect {host}:27018
exit
launchers.notes:
This is the staged 'Play Counter-Strike.bat' line (the box's own FLEETRES, MESA_FORCE_SSE=1, -full, -gl) plus three additions: -condebug, +connect {host}:27018 and the userconfig.cfg name.

Why -gl: without it the engine silently starts on sw.dll (measured on .143, 2026-08-31). It also overrides .240's HKCU EngineD3D=1, re-read 2026-11-11.
Why MESA_FORCE_SSE: load-bearing on .124's Mesa-based retroicd.dll, inert elsewhere.

Verified 2026-11-11 by DIRLIST/DOWNLOAD on all nine boxes:
- hl.exe 86077, FLEETRES.BAT 4917, FLEETRES.EXE 33280, hw.dll 1840440 and sw.dll 1672504 all match the library.
- No userconfig.cfg exists anywhere.
- config.cfg ends with 'exec userconfig.cfg' on every box.
- No game is running.

lanparty.py render_bat substitutes {name} -> Fleet<octet> and {host} -> 192.168.1.132 (its HOST). It needs ASCII only, which this bat is.

F5 is 'snapshot' in every box's config.cfg and in protector.cfg. The F6 scoreboard toggle is a bonus only: protector.cfg binds F6 "", and every box binds TAB to BCShield's runtime '+showscores_hook', so a plain +showscores alias may be wiped or hooked.

The 2026-10-13 version of this line (+connect :27015, no userconfig) put 10 of 10 boxes in the server.

For .197, if it comes up, this is the right launcher too.

After the round, DELETE C:\Games\CounterStrike16\cstrike\userconfig.cfg on each box. Otherwise LAN-party players stay renamed Fleet<octet>.

launchers.bat:
@echo off
rem CounterStrike16 fleet round, .186: Windows 7 32-bit on the Standard VGA driver - software renderer, direct join on 27018 as {name}
cd /d "C:\Games\CounterStrike16"
call "C:\Games\CounterStrike16\FLEETRES.BAT"
cd /d "C:\Games\CounterStrike16"
> "C:\Games\CounterStrike16\cstrike\userconfig.cfg" echo name "{name}"
>> "C:\Games\CounterStrike16\cstrike\userconfig.cfg" echo alias fleetsb1 "+showscores; bind F6 fleetsb0"
>> "C:\Games\CounterStrike16\cstrike\userconfig.cfg" echo alias fleetsb0 "-showscores; bind F6 fleetsb1"
>> "C:\Games\CounterStrike16\cstrike\userconfig.cfg" echo bind F6 fleetsb1
rem -soft is sw.dll: no OpenGL ICD is registered here and none can be - a GTX 1650 has no 32-bit Windows driver - so -gl would land on the GDI OpenGL 1.1 renderer
start "" hl.exe -game cstrike -full -soft -w %FR_W% -h %FR_H% -condebug +name {name} +connect {host}:27018
exit
launchers.notes:
Why -soft every time: .186 is an ASUS P5QL / E5300 with a GeForce GTX 1650 (10DE:1F82). It runs Windows 7 RTM 32-bit (wmic OSArchitecture=32-bit), so the card sits on Windows' Standard VGA driver. OpenGLDrivers is empty (REGREAD 2026-11-11). NVIDIA released no 32-bit drivers after Release 390, before the GTX 1650 existed, so installing a driver will not change this.

Why no run-time ICD check: the earlier reg query was removed because a Win7 WDDM driver registers its ICD in the display class key, not under OpenGLDrivers. A detector like that misroutes a Win7 box that does have a driver. Pick the launcher at plan time from HWPROFILE gpu.name instead. If .186 ever reports a real adapter, give it the XP launcher.

Untested: this software path has never run on .186. CS has never run there under Windows 7 at all (compat_mp: untested; Win7 installed 2026-10-26). GoldSrc's software renderer may refuse 1920x1080, the FLEETRES and registry mode here; if hl.exe exits or comes up wrong, retry with -w 1280 -h 960.

If it stalls black after 'Connection accepted' with -full, relaunch once with -window in place of -full. That fallback comes from a different machine: the Win7 Dell then at .246, on 2026-08-31, where a windowed join always worked. Windowed is a tool, not a pass: record it as windowed-only.

The tree matches the library: hl.exe 86077, sw.dll 1672504, FLEETRES 4917/33280. C:\fleetmp is empty or absent; lanparty.py MKDIRs it.

CounterStrike16.in_game_proof:
PRIMARY WITNESS: the server's rcon status on 192.168.1.132:27018 (procedure under server.roster_how). It lists every connected client, including ones still at SELECT TEAM, as:
  # n "<name>" <uid> STEAM_ID_LAN <frags> <time> <ping> <loss> 192.168.1.<octet>:27005
With a direct join the address is the box. The name reads Fleet<octet> if the userconfig.cfg fix took, otherwise '(n)Jucator - www.bcs16.ro' (.240: 'RIAM - www.bcs16.ro'). Bots read BOT and have no address.

THE HLDS LOG has the same events (journal, plus ~/hlds-cs16/cstrike/logs/L<MMDD><NNN>.log), in this order:
1. "<name><uid><STEAM_ID_LAN><>" connected, address "192.168.1.<octet>:27005" - this ties the uid to the box.
2. "<name><uid><STEAM_ID_LAN><>" entered the game - in the server, at SELECT TEAM.
3. "<name><uid><STEAM_ID_LAN><>" joined team "TERRORIST"|"CT" - key 5 took; the class menu follows.
Nothing is logged for key 6. A box that is spawned and playing shows in its own frame or F5 snapshot (HUD), or in later log lines naming the player.

A2S IS NOT A WITNESS FOR HUMANS. On 2026-10-13, A2S_PLAYER (cs.json, roster []) returned no names while the log already had 9 humans 'joined team' and the frames showed them at CHOOSE A CLASS. Use A2S only for the bot count. lanparty.py check's 'named_on_server' will read false for every box.

CLIENT SIDE: DOWNLOAD C:\Games\CounterStrike16\qconsole.log. -condebug writes it in the game ROOT. .124 still holds one from 2026-10-01, so check the modified time. Look for 'Connection accepted by 192.168.1.132:27018' and 'BUILD 10211 SERVER'.

ON SCREEN, once a box is past the menus: UIKEY F6 (scoreboard on, a bonus), UIKEY F5 (snapshot; bound in every config.cfg and in protector.cfg), UIKEY F6 (off). Then DOWNLOAD the newest C:\Games\CounterStrike16\cstrike\<map>NNNN.bmp, picked by time: .124 already holds 2026-09-28 cs_747, de_train and Snapshot files.

known_blockers: .243: title not deployed (operator override 'not wanted on .243', 2026-09-29). Its 165 MHz P54C is also 29% under the 233 MHz floor.

.186: no display driver, and none can be installed on this OS. GTX 1650 (10DE:1F82) on Windows 7 RTM 32-bit, running Windows' Standard VGA driver, OpenGLDrivers empty. NVIDIA's 32-bit drivers ended with Release 390, and the GTX 1650 shipped in 2019 with 64-bit drivers only. -gl needs a different card or 64-bit Windows. Only the never-tested software-renderer launcher applies. compat_render's 2026-10-01 'verified opengl' row for .186 describes the previous XP install (GeForce 7900 GT).

+name on the command line is ignored (2026-10-13). The launcher's cstrike\userconfig.cfg name rests on 'exec userconfig.cfg' being the last line of config.cfg on all 9 boxes (verified 2026-11-11). It has not yet been seen on hardware for this tree. If it fails, the direct join still identifies each box by IP.

Team and class selection is keyboard work: UIKEY 5, then UIKEY 6 only after that box's 'joined team' line. On 2026-10-13, 9 of 10 boxes took key 5 in fullscreen; .171 stayed at SELECT TEAM. A box that never takes keys can only be shown connected (rcon status plus 'entered the game'), not on a team.
risks: .124 shutdown: do not hard-kill first. Use EXEC cmd /c taskkill /im hl.exe (no /f), poll about 10 s, and only then use PROCKILL or /f (v56k_bench.graceful_kill). A TerminateProcess'd Glide process leaves a dead board mapping (c0000005 in grGlideInit for the next game, seen on CS 1.6), and a hard kill mid-frame preceded the 2026-09-24 wedge. lanparty.py run (kill_first) and lanparty.py kill both PROCKILL every game exe, .124 included: close .124's previous title gracefully before the run, and do not use lanparty kill on .124. Never use -d3d on .124; -gl keeps it on retroicd.dll.

A graceful close (WM_CLOSE or an in-game quit) rewrites cstrike\config.cfg with name Fleet<octet> and 'bind F6 fleetsb1'; PROCKILL does not. .124 is the box this recipe closes gracefully. Its pre-round config.cfg is byte-identical to the library's (verified 2026-11-11, as are .110 .133 .143 .171 .184 .186), so UPLOAD the library's cstrike\config.cfg back over it after the round. .123 and .240 carry their own edits; .240's names its player RIAM. DOWNLOAD those two first if either could exit cleanly. On every box, DELETE C:\Games\CounterStrike16\cstrike\userconfig.cfg after the round.

Key 6 on SELECT TEAM is SPECTATE. Gate it on that box's 'joined team' line. Never send RETURN or ENTER blind: a key that misses the game lands on the desktop and can launch the selected icon. Check that WINLIST's foreground is Valve001 before every UIKEY.
A2S lists no LAN humans on this server: an empty A2S roster is normal, not a failed join. rcon status is the authority. Poll A2S at most once a second (HLDS max_queries_sec 3).
lanparty.py's built-in 'cs' entry uses port 27015 (the proxy) for its packet sniff. For this direct-join round, sniff 27018, or every box reads 0 packets.

Dial 192.168.1.132. The host also holds DHCP .196 on enp129s0. HLDS sits on 0.0.0.0:27018 and its replies leave from the route's src, which is .132 ('ip route get 192.168.1.110' on 2026-11-11). Whether a GoldSrc client accepts replies from a different address than it dialled has not been measured. Re-check ip route get before the round.

Firewall: ufw ENABLED=no and nftables is inactive, but iptables cannot be read without root. LAN boxes joined the host's Q3 and Q2 servers directly 10/10 on 2026-10-13, so host INPUT does not filter UDP game ports in general. If 27018 fails for a box, use the :27015 proxy (10/10 on 2026-10-13; every client shows as 127.0.0.1).

Map rotation: mp_timelimit 20, 16 maps. A change mid-check reloads every client, up to about 45 s on the P3 boxes (.133, .184). All 16 rotation maps and de_dust2 are md5-identical client vs server, so there is no download or CRC kick. Put no wait-chain in userconfig.cfg: a pending script blocks the map-change reconnect (lan_check.py, 2026-09-28).
Auto-assign put all nine humans on TERRORIST on 2026-10-13. mp_autoteambalance evens teams at round end. Staggering key 5 by about 1 s per box lets auto-assign alternate teams.
YaPB bots leave only when humans join a team, not when they connect. Humans parked at SELECT TEAM do not displace bots. 16 slots cover 9 to 11 humans plus 3 bots either way.
Library drift, harmless here: cstrike\autoexec.cfg (library, 2026-08-29) is missing on .123 .124 .133 .143 .171 .184 .240 (DIRLIST 2026-11-11). Nothing in this round depends on it.
.240's HKCU Half-Life Settings has EngineD3D=1 (re-read 2026-11-11). The launcher's -gl overrides it. Never drop -gl, or the engine falls to sw.dll silently.
BCShield (packed DLL) blocks timerefresh and logs blocked server stufftext to SVC_BlockCommand.log (.124's copy shows the 2026-10-13 join). It does not affect the round.

server.unit: cs16-server
server.query_kind: a2s
server.roster_how:
AUTHORITATIVE: rcon status sent straight to 27018. In Python from the host:
  s = socket(AF_INET, SOCK_DGRAM); s.connect(('192.168.1.132', 27018))
  send b'\xff\xff\xff\xffchallenge rcon\n'; chal = reply[4:].split()[2]
  send b'\xff\xff\xff\xffrcon <chal> "retroadmin" status\n'
Tested 2026-11-11. The reply carries 'version : 48/1.1.2.7/Stdio 10211', then player lines '# n "name" uid uniqueid frag time ping loss adr'. Bots show uniqueid BOT and no address.

A2S, for bots only: A2S_PLAYER to 27018 answers 'A' plus a challenge first, then 'D'. The :27015 proxy answers 'D' with no challenge (tested 2026-11-11). It lists the YaPB bots ('Flying Martini', 'Brandon', 'bussemann'). It listed no LAN humans on 2026-10-13, even after they had joined a team. A2S_INFO's bots byte gives the bot count (players=3 bots=3 at check time).
server.log_how:
Journal: journalctl --user -u cs16-server --since '<launch time>' --no-pager | grep -E 'connected, address|entered the game|joined team|disconnected|Kick'. The server echoes its log lines to stdout, so they reach the journal, but retention is short: it starts 2026-11-07, and the 2026-10-13 entries are gone.

Durable copy: ~/hlds-cs16/cstrike/logs/L<MMDD><NNN>.log (server.cfg 'log on'). A new file starts at every map change, so read every file newer than the launch.

Per box, in order:
1. "<name><uid><STEAM_ID_LAN><>" connected, address "192.168.1.<octet>:27005" - maps uid to box.
2. ... entered the game
3. ... joined team "TERRORIST"|"CT" - logged at key 5, before the class menu.
There is no line for key 6. Bot lines carry <BOT>.

Quake3-TeamArena.mp_summary:
The dev host runs this title's server, and it is up. It is the systemd --user unit q3ta-server: ioq3ded from the Ubuntu ioquake3 package (version string 'ioq3 1.36+u20251228.3ef30e75+dfsg-1/Ubuntu'), started with fs_game missionpack, net_port 27962, dedicated 2 and com_legacyprotocol 68. Its config: sv_pure 0, 12 slots, FFA, timelimit 15, fraglimit 25, and 3 Hard fill bots (bot_minplayers 3, g_spSkill 4). The map rotation is mpteam1 -> mpterra1 -> mpteam6. The live server.cfg is identical to scripts/game-servers/q3ta/server.cfg. getstatus and rcon status were re-read on 2026-11-11 at about 13:45.

Which game module the server runs matters for this round. It is the retail 1.32 Team Arena vm/qagame.qvm from missionpack/pak3.pk3; server.log says 'Loading vm file vm/qagame.qvm ... found in .../missionpack/pak3.pk3'. It is NOT Debian's /usr/lib/ioquake3/missionpack/qagame.so, as scripts/game-servers/README.md claims. id's 1.32 CheckIntermissionExit clears the exit timer whenever no human is ready, and it has no human-count guard (ioq3's own g_main.c added one). So a server with only bots sits at intermission until it is restarted, and server.log shows exactly that after many restarts. With humans connected, the map advances only when a human presses ATTACK or USE (ENTER is bound to +button2): 10 s after the first human is ready, or at once if every human is ready.

Every applicable box joins with no menu work. The launcher calls the title's own FLEETRES.BAT and FLEETGL.BAT exactly as 'Play Team Arena.bat' does. It then adds +set fs_game missionpack +set name Fleet<octet> +connect 192.168.1.132:27962, with a separate profile in C:\fleetmp\q3ta.

Every box runs ioquake3.x86.exe. No box has system32\3dfxvgl.dll (case-insensitive listing of system32\3dfx*), so FLEETGL.BAT never switches to retail quake3.exe.

8 of the 9 boxes with shortcuts apply.

launchers.bat:
@echo off
rem Quake III Team Arena - fleet LAN round: joins q3ta-server {host}:27962 as {name}.
rem Engine and per-box resolution come from the title's own FLEETRES.BAT and
rem FLEETGL.BAT, exactly as Play Team Arena.bat does. The profile is isolated in
rem C:\fleetmp\q3ta so the box's own Team Arena name and binds are not overwritten.
set "Q3DIR=C:\Games\Quake3-TeamArena"
set "Q3HOME=C:\fleetmp\q3ta"
set "FR_ENGINE="
cd /d "%Q3DIR%"
call "%Q3DIR%\FLEETRES.BAT"
> "%Q3DIR%\missionpack\fleetres.cfg" echo // written by the launcher at every start - do not edit
>>"%Q3DIR%\missionpack\fleetres.cfg" echo seta r_mode "-1"
>>"%Q3DIR%\missionpack\fleetres.cfg" echo seta r_customwidth "%FR_W%"
>>"%Q3DIR%\missionpack\fleetres.cfg" echo seta r_customheight "%FR_H%"
>>"%Q3DIR%\missionpack\fleetres.cfg" echo seta r_customaspect "1"
>>"%Q3DIR%\missionpack\fleetres.cfg" echo seta r_customPixelAspect "1"
>>"%Q3DIR%\missionpack\fleetres.cfg" echo seta r_fullscreen "1"
>>"%Q3DIR%\missionpack\fleetres.cfg" echo seta r_displayRefresh "%FR_HZ%"
>>"%Q3DIR%\missionpack\fleetres.cfg" echo seta cg_fov "%FR_FOV%"
call "%Q3DIR%\FLEETGL.BAT" "%Q3DIR%\missionpack\fleetres.cfg"
if not defined FR_ENGINE set "FR_ENGINE=ioquake3.x86.exe"
if not exist "%Q3HOME%\missionpack" mkdir "%Q3HOME%\missionpack"
rem fleetmp.cfg is a +exec startup command, so it runs after every other cfg.
rem The keys this round depends on are pinned here: with an empty homepath the
rem engine falls back to a stray q3config.cfg in the install tree on .124 .133
rem .143 and .171, not to the stock default.cfg binds.
> "%Q3HOME%\missionpack\fleetmp.cfg" echo // LAN round only - written by C:\fleetmp\Quake3-TeamArena.bat
>>"%Q3HOME%\missionpack\fleetmp.cfg" echo bind ENTER "+button2"
>>"%Q3HOME%\missionpack\fleetmp.cfg" echo bind CTRL "+attack"
>>"%Q3HOME%\missionpack\fleetmp.cfg" echo bind MOUSE1 "+attack"
>>"%Q3HOME%\missionpack\fleetmp.cfg" echo bind TAB "+scores"
>>"%Q3HOME%\missionpack\fleetmp.cfg" echo set fleetsb_on "+scores"
>>"%Q3HOME%\missionpack\fleetmp.cfg" echo set fleetsb_off "-scores"
>>"%Q3HOME%\missionpack\fleetmp.cfg" echo bind F5 "say {name} in game"
>>"%Q3HOME%\missionpack\fleetmp.cfg" echo bind F6 "vstr fleetsb_on"
>>"%Q3HOME%\missionpack\fleetmp.cfg" echo bind F7 "vstr fleetsb_off"
>>"%Q3HOME%\missionpack\fleetmp.cfg" echo bind F11 "screenshotJPEG"
cd /d "%Q3DIR%"
start "" %FR_ENGINE% +set fs_homepath %Q3HOME% +set fs_game missionpack +set com_hunkMegs 64 +set logfile 2 +set r_mode -1 +set r_customwidth %FR_W% +set r_customheight %FR_H% +set r_customaspect 1 +set r_customPixelAspect 1 +set r_fullscreen 1 +set cg_fov %FR_FOV% +set name {name} +exec fleetmp.cfg +connect {host}:27962
exit
launchers.notes:
The pattern is lanparty.py 'q3' (10/10 on 2026-10-13) plus Play Team Arena.bat's fleetres.cfg block. Rendered through lanparty.render_bat, the launcher is pure ASCII with no parentheses. Its syntax is valid cmd: every echo line puts the redirect first, so there is no '1>' handle ambiguity.

File checks, 2026-11-11, DIRLIST on all 9 boxes that have the tree:
- C:\Games\Quake3-TeamArena holds FLEETRES.BAT (4917 B), FLEETRES.EXE (33280 B), FLEETGL.BAT (4094 B), ioquake3.x86.exe (1363456 B), SDL.dll (338432 B), quake3.exe and 'Play Team Arena.bat', all the same sizes as the library.
- missionpack pak0-pak3 match the library byte counts (pak0 is 351623691 B). autoexec.cfg is the library's 1521-byte copy, which execs fleetres.cfg. q3key and zz-fleetres-menus.pk3 are present.
- C:\fleetmp already exists on all 8 applicable boxes; the 10-13 launchers are still in it.

fleetres.cfg is rewritten with the same lines and values that Play Team Arena.bat and GAMERES write. FR_HZ is the persisted desktop rate. .123's current 'r_displayRefresh 100' is not stale: GAMERES today reports its persisted mode as 1280x1024@100, with hz_launcher 100.

The separate profile C:\fleetmp\q3ta uses +set fs_homepath with this same ioquake3.x86.exe, which is the method driver-bench (run_bench.py, C:\q3home) and v56k_bench already use on fleet boxes. It leaves each player's %APPDATA%\Quake3\missionpack\q3config.cfg untouched: Tozter on .123, Goofus on .143, Xypher Orion on .171, Naked Phil on .240. It also fixes two paths:
- the console log: C:\fleetmp\q3ta\missionpack\qconsole.log, unbuffered because of logfile 2;
- screenshots: C:\fleetmp\q3ta\missionpack\screenshots\shotNNNN.jpg.

The profile does NOT give every box the stock defaults. With no q3config.cfg in the homepath, ioq3 execs the next q3config.cfg on its search path:
- C:\Games\Quake3-TeamArena\baseq3\q3config.cfg on .124 (from a 2026-10-03 benchmark), .133 (08-30) and .143 (08-29);
- missionpack\q3config.cfg on .171 (from 2004).
All four were downloaded and read. Each binds ENTER to +button2, CTRL and MOUSE1 to +attack, and TAB to +scores. Everything else in them is overridden or harmless:
- name and com_hunkMegs lose to +set, because Com_StartupVariable runs again after the cfgs;
- the r_* settings lose to fleetres.cfg;
- .124's 'timedemo 1' is a CVAR_CHEAT cvar, reset when the client joins a sv_cheats 0 server;
- .124's 'com_maxfps 0' is overridden by autoexec's 125;
- 'rate 3000' is ignored for LAN clients by this ioq3 server (sv_lanForceRate).
The four binds are pinned in fleetmp.cfg anyway, because the RETURN step depends on ENTER. After the first clean exit, ioq3 writes C:\fleetmp\q3ta\missionpack\q3config.cfg and q3key, and later rounds read those instead.

com_hunkMegs 64 is the value every box's own Team Arena q3config.cfg uses. F6 and F7 go through vstr because UIKEY sends key-down and key-up back to back (agent/src/input.c); a plain +scores bind would close the scoreboard at once.

Run it with LAUNCH "C:\fleetmp\Quake3-TeamArena.bat", not EXEC. Close any running ioquake3/quake3 first; on .124, use WM_CLOSE first.

Quake3-TeamArena.in_game_proof:
1) Strongest proof, name + IP: send rcon status on UDP 27962 (packet b'\xff\xff\xff\xffrcon retroadmin status'). The reply has the columns 'cl score ping name address rate'.
- ioq3 prints the address as '^7' followed by the IP, with NO port (SV_Status_f -> NET_AdrToString, numeric host only). A box reads e.g. 'Fleet110        ^7192.168.1.110'.
- A bot reads '^7bot'. Verified live today: 'Sarge           ^7bot'.
- Strip ^ colour codes before matching. A client that is still loading shows CNCT in the ping column.

2) getstatus on 27962 lists the same Fleet<octet> names. Line 0 is 'statusResponse', line 1 is the infostring, then one line per player: <score> <ping> "<name>". Fleet boxes read ping 0 on this LAN; in the 10-13 roster, Fleet110, 123, 133 and 171 were all 0. So the bot count from gameservers.py probe_q3, which treats ping 0 as a bot, is wrong during the round. Go by name, as lanparty.py roster() does.

3) The server's log is /home/voidsstr/q3ta-server/server.log. The unit appends stdout there, and journald holds only the start line. After the latest 'Server: <map>' line, each box needs 'broadcast: print "Fleet<octet>^7 entered the game\n"'. Then send UIKEY F5 on that box, after checking that WINLIST foreground is ioquake3. The log must gain 'say: Fleet<octet>: Fleet<octet> in game', which proves the box's own input reaches the server in-game. Leave at least 2 s between F5 and F6 on a box: sv_floodProtect is 1, so the server ignores a second client command within 1 s, and +scores sends a 'score' command.

4) A per-box picture with the roster:
- send UIKEY F6 (scoreboard held open) and wait about 1 s;
- send UIKEY F11 (screenshotJPEG);
- DIRLIST C:\fleetmp\q3ta\missionpack\screenshots and DOWNLOAD the newest shotNNNN.jpg;
- send UIKEY F7.
At intermission the scoreboard shows by itself.

A running ioquake3.x86.exe is not proof. After any map change, repeat 1 and 3, because every box must re-enter the game.
known_blockers: 192.168.1.186: no 3D display driver, and none is available for this install. The GTX 1650 (10DE:1F82) runs on Standard VGA under 32-bit Windows 7 RTM, and NVIDIA has no 32-bit driver for Turing. The box needs 64-bit Windows 7 SP1 or later, or a different card.
192.168.1.243: not installed, and gated (the P166 is below the 233 MHz floor; operator override 'not wanted on .243').
risks:
The server is frozen at intermission right now. Root cause: id's 1.32 qagame.qvm needs a human to be ready before the level can exit.
- Boxes will sit on the scoreboard until one presses RETURN, or until an arrival triggers the exit, as on 2026-11-07.
- Either way, every client reloads mpterra1 mid-round. A box that is still loading can miss it, so re-check rcon status after about 90 s and relaunch any box that is missing.
- Detect intermission with: grep -E '^(Exit:|Server: )' /home/voidsstr/q3ta-server/server.log | tail -1. The last line reads 'Exit:' while the server is at intermission.

Descent3.title_display: Descent 3 (1999, v1.4) - Anarchy on the dev host's dedicated server
Descent3.mp_summary: The dev host runs descent3-server, a systemd --user unit. It starts the Docker container d3srv (retro-wine:bookworm, --net=host), which runs `wine main.exe -launched -dedicated Dedicated.cfg`: Anarchy on fury.mn3, game traffic on UDP 2092, TimeLimit 30. Live on 2026-11-11, main.exe's own GameSpy responder on UDP 20142 answered with gamever 'Retail 1.4.0', hostport 2092, numplayers 1 (only its '-Server-' slot) and maxplayers 8. Every XP box joins with the staged Join launcher's switches (-launched -nointro -pilot X -directip +connect <ip>) and needs no menu. That was proven unattended on .123 on 2026-10-02: the kept frame shows the multiplayer HUD (Network Ping 29ms, Kills/Deaths), and the server's stats file recorded the pilot. D3's menus also accept the agent's keyboard input (UIKEY drove them on .195 and .240 on 2026-09-29); only absolute mouse clicks fail. So the 'menus not automatable / needs a person' notes in requires.json, README-FLEET.txt and lan-multiplayer-status.md are out of date, and so is the game-servers README's 'answers no text query'. Three gaps stand between this and a full-fleet round. (1) MaxPlayers defaults to 8 and the server's own slot counts toward it: the join check is MultiCountPlayers() < max_players, and MultiDoGetGameInfo itself subtracts the dedicated server's slot. Only 7 of the 8 boxes fit, so raise it to 12 and restart before the round. (2) Every box flies the same staged pilot sdf.plt, so every callsign is 'sdf'. Per-box names need a per-box pilot uploaded to C:\fleetmp\Fleet<octet>.plt, which is a separate harness step that lanparty.py does not do; without it the launcher falls back to SDF. (3) No client has ever been connected across a level change on this server, so start the round right after a level end. gameservers.py's probe_d3 is only a TCP connect and reports players null. Read the roster from GameSpy on UDP 20142, dropping '-Server-', and use per-box packet counts to UDP 2092 as evidence that does not depend on names.

@echo off
rem Descent 3 - fleet MP round: join the dev host descent3-server at {host} UDP 2092 as {name}.
rem Same switches as the staged Join Descent 3 - LAN.bat, proven on .123 2026-10-02.
rem -pilot {name} uses C:\fleetmp\{name}.plt - the staged sdf.plt renamed inside; without it SDF.
cd /d "C:\Games\Descent3"
if not exist "C:\Games\Descent3\main.exe" exit
set D3PILOT=SDF
if exist "C:\fleetmp\{name}.plt" copy /y "C:\fleetmp\{name}.plt" "C:\Games\Descent3\{name}.plt" >nul
if exist "C:\Games\Descent3\{name}.plt" set D3PILOT={name}
call "C:\Games\Descent3\FLEETRES.BAT"
cd /d "C:\Games\Descent3"
if /i "%FR_UE1DEV%"=="GlideDrv.GlideRenderDevice" reg add "HKLM\Software\Outrage\Descent3" /v PreferredRenderer /t REG_DWORD /d 2 /f >nul
set D3CAP=
set D3HZ=0

server.unit: descent3-server
server.query_kind: GameSpy status query on UDP 20142, answered by main.exe 1.4's built-in responder (binary strings -gamespyport, gamespy.cfg, \final\, \queryid\%d.%d). The default port 20142 is confirmed live. The reply carries gamename descent3, gamever, hostname, hostport, mapname, gametype, numplayers, maxplayers, then player_N/frags_N/deaths_N/team_N/ping_N, then final and queryid; \basic\, \info\, \players\ and \rules\ also answer. gameservers.py probe_d3 is only a TCP connect to 2092 (the remote-console listener) and reports players null.
server.roster_how: UDP sendto(b'\\status\\', ('192.168.1.132', 20142)). Read packets until one contains b'\\final\\' (2 s timeout; each reply ends in a NUL, so strip it). Then kv = txt.split('\\')[1:] and d = dict(zip(kv[0::2], kv[1::2])). Players are d['player_%d'] for i in range(int(d['numplayers'])), with ping_%d, frags_%d and deaths_%d. Drop the entry named '-Server-' (team -1, ping 0): it is the dedicated server's own observer slot and is counted in numplayers. Each remaining name is a pilot callsign: Fleet<octet> with the uploaded pilot, 'sdf' without it. lanparty.py's GameSpy branch works pointed at port 20142, but it marks '-Server-' as a human for this key, so exclude it by name. Measured idle on 2026-11-11 ~13:30: gamever 'Retail 1.4.0', hostname 'Dedicated Server!', hostport 2092, mapname fury.mn3, gametype Anarchy, numplayers 1, maxplayers 8. GameSpy's timelimit field reads 0 even though TimeLimit=30 is in force, so don't read the level timer from it.
server.log_how: No log line carries a client name or IP. The unit appends only the docker client's stdout to ~/descent3-server/server.log ('[entry] ...' and wine lines, the same as docker logs d3srv), and journalctl --user -u descent3-server shows only unit start/stop. Live names: the GameSpy roster above. Live per-box traffic without names: count UDP to 192.168.1.132:2092 per source IP (worktree lanparty.py sniff/check: tcpdump -i enp129s0 via sudo -S with ~/.fleet-sudo; not yet exercised). Durable record after each level end: cat "$(ls -t ~/descent3-server/netgames/*.stats | head -1)". It lists '[Rank] [Name] [Score] [Kills] [Deaths] [Suicides] [Time In Game]' per callsign. A '*' marks a player no longer connected, and such ghost records persist until the server restarts. Files are root-owned but readable.
server.bots_note: No bots are possible: neither dmfc.dll nor main.exe has bot code (game-servers skill), and Anarchy has no robots. The only non-human entry is '-Server-', which permanently takes 1 of the max_players slots and never yields, so the effective client capacity is MaxPlayers - 1.
server.changes_needed: Before an 8-box round, append MaxPlayers=12 to ~/descent3-server/Dedicated.cfg with a CRLF line end like the rest of the file. That is the server's own copy, md5-identical to the library's; the key is absent now, so the default 8 applies and leaves 7 client slots. Then run systemctl --user restart descent3-server. MaxPlayers is CVAR_GAMEINIT (read only at start) and is clamped to 2..MAX_PLAYERS; only the disabled DEMO line caps it at 16, and 12 is inside either range. Confirm the GameSpy reply says maxplayers 12, TCP 2092 is LISTENing again, and the watchdog did not bounce the unit. 12 also covers .145 and .197. The server config is not in git (there is no scripts/game-servers/descent3/), so record the change in the fleetbook. RedAlert2.title_display: Command and Conquer - Red Alert 2 - LAN, peer-hosted
RedAlert2.mp_summary:
Westwood peer-to-peer LAN. RA2's LAN code speaks IPX. The tree's own wsock32.dll (the Understorm/CnCNet-pattern shim, md5 a195155a1a31995e1eb685854acac3dc) implements socket/bind/sendto/recvfrom itself over ws2_32 and carries the traffic as UDP, so the NWLink IPX that agent 1.97.0 installed on the XP boxes is bypassed.

There is no server for this title on 192.168.1.132: no row in gameservers.py SERVERS, no unit in ~/.config/systemd/user, no container, and nothing listening on UDP 1234-1237 (ss -ulnp).

There is no join switch either. game.exe's switch table is -WIN -16 -480 -%dX%d -ATTRACT -MESSAGES -STEALTH -NOROUTER -NETGEAR -DLINK1 -SPEEDCONTROL -DROP= -MPDEBUG -SOCKET -DESTNET -CD -play -record -noaudio -nostr -str. None of them connects, and the CnCNet spawner is not in the tree. So one box hosts in the in-game LAN lobby and the rest join there, all by agent UICLICKs.

A game seats at most 8 players. MPMaps MaxPlayers tops out at 8, and the bonus .mmx maps Roulette, Death and PowdrKeg are 2-8 as well. The 8 XP boxes with the shortcut fill it exactly; .240 hosts. RA2 1.006 also has an observer slot (game.exe: GUI:Observer, GUI:OpenObserver, 'Sending observer slot of 8'). On maps under 8 players it shows as the bottom row, and it is not a player seat.

launchers.bat:
@echo off
rem Red Alert 2 LAN round. Peer game, no host server: .240 hosts in the LAN lobby, the other seven join there.
cd /d "C:\Games\RedAlert2"
rem per-box LAN name - RA2 reads [MultiPlayer] Handle from RA2.INI
"C:\Games\RedAlert2\FLEETRES.EXE" -ini "C:\Games\RedAlert2\RA2.INI" MultiPlayer Handle {name}
rem preselect an 8-player Battle map for whoever hosts - MPMaps.ini MultiMaps index 27
"C:\Games\RedAlert2\FLEETRES.EXE" -ini "C:\Games\RedAlert2\RA2.INI" LAN ScenIndex 27
call "C:\Games\RedAlert2\Launch Red Alert 2.bat"
launchers.notes:
LAUNCH EVERY BOX EXACTLY ONCE. The same file goes on every box, including the host. This entry is .240's launch; host_box.command is not a second one. Here is why it matters. lanparty.py run starts a title's host.bat first, then every box in its bats, and passes kill_first=[] for the host box. So .240 listed in both places gets two copies with nothing killed in between. When the second copy's 'start /wait Ra2.exe' returns, the staged bat's own last lines (taskkill /f /im Ra2.exe, taskkill /f /im game.exe) kill the host's real game by image name. Put .240 in one place only, or run lanparty.py with --no-host. ScenIndex only matters to whoever presses New. {host} is unused because RA2 finds the host's game by LAN broadcast.

Start it with LAUNCH (GUI), as lanparty.py does (it uploads C:\fleetmp\<key>.bat and sends LAUNCH "<path>"; {name} becomes Fleet<octet>). The cd /d is required: the staged launcher runs 'start /wait Ra2.exe -speedcontrol' from the current directory. Everything the staged launcher does stays intact:
- the per-box Serial, written only if absent;
- FLEETRES.BAT;
- RA2.INI [Video] = FR_W x FR_H;
- Ra2.exe -speedcontrol, with no -WIN, so fullscreen;
- the taskkill lines afterwards.

The Handle preset. FLEETRES.EXE -ini <file> <section> <key> <value> is a bare WritePrivateProfileStringA (provisioning/fleetres/fleetres.c) with no side effects. The staged FLEETRES.EXE has the same md5 as the repo build (926d37e05132eee59894a6fc9a5d0e54). It adds Handle to [MultiPlayer], which no box has today (RA2.INI read on all 9). 'Handle' sits in game.exe's and gamemd.exe's [MultiPlayer] key cluster beside SideEx, ColorEx, LastNickSlot, WOLLimitResolution and PhoneIndex, all keys the staged ra2.ini [MultiPlayer] already carries. It is very likely, not proven on hardware, to be the lobby's 'Your Name' field.

The ScenIndex preset. ra2.mix's MPMaps.ini [MultiMaps] starts 1=MP02T2 Isle of War, which is what ScenIndex=0 produced on 09-01. Zero-based index 27 is MP22S8 'Arctic Circle (2-8)' if the list is unfiltered. If the list is filtered to standard (Battle) maps it is MP32S8 'Heck Freezes Over (2-8)': MP21S2 and MP10S4 are the only non-standard entries before it. Both have MaxPlayers=8. Unverified: if the bonus .mmx maps sit before the MPMaps entries, the index lands elsewhere. Read the Host Screen panel.

After the launch the agent drives the lobby (see host_box and first_run). Click at shell coordinate + offset. The offset is ((W-800)/2,(H-600)/2) for the mode RA2 sets, which is FR_W x FR_H, the GAMERES 'wide' target. It is already in each box's RA2.INI (read 2026-11-11):
- .240: +560,+240 (1920x1080)
- .110: +400,+300 (1600x1200)
- .123/.124/.133/.143/.171: +240,+180 (1280x960)
- .184: +112,+84 (1024x768)
The centring is measured at two sizes. The 09-01 frames put the shell at 560,240 in 1920x1080, and the 08-31 .143 frame bounds it at 112,84-910,682 in 1024x768. Confirm from the box's SCREENSHOT size at the main menu.

Shell points, measured on the 09-01 1920x1080 frames:
- main menu: Network 719,304; logo for the focus click 316,200
- lobby: Your Name 283,86; Games list row 2 (first hosted game) 427,161; New 719,220; Join 719,262
- Host Screen: Start Game 719,262; Customize Battle 719,304
- Join Screen: Accept 719,262

Avoid the bottom button at 719,556 on every screen (Exit Game / Main Menu / Back).

Cleanup: PROCKILL the game.exe whose parent is Ra2.exe, then Ra2.exe if it is still alive; the bat's cmd then exits by itself. Kill by PID only. Tiberian Sun also runs as GAME.EXE, and on .124 a cmd.exe is the agent's own watchdog (parent of retro_agent.exe and a ping.exe). Afterwards confirm each box is back at its persisted desktop mode (DISPLAYCFG get, or GAMERES live vs persisted). A killed exclusive-mode game can leave the desktop at the game's mode.

Optional Yuri's Revenge round: the same pattern with RA2MD.INI and 'Launch Yuri's Revenge.bat'. Its processes are RA2MD.exe and gamemd.exe (09-28 sweep). Everyone in a round must run the same game: RA2 and YR clients cannot see each other. host_box.command:
No separate launch. .240 is started ONCE by the launchers entry (LAUNCH C:\fleetmp\RedAlert2.bat, the same file as the joiners). After ~45 s, and a screenshot showing the Main Menu, run these at 1920x1080 (shell offset +560,+240):
1. UICLICK 876 440 (focus: the decorative logo), then WINLIST. The foreground pid must be game.exe's.
2. UICLICK 1279 544 (Network) -> 'Lobby'. Your Name must read Fleet240.
3. UICLICK 1279 460 (New) -> 'Host Screen'. The map panel under 'Battle' must end '(2-8)', and the 8 player rows must read Fleet240 + 7 Open. If they do not, fix it before anyone joins: UICLICK 1279 544 (Customize Battle) and pick a (2-8) map by sight.
4. Wait while the joiners join and accept. If that takes more than ~8 minutes, UICLICK 600 740 (empty panel background) so the screensaver does not start.
5. When all eight names are in player rows, with none in an Observer row: UICLICK 1279 502 (Start Game).

A peer game: .240's own game.exe IS the host and a player. There is no separate server process, so nothing competes for a port.

Why .240:

RedAlert2.in_game_proof:
There is no server roster; the host's screens are the roster.

1. Before Start: a screenshot of the host .240's Host Screen with all eight names in its player rows (Fleet110, Fleet123, Fleet124, Fleet133, Fleet143, Fleet171, Fleet184, Fleet240) and the map panel ending '(2-8)'. Each name comes from that box's own RA2.INI Handle, so a name proves that box. A name in an Observer row is not a player. Add each joiner's own Join Screen frame showing its row.

2. After Start, take both of these:
   - Every box's own frame shows the RA2 battlefield with the sidebar at its own full mode, not the 800x600 shell.
   - On the host, UIKEY TAB opens the Diplomacy screen, which lists all active players by name, with colour and kills. Screenshot it.

3. Optional: each joiner sends '\' + 'Fleet<octet> in' + RETURN, and the line appears on the host's screen within a few seconds. The 08-31 run proved .143 this way ('JOIN143: LAN OK FROM 143' on .246's screen).

A running game.exe proves nothing. RA2 is lockstep: a box that drops shows up on every other screen as a disconnect or wait message, which is the failure signal.
RedAlert2.screenshot_notes:
XP GDI SCREENSHOT works for RA2, in the shell and in-game. Evidence:
- the 09-01 frames on .123 and .240 at 1920x1080 (shell and in-game);
- the 08-31 .143 frames at 1024x768;
- FLEET-NOTES' Yuri in-game frame at 1920x1080 on .240.
RA2 is 16-bpp, so colours are right (not the 8-bit confetti case).

The menu is an 800x600 shell centred in the box's full mode, so judge resolution from the in-game frame, never the menu. Use SCREENSHOT 1 (half size) while driving the lobby and double the coordinates you read off it.

.124 (vcr-kmd): lanparty.py already takes C:\vcr\vcrctl.exe fbshot there and falls back to GDI if it fails (vcrctl.exe is present, DIRLIST 2026-11-11). That is fine, but GDI is not shown to be unreliable for this title. The two items once cited for that are not evidence about vcr-kmd. The 08-31 compat row ('GDI SCREENSHOT is black') was measured while .124 still had its GeForce2 GTS. The 09-28 01:54 smoke frame shows the desktop because RA2 had already exited after the ESC presses.

The vcr-kmd evidence points the other way. The 09-28 23:51 lan_sweep run took GDI SCREENSHOT 0 frames at 1280x960: mean 23.0 / sd 47.9 at 30 s, 22.4 / 47.7 at 60 s. A 1280x960 centred crop of the 09-01 RA2 main menu measures 23.0 / 47.8, and .124's desktop measures 18.8 / 49.0. So GDI almost certainly captured the menu. RA2 is DirectDraw with software emulation (aqrit ForceDirectDrawEmulation=1 on XP), not D3D. Take one frame each way in the first round and keep whichever shows the game.

Fallback on any box: UIKEY PRINTSCREEN in-game writes C:\Games\RedAlert2\SCRN0000.pcx. DOWNLOAD it, then DELETE it, because GAMESYNC never deletes files.
known_blockers: No join from the command line and no host server. Every one of the 8 boxes must be walked through the LAN lobby by agent clicks: Network, then New on the host or select + Join + Accept on the joiners, then Start Game. It has been done with 2 boxes three times (.123+.240 on 2026-08-29, .246+.143 on 2026-08-31, .123+.240 on 2026-09-01) and never with more.

RA2 LAN seats 8 players: MaxPlayers tops out at 8, and only a (2-8) map gives 8 player rows; the observer slot is not a seat. 9 online boxes carry the shortcut, so .186 sits out. .145 and .197 must stay out if they are switched on.

The default LAN map, Isle of War (2), seats only 2. The host needs an 8-player Battle map before anyone joins. The launcher presets [LAN] ScenIndex=27, which is unverified; the fallback is Customize Battle by sight.
risks: Never press ESC. In the shell it is the back key (Exit Game on the main menu, leave-room in the lobby); in-game it opens the Options menu. The .124 lan_check smoke that pressed ESC at 20 s and 28 s found RA2 gone by 40 s (cause likely, not proven).

Launch each box once. .240 must not be started both as the host and as a launcher box. The staged bat ends with taskkill /f /im Ra2.exe and taskkill /f /im game.exe, so a second copy whose Ra2.exe returns early kills the host's game.
Focus: the game can start behind the agent or bat console. This was measured on .124 for RA2, YR and TS. Click the game once and check the WINLIST foreground pid before any key.

Screensaver: ssstars.scr runs on all 8 XP boxes now and re-arms after 600 s without input. PROCKILL it by PID before launching, and give every box a harmless input at least every ~8 minutes. SCREENSHOT is not input.
Name preset unverified: 'Handle' is inferred from the [MultiPlayer] key cluster in game.exe. If the lobby shows [New Player], type the name as the 09-01 run did.

Map preset unverified: ScenIndex semantics are inferred from MPMaps.ini order. Index 27 is an 8-player Battle map whether or not the list is filtered to Battle maps, but not if the bonus .mmx maps come first. Read the Host Screen panel.

Observer slot: RA2 1.006 has one (game.exe GUI:OpenObserver, 'Sending observer slot of 8'). On a map under 8 players the bottom row is that slot, so a 6-player map seats 6 players + 1 observer. Only a (2-8) map seats all eight.

.124 (Voodoo 5 6000 on vcr-kmd): RA2 is DirectDraw software emulation, not D3D, so the D3D HAL is not involved. RA2 reached its menu there at 1280x960 on 2026-09-28 (Ra2.exe and game.exe alive at 30 s and 60 s; the GDI frame stats match the menu) but was never driven past the menu. The 1280x960x16 mode switch goes to a 1998 CRT. The box has 255 MB RAM. Its tree has an extra ddraw.dll.wrapper.bak, the same size as the live ddraw.dll, which matches the library.

This is the first RA2 LAN since agent 1.97.0 put NWLink IPX on every XP box. The tree's wsock32.dll implements socket/bind/sendto/recvfrom itself (importing only WSASocketA/WSASendTo/WSARecvFrom and forwarding the rest to ws2_32), so discovery should still go over UDP. All 8 boxes report ipx active, so they are at least consistent. If a joiner cannot see Fleet240's game, check this first.
Lockstep: the match runs at the slowest box's pace. .133 (P3-700, 1280x960) and .184 (P3-845, GeForce2 32 MB, 1024x768) run software-emulated DirectDraw. Slow, but expected to hold.

.110 (1600x1200) and .184 have never been verified to render RA2. .110 has never launched it at all (no Westwood serial yet), so screenshot it before the first click. The top-level files of all 9 trees match the library by size (DIRLIST 2026-11-11). ra2.ini and RA2MD.INI differ only by GAMERES' [Video] edit, and subfolders were not compared.

Westwood serials: 7 boxes hold distinct values. .110 has none yet. Its launcher will mint 1720050557 from C: volume 1C20-C57D (re-read 2026-11-11), which collides with none. Two boxes with the same serial get 'There is already a player with your serial# in that game.'

.123 was flagged fragile on 2026-09-01: it rebooted twice during a long run of fullscreen mode switches, one of which was RA2 at 1920x1080x16. It has since been activated and moved to a CRT (desktop 1280x1024, RA2 at 1280x960), and it ran all 7 titles in the 10-13 ten-box run.
Simultaneous joins can collide, so stagger them. The host must not change options after joiners accept, because that resets every Accept.
Kill by PID only: game.exe is also Tiberian Sun's image name, and on .124 a cmd.exe is the agent's own watchdog (parent of retro_agent.exe and a ping.exe).
retro_chat.exe runs on .133, .143 and .240. If a chat prompt arrives mid-round, its window may take the foreground from the exclusive-mode game.

wuauclt.exe (Windows Update client) runs on .110, .123, .133 and .184 (PROCLIST 2026-11-11). A notification can take the foreground. The bench quiesce kills it; PROCKILL it by PID if a box keeps losing focus.

The launcher's RA2.INI edits (Handle, ScenIndex) make the next GAMESYNC recopy ra2.ini once, because the GAMERES ledger no longer matches. That churn is harmless. The game also rewrites ra2.ini on a clean exit.
After PROCKILL, check each box is back at its persisted desktop mode. A killed exclusive-mode game can leave the desktop at the game's mode.
.143's live desktop is 1024x768, while its persisted/panel mode is 1280x1024. RA2 still gets the persisted target, 1280x960.

Set {host} = 192.168.1.123, the haloded box. UPLOAD this as C:\fleetmp\Halo.bat and LAUNCH "C:\fleetmp\Halo.bat" (the lanparty.py pattern; render_bat turns {name} into Fleet<octet>).

- '-name {name}'. halo.exe 0x4c9c80 reads it only after -connect, and it only SELECTS an existing profile whose stored name matches. With no Fleet<octet> profile it does nothing (verified in code).

KEEP the reg import line. It is what moves .110, .123 and .240 off the library key, which their registries hold today and which is .171's key. .171 has no box-local file and plays on the library key, which stays unique only while every other box imports its own.

> "C:\Games\Halo\dedinit.txt" echo sv_public 0

reg add "HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Microsoft Games\Halo" /v ExitFlag /t REG_SZ /d clean /f >nul 2>&1

host_box.notes:
STAGING, done by the round (box-local, not a library edit; NOT done by this scout):
1. UPLOAD C:\Games\Halo\haloded.exe with the bytes of /mnt/retro-share/Files/tmp/halo-build/_patch/haloded.exe (2,342,912 B, md5 e1333f5597aae7bb3dde70c473499d23, FileVersion 01.00.10.0621, the same as the staged halo.exe). DIRLIST C:\Games\Halo to confirm the size. .123 has no share mapped (SYSINFO lists no network drive), so UPLOAD is the reliable route.
2. UPLOAD this batch as C:\fleetmp\Halo-host.bat (lanparty.py names it <key>-host.bat) and LAUNCH it. It refuses unless haloded.exe has the exact size and Strings.dll and MAPS\bloodgulch.map are present. It then writes dedinit.txt, resets ExitFlag and starts the server in its own console, which renames itself 'Halo Console (1)'.

WHY THESE FLAGS (checked in haloded's code):
- -exec is fopen(arg, "r") (0x4eb030 -> 0x4eb0c0), relative to the current directory, defaulting to init.txt; hence the cd /d. Lines split on CR, LF and TAB, so CRLF is fine.
- -path replaces <My Documents>\My Games\Halo (0x466a60), keeping the server's files apart from .123's client profile. It does NOT separate the registry: both binaries share HKCU ...\Halo\ExitFlag, hence the reset.
- haloded will not start without strings.dll ('Invalid / missing strings.dll') and needs MAPS, so it runs from the tree.
- The first four dedinit lines are exactly the 09-29 file. 'sv_timelimit 0' is the one untested addition. haloded's help says 0 = infinite and -1 = default, so it stops the game ending into 'Game Complete. Dedicated server is now idle.'. Drop it if the server misbehaves.

READINESS, 15-30 s after LAUNCH and BEFORE any client starts:
- PROCLIST shows haloded.exe and no halo.exe.
- EXEC cmd /c netstat -ano -p udp | find ":2302" shows 0.0.0.0:2302 owned by haloded's PID. Halo's client also binds 2302 even at its menu, so this check means nothing once a client runs on .123.
- From the dev host, send the 8 bytes \status\ to 192.168.1.123:2302. Expect \hostname\Retro Fleet LAN ... \numplayers\0 ... \maxplayers\16 (server.roster_how).
- If nothing binds, run WINLIST on .123. A 'Halo - Warning' window owned by haloded.exe is the unclean-exit dialog; UIKEY RETURN = Continue Anyway. A console line 'Another application is using port 2302' means a halo.exe holds the port: WM_CLOSE it and relaunch this batch.
- Windows Firewall is off on .123 (EnableFirewall=0 in both profiles, read 2026-11-11).

WHY .123: it is the fastest XP box (Athlon 64 4000+, 2 GB, HD 3850) and it played in the 09-29 game. Its own key is fleet-gamekey-halo-pc-5 (audit fp ac1e7504ab). Caveats: one logical CPU, unlike the 4-core 09-29 host, and two drops off the LAN mid-session on 2026-09-01.

FALLBACK HOST .110 (P4 2.8 GHz, one logical CPU, 1150 MB, firewall off): repeat steps 1-2 there and relaunch every client with {host}=192.168.1.110. .110 then gets the -port 2304 -cport 2305 client, and .123 the plain one.

TEARDOWN:
1. Close every client with EXEC cmd /c taskkill /pid <halo.exe pid>, without /f (WM_CLOSE). Halo exits clean and writes ExitFlag=clean.
2. Then EXEC cmd /c taskkill /f /im haloded.exe; XP will not end a console process without /f.
3. REGREAD HKCU Software\Microsoft\Microsoft Games\Halo afterwards should read ExitFlag=clean.
GAMESYNC never deletes, so haloded.exe, dedinit.txt and ded\ stay in .123's tree. That is harmless, but they are not in the library.

server.query_kind:
GameSpy qr2 on the game port, plus its qr1-compatible legacy branch. From a static reading of haloded.exe:
- The game-socket classifier (0x45b14d-0x45b17e) passes a datagram to the qr2 parser 0x5982a0 when it starts with '\' (legacy), ';' (CD key) or FE FD (qr2).
- The FE FD path (0x59834c) needs length >= 7, a type byte 0..6 and a 4-byte instance id.
- The '\' path (0x59830e -> 0x598160) answers ANY backslash query with all server, player and team keys.
- qr2 is initialised at 0x58d79a with the public flag as a parameter, so sv_public 0 should not silence it.
The '\status\' string the earlier recipe cited is the client-side query sender (0x5a28a4), not this handler. None of this has been run live, and gameservers.py PROBES has no Halo probe.
server.roster_how:
Simplest, and already parsed by scripts/fleet/lanparty.py: the legacy GameSpy query. Send the 8 ASCII bytes \status\ over UDP to 192.168.1.123:2302.

The reply is one datagram of \key\value pairs:
- server keys first (hostname, numplayers, maxplayers, mapname, gametype, ...);
- then player_0, score_0, ping_0, team_0 ... (formatted '%s%d' at 0x597fed);
- ending \final\\queryid\1.1.

This worktree's modified lanparty.py roster() sends to host_ip_of(t), the host box, when the title has host.box set. So a title entry with query ["gamespy", 2302] and host.box 123 works unchanged. The committed HEAD version still sends only to 192.168.1.132.

Native alternative, qr2:
  s.sendto(b'\xfe\xfd\x00\x77\x6a\x9d\x9d\xff\xff\xff', ('192.168.1.123', 2302))
Expect d[0] == 0 and d[1:5] == the id, then NUL-separated rules up to an empty key, then the player section. Parse it defensively.

Names are each box's Halo PROFILE name, not Fleet<octet>:
- .123 is 'New001' and .171 is 'Carter';
- .110, .124 and .240 have no savegames folder (read 2026-11-11), so they join under a default name, likely also 'New001'.
So match numplayers against the number of boxes launched, and identify boxes by screenshot, unless Fleet<octet> profiles are seeded (first_run).

first_run.symptom: 'Halo - Warning' dialog at startup: 'the game did not exit correctly ... safe mode' (Strings.dll dialog 102, string 106). It is driven by HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Microsoft Games\Halo\ExitFlag. Each start moves clean -> 'bad 1' -> 'bad 2', a clean exit writes 'clean', and only 'bad 2' raises the dialog. On a client box it therefore follows TWO consecutive unclean exits (PROCKILL, taskkill /f or a crash). On the HOST box, haloded.exe and halo.exe share the flag and run the same check, so one forced kill of both is enough, and haloded then waits at this dialog before binding 2302.
first_run.keys: UIKEY RETURN
first_run.notes:
Every launcher here prevents it with 'reg add ... ExitFlag clean'. All five boxes read 'clean' on 2026-11-11.

If it still appears, first confirm with WINLIST that the foreground window is 'Halo - Warning', owned by halo.exe or haloded.exe. It is an ordinary Win32 dialog, so keys reach it. The en-US tab order is 'Continue Anyway' (DEFPUSHBUTTON, id 1004, first tab stop) -> 'Continue in Safe Mode' -> 'Exit' -> the checkbox 'Don't show this warning again'. RETURN = Continue Anyway, after which halo.exe goes on to -connect.

To also tick the checkbox: TAB, TAB, TAB, SPACE, then TAB (it wraps to Continue Anyway) and SPACE.

If both Continue buttons are greyed and only Exit is live, that is the product-key FATAL. Re-run scripts/halo/assign_keys.py for that box; keys will not fix it.

first_run.symptom: Black screen with an 'ATTENTION - Your CD Key is invalid.' box in Halo's shell after -connect (string in MAPS\ui.map).
first_run.keys: none (the shell ignores UIKEY and UICLICK)
first_run.notes:
One of two causes:

review_issues: host_box.command cannot be launched as a batch file. It mixes prose with two files. Pasted verbatim as the host .bat (lanparty.py uploads host.bat as-is), line 1 'C:\fleetmp\HaloHost.bat (start it with LAUNCH ...):' runs that same batch again without CALL. The batch then hands control to itself and loops, so haloded never starts, and the dedinit.txt lines would run as commands. Fixed: command is now the batch alone, and it writes dedinit.txt itself.

halo.exe and haloded.exe share HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Microsoft Games\Halo\ExitFlag, so either can raise the 'did not exit correctly' dialog. Both run the same check (haloded 0x595250 called at 0x55a2f6; halo.exe 0x57e850 at 0x541725). Each start moves the flag clean -> 'bad 1' -> 'bad 2', and only 'bad 2' raises Strings.dll dialog 102 / string 106. So the teardown claim 'taskkill /f haloded - a console app, so no crash-recovery dialog follows' is false. On the host box one forced kill of both processes leaves 'bad 2'; lanparty.py run does exactly that, PROCKILLing every game exe on the host box before relaunching it. The next haloded start then waits at a modal dialog before binding 2302, and every client gets 'Unable to join game'. On a client box the dialog needs TWO consecutive unclean exits, not one as first_run said. Fixed: every launcher now resets ExitFlag to 'clean' first, and first_run documents the haloded case. All five boxes read ExitFlag=clean on 2026-11-11.

The host setup itself is untested, and the recipe does not say so. The proven 09-29 host was .145, a 4-core i5-2400 (docs/fleet-inventory.md). .123 and the alternate host .110 each report ONE logical CPU (SYSINFO processors=1), so haloded will share a single core with .123's own fullscreen client, which has never been tried. The recipe's '.110 (P4 2.8 HT)' is also wrong for the same reason. Added to mp_summary and risks, with a fallback: WM_CLOSE .123's client to leave a pure server.

The recipe leaves out .123's recorded instability. docs/lan-multiplayer-status.md: '.123 went off the LAN twice mid-session - treat it as fragile' (2026-09-01, with no command sent). As host it is a single point of failure for every player. It did survive the 09-29 Halo game and the 10-13 party. Added as a risk, with a written fallback to host on .110 (firewall off, EnableFirewall=0 read 2026-11-11).

screenshot_notes forbids plain 'vcrctl fbshot' on .124 while Halo holds D3D exclusive mode. But lanparty.py shot_box runs exactly that for VCR_BOXES={124} (EXECW 30 C:\vcr\vcrctl.exe fbshot). The v56k plan, item 4, says the stuck win32k thread keeps the process alive and the agent EXEC waits on it. The recipe must say not to use lanparty check's frame path for .124. GDI SCREENSHOT captured Halo's menu at 1280x960 there on 11-08.

in_game_proof puts the HUD in the wrong place. In the 09-29 frames the shield bar and health segments, with the player icon, are top-RIGHT. Top-left is the weapon's ammo/battery counter ('098' plus a bar). Corrected.

The query claim rested on the wrong evidence, but the conclusion holds. The '\status\' string in haloded belongs to the client-side query SENDER: 0x5a28a4 builds '\status\' or '\basic\\info\' and sendto()s it. It is not a server handler. The server does answer, by another path: the game-socket classifier (0x45b15e) hands datagrams starting '\', ';' or FE FD to the qr2 parser 0x5982a0. Its legacy branch (0x59830e -> 0x598160) replies with every server, player and team key ('%s%d' gives player_0 ...), ending '\final\\queryid\1.1'. qr2 is initialised at 0x58d79a with the public flag as a parameter, so sv_public 0 should still answer. Also, the worktree's modified lanparty.py roster() already queries host_ip_of(t) for a title with a host box. 'It sends only to 192.168.1.132' is true only of the committed HEAD version. Still never run live.

The -novideo rationale is inaccurate. halo.exe sets the intro-skip flag [0x7196e8] for -novideo OR -connect (0x541418-0x541440), and 0x4c773d skips bungie/gearbox/mgs.bik when it is set. So every -connect launch already skipped the intros, the 09-29 joins included; the 13-minute .124 intros came from a plain menu launch. -novideo is kept because it does no harm.

Hardware changed since the proven game, and the recipe does not flag it. .240 is now a Radeon X1950 Pro (1002:7280); on 09-29/10-03 it was an X1600 (1002:71C0), and neither is listed in the staged config.txt. .123 now drives a CRT with no EDID, so its -vidmode becomes 1280,960,100 (GAMERES 2026-11-11). Halo has not been seen on either setup. Added as risks.

Staging gaps. haloded also refuses to start without the tree's strings.dll ('Invalid / missing strings.dll'), not only MAPS. haloded has no -cport switch, so it binds 2302 and the default 2303; that is the real reason the host client moves to 2304/2305. The host batch now checks haloded.exe's exact size (2342912), Strings.dll and MAPS\bloodgulch.map before it starts.

The procedure does not match lanparty.py. lanparty.py writes the host launcher as C:\fleetmp\<key>-host.bat, not HaloHost.bat, and it launches every client at once after host.wait. So '.124 last' needs a second run: 'run Halo --boxes 124 --no-host'.

It becomes eligible once an NVIDIA Windows 7 driver is installed, which is a driver-audit item this round does not change.

launchers.notes:
AXIS group: 'team r' = TEAM_RED = Axis, t\1 in server.log. The text is unchanged and was checked line by line:
- Every path exists in the library and on all 8 boxes: FLEETRES.BAT 4917 B, FLEETRES.EXE 33280 B, WolfMP.exe 1077310 B, and Main\autoexec.cfg 1423 B, which ends 'exec fleetres.cfg'.
- FLEETRES.BAT has no setlocal, so FR_W, FR_H and FR_HZ survive the call.
- The redirections are the same form the staged launchers use.
- lanparty.render_bat turns {name} and {host} into Fleet<octet> and 192.168.1.132 and the line ends into CRLF (rendered and checked).

The staged Join bat is not called because it cannot set a name and it ends in 'exit', which would end this script too.

Why the extra lines:
- At init, RTCW applies the configs (wolfconfig_mp.cfg, then autoexec.cfg, which execs fleetres.cfg) over command-line +set for latched renderer cvars. .124's rtcwconsole.log of 2026-10-03 loaded system32 opengl32 despite '+set r_glDriver retrogl', then printed 'r_glDriver will be changed upon restarting'. So the resolution and r_glDriver must sit in fleetres.cfg.
- name, com_maxfps, connect and exec run from the command buffer in command-line order at the first frame, so the connect carries the name. .124's wolfconfig_mp.cfg still says WolfPlayer.
- fleetmp.cfg runs after the connect. 'wait' counts only frames not spent loading. 'team' fires about 17 s after ClientBegin on a box holding 85 fps, and 30-60 s on .133 or .184; the say follows 300 frames later. lan_check.py's RTCW soak proved that exec'd waits survive the connect and map load on this client.

Tribes2.mp_summary:
The host has a server for this title: tribes2-server, a docker container (not a systemd unit) on 192.168.1.132, UDP 28000. gameservers.py lists it with probe t2, port/join 28000, manager docker. It runs Classic CTF on Katabatic with 32 slots and 3 fixed bots, launched as `wine Tribes2.exe -dedicated -online -mod Classic -mission Katabatic CTF`.

Because there is no -nologin, console_start.cs sets $PlayingOnline=1, and t2csri/serverSide.cs then turns on the TribesNext auth package. Every non-local client must return a tribesnext.com-signed certificate within 15 s, or the server drops it with "This is a TribesNext server. You must install the TribesNext client to play." No box has an account: there is no *.store file in GameData on any of the 9 boxes (DIRLIST, 2026-11-11). Making an account is a manual in-game step (mouse entropy, then tribesnext.com). AS CONFIGURED NOW NO BOX CAN JOIN, and a round can only show that drop.

Once the server runs -nologin, the join needs no one at the keyboard. server.changes_needed gives three ways: an in-container edit plus docker restart, a rebuild, or a second instance on 28001. The launcher runs `Tribes2.exe -nologin -connect IP:{host}:28000 -mod Classic`. console_start.cs turns -nologin followed by -connect into LaunchMode Connect, and console_end.cs DispatchLaunchMode then runs OnlineLogIn(); setNetPort(0); JoinGame(address). The server's and the staged client's Tribes2.exe, base\*.vl2 and Classic\scripts\*.cs are md5-identical (52 files), so there is no version or CRC mismatch.

The round has to handle three things:
1. The first-run EULA. No box has $pref::AcceptedEULA, .124 included.
2. The player name. No box has a warrior, so the name would be '' and the server would call the box 'Poser'.
3. Observer mode. A client that has joined stays an observer on team 'Unassigned' until it presses FIRE (mouse button 0 only). Each box needs one left click after loading before the roster shows it on Storm or Inferno.

For 1 and 2, the launcher appends lines to Classic\prefs\ClientPrefs.cs: EULA accepted, intro skipped, Voodoo warning seen, and a Fleet<octet> warrior. console_start.cs execs that file (as $clientprefs) before the intro and the EULA check. .124's 2026-10-02 tune shows the engine reads that file under -mod Classic.

CORRECTIVE FINDING, verified live 2026-11-11 ~18:55Z: the server's Torque info reply is NOT encrypted. Asked with flag 0x02 it comes back as plain text, with every name tagged bot or human, plus a players byte and a bots byte: 3/32, bots=3 (Nova-9, Akhiles, Hotspur). gameservers.py probe_t2, scripts/game-servers/README.md, the CLAUDE.md bot paragraph and the lanparty.py docstring all say otherwise.

Tribes 2 has never loaded a mission on any fleet box. There is no lighting cache in base\lighting or Classic\lighting anywhere, and the compat DB has the title untested everywhere. .124 has only run the shell: in the 2026-09-28/29 sweeps the process was alive and the frames were unreadable.

The 8 XP boxes apply. .186 (no usable GPU driver on 32-bit Win7) and .243 (165 MHz, gated, not deployed) do not. No binary that runs contains SSE or CMOV, so the boxes without SSE2 are fine.

Fallback, only if no server change is allowed: .123 runs a -nologin dedicated server and all 8 boxes join it (see host_box).

Its NVIDIA GTX 1650 (PCI 10DE:1F82) runs on Microsoft's 'Standard VGA Graphics Adapter' (vga service; VIDEODIAG and HWPROFILE, 2026-11-11). NVIDIA's 32-bit Windows drivers ended with the R390 branch, before Turing, so this card cannot get a vendor driver here. launchers.bat:
@echo off
rem Tribes 2 fleet round: join the server by IP with no menus.
rem console_start.cs: -nologin then -connect gives LaunchMode Connect; console_end.cs DispatchLaunchMode then runs JoinGame.
rem Tribes2 ships NO FLEETRES.BAT by design - see the title's notes.txt; the engine enumerates the driver's modes.
rem Keep -mod Classic LAST: console_start.cs skips the argument after -mod X.
setlocal enableextensions
if not exist "C:\Games\Tribes2\GameData\Tribes2.exe" goto missing
cd /d "C:\Games\Tribes2\GameData"
del .\base\scripts\*.dso 1> nul 2>&1
del .\base\scripts\autoexec\*.dso 1> nul 2>&1
del .\base\scripts\packs\*.dso 1> nul 2>&1
del .\base\scripts\turrets\*.dso 1> nul 2>&1
del .\base\scripts\vehicles\*.dso 1> nul 2>&1
del .\base\scripts\weapons\*.dso 1> nul 2>&1
del .\Classic\scripts\*.dso 1> nul 2>&1
del .\Classic\scripts\autoexec\*.dso 1> nul 2>&1
del .\Classic\scripts\packs\*.dso 1> nul 2>&1
del .\Classic\scripts\turrets\*.dso 1> nul 2>&1
del .\Classic\scripts\vehicles\*.dso 1> nul 2>&1
del .\Classic\scripts\weapons\*.dso 1> nul 2>&1
rem Per-box warrior, EULA accepted, intro and Voodoo warning skipped, in the prefs file the engine execs before its EULA check.
md "C:\Games\Tribes2\GameData\Classic\prefs" 1> nul 2>&1
set T2P=C:\Games\Tribes2\GameData\Classic\prefs\ClientPrefs.cs
>> "%T2P%" echo.
>> "%T2P%" echo $pref::AcceptedEULA = 1;
>> "%T2P%" echo $pref::SkipIntro = 1;
>> "%T2P%" echo $pref::SawVoodooWarning = 1;
>> "%T2P%" echo $pref::Video::fullScreen = 1;
>> "%T2P%" echo $pref::Player::Count = 1;
>> "%T2P%" echo $pref::Player::Current = 0;
>> "%T2P%" echo $pref::Player[0] = "{name}\tHuman Male\tbeagle\tMale1";
start "" /D "C:\Games\Tribes2\GameData" "C:\Games\Tribes2\GameData\Tribes2.exe" -nologin -connect IP:{host}:28000 -mod Classic
exit
:missing
echo Tribes 2 is not installed here - GAMESYNC the Tribes2 title.
ping -n 11 127.0.0.1 > nul
exit

{host} is 192.168.1.132 (tribes2-server, once it runs -nologin), or 192.168.1.123 for the fallback. Under Option B, change 28000 to 28001 here AND in the roster query AND in the sniff.

server.unit: tribes2-server: a docker container (image nsc-tribes2-tribesnext:latest, built 2026-08-24; manager docker, not systemd), built from retro-agent-private/scripts/game-servers/tribes2-docker. server.query_kind:
Torque binary over UDP 28000. It is not GameSpy, and a \status\ probe never gets an answer.
- Liveness: send 0x0E; the server answers 0x10 and echoes the 4 key bytes (gameservers.py probe_t2).
- Roster: send GameInfoRequest 0x12 with flags 0x02; the server answers with a plaintext 0x14.

lanparty.py roster() has no Torque branch. An unknown query kind falls through to the GameSpy probe, so the round needs its own parser; the format is in roster_how.
server.roster_how:
Send UDP to the server port: bytes 12 02 followed by 4 random key bytes. The reply starts with 0x14, then the flags byte, then bytes 2-5 echo the key.

Reply layout after the key:
- Three u8-length strings: mod ('Classic'), game type ('Capture the Flag'), map ('Katabatic').
- u8 status (bit 0 = dedicated), u8 players (bots included), u8 max (32), u8 bots, u16le cpu.
- A u8-length info string.
- A u16le content length, then the content, split on newlines (DefaultGame::getServerStatusString):
  - line 0 is the team count N;
  - then N lines of 'team TAB score';
  - then the client count;
  - then one 'name TAB team TAB score' line per client.

Each name carries TorqueScript colour bytes that say what it is:
- 10 0E (\cp\c9): bot.
- 10 0C (\cp\c8): unauthenticated human ('smurf'). Every -nologin box shows up this way.
- 10 07 or 10 0B: TribesNext-authenticated.
Strip bytes 01-07, 0B, 0C and 0E-11 to get the plain name.

Humans = players byte minus bots byte. A client that has just joined is on team 'Unassigned' until it presses FIRE in the mission, then Storm or Inferno.

With flags 0x00, only the three header strings are Huffman-compressed; the content block is still plain. That is what was mistaken for encryption.

Verified live 2026-11-11: 3/32, bots=3, Nova-9 (Storm), Akhiles (Inferno), Hotspur (Storm).
server.log_how:
Nothing per-client can be read on the host today. `docker logs tribes2-server` is 459 lines of Wine noise ('Application tried to create a window, but no driver could be loaded.', 'Error opening terminal: unknown.') and contains no CADD or CDROP lines.

The game console does print 'CADD: <clientId> IP:192.168.1.x:port' on every connect and 'CDROP: ...' on every drop (Classic/scripts/server.cs lines 676 and 787). But that output goes to wineconsole inside the container. No console.log is written, and Classic telnet is off ($Host::ClassicTelnet = 0).

- For names, use the info-reply roster.
- For IPs, count packets per source IP to the server port with `scripts/fleet/lanparty.py sniff`. It uses tcpdump on enp129s0 via ~/.fleet-sudo, and both are present.

While the server runs -online, a -nologin box appears in the roster with an EMPTY name for up to 15 s (its pre-authentication GameConnection) and is then dropped.
server.bots_note:
3 Classic AI bots at difficulty 0.75 (the fleet's 'Hard'). The count is FIXED ($Host::BotCount 3), not a backfill: humans join beside the bots, and Classic caps bots at MaxPlayers-1. 8 boxes plus 3 bots is 11 of 32 slots. Bots carry the 10 0E tag and can never be mistaken for a box.

The bots were added by an in-container edit on 2026-10-01 (ServerPrefs.cs.pre-bots is in the container). The 2026-08-24 image predates that edit, so an Option B instance has no bots. The _custom ServerPrefs.cs (commit 7ad4c5e) does include them, so an Option A rebuild keeps them.
server.changes_needed:
REQUIRED before any box can join unattended. NOT done: this run is read-only, and the choice belongs to the operator. The server has to come off TribesNext authentication; nothing on the client side can get past the current -online server.

Option A' (no rebuild, reversible): edit the running container the same way the 2026-10-01 bot change was made, then restart it.
1. `docker exec tribes2-server sed -i '/^exec wine/s/ -online / -nologin /' start-server`
2. `docker restart tribes2-server`
3. Check `docker exec tribes2-server ps auxww` shows -nologin, and that the 0x12 query answers.
The change survives docker restart and host reboots (same container, restart: unless-stopped). It is lost only if the container is recreated. To revert, run the same sed with the two words swapped, then restart. If the server stays mute for 3 watchdog passes (60 s) while booting, the watchdog may restart it again.

Option A (persistent, the route notes.txt proposes):
1. Change -online to -nologin on the exec line of retro-agent-private/scripts/game-servers/tribes2-docker/_scripts/start-server.
2. In that directory run `docker build --network=host -t nsc-tribes2-tribesnext:latest .` (the legacy builder; buildkit hangs at apt).
3. Run `docker compose up -d --no-build`.
CAUTION: files/ holds only README.md, so the build re-downloads tribes2gsi.exe (~539 MB) from depot.tribes2.net, plus TribesNext_rc2a.exe and the Linux overlay from tribesnext.com and lutris.net. To build offline, first copy the share's Files/Games/Windows XP/Tribes2_gsi.exe (564,721,416 B) to files/tribes2gsi.exe; check its md5 first.

Option B (main server untouched): start a temporary second instance on 28001:
`docker run -d --rm --name tribes2-lan -p 28001:28001/udp nsc-tribes2-tribesnext:latest bash -c 'sed -i "s/^\$Host::Port *= *28000;/\$Host::Port = 28001;/" GameData/Classic/prefs/ServerPrefs.cs && sed "s/ -online / -nologin /" start-server > /tmp/ss && exec bash /tmp/ss'`
The image's ServerPrefs.cs (commit 566cd52) has `$Host::Port          = 28000;`, which this sed matches. Move the launcher, the roster query and the sniff to 28001. This instance has no bots. Stop it with `docker stop tribes2-lan`; --rm then deletes it.

Do NOT stop tribes2-server to free port 28000. The watchdog restarts an exited container on its next 20 s pass, and a running-but-mute one after 3 passes.

OPTIONAL, for server-side IP evidence: set $Host::ClassicTelnet = 1 with real passwords and restart. Container port 666/tcp is already published as host 27999, so `telnet 127.0.0.1 27999` would then show the CADD lines.

Side finding: start-server's '-mission "$MAP" "$GAMETYPE"' is never parsed. console_start.cs advances by 3 arguments for '-mod X', which skips -mission. As a result, T2_MAP and T2_GAMETYPE do nothing: console_end.cs CreateServer($Host::Map, $Host::MissionType) takes the map from ServerPrefs.cs. The comment in start-server claiming 'ServerPrefs alone never starts a mission' is also wrong.

Tribes2.in_game_proof:
The strongest proof, per box, is the server's own info reply. Send 0x12/0x02 to 192.168.1.132:28000 (192.168.1.132:28001 under Option B, or 192.168.1.123:28000 in the fallback); the format is in server.roster_how.

1. CONNECTED: 'Fleet<octet>' appears with the unauthenticated-human tag (bytes 10 0C ... 11). Humans = players byte minus bots byte. The 3 bots are tagged 10 0E and never count. An entry with an EMPTY name that vanishes after about 15 s means the server is still -online.

2. IN THE MISSION: a client that has joined stays an observer on team 'Unassigned' until it fires. server.cs serverSetClientTeamState sets camera mode justJoined, and camera.cs assigns a team only on trigger 0. After the load wait:
   a. Dismiss any modal box with UIKEY RETURN.
   b. UICLICK the screen centre with the left button (FIRE, its only default binding).
   c. Within a few seconds the roster should show the box on Storm or Inferno.
That team change proves the box loaded the mission and spawned. A box still 'Unassigned' after the click is still loading or lighting, or has a dialog up: screenshot it.

To corroborate:
- tcpdump packet counts per source IP to the server port (lanparty.py sniff, about 8 s). This is the only host-side evidence that carries the IP.
- An in-game frame after UIKEY F2 (toggleScoreScreen, bound in moveMap, which stays active in observer mode) showing every Fleet name. Press F2 again to close it.

A running Tribes2.exe proves nothing, and no server log line exists without the optional telnet change.
Tribes2.screenshot_notes:
On the 7 NVIDIA and ATI XP boxes, XP GDI `SCREENSHOT 0` should photograph Tribes 2's fullscreen OpenGL. It has never been tried, because the title has never gone past the shell on any box. On first run expect 800x600 at 16 or 32 bpp (see the launcher notes).

.124 (vcr-kmd): run `EXECW 30 C:\vcr\vcrctl.exe fbshot C:\fleetmp\fb.bmp`, then DOWNLOAD the file; lanparty.py VCR_BOXES already does this. The 2026-09-28/29 sweep frames at 800x600x16 were horizontal noise (Tribes_2_Solo_and_LAN_60s.png), so a noisy frame on .124 is a capture fault, not a verdict on rendering. The box now runs at 1280x960x32.

If GDI returns a black or stale frame on another box, ALT+ENTER (GlobalActionMap 'alt enter' -> toggleFullScreen() in console_end.cs) gives a window that can be captured. Switch back with ALT+ENTER and record the fullscreen result. Do not do this on .124.

Before taking the frame, in order:
1. Dismiss any WARNING with RETURN.
2. Click once to spawn (FIRE).
3. UIKEY F2 for the score screen with every player's name.
The engine only enumerates 16- and 32-bit modes, so there is no 8-bit palette problem.
