review_issues: MATERIAL - in_game_proof cannot pass as written. Classic server.cs serverSetClientTeamState puts every newly connected client in camera mode 'justJoined' (the live server has $Host::TournamentMode 0). The client then sits as an observer on team 0, 'Unassigned', until it presses FIRE: camera.cs Observer::onTrigger calls Game.assignClientTeam only on trigger 0. By default FIRE is bound only to mouse button0 (controlDefaults.cs, in moveMap and observerMap). The recipe never sends that click, so no box would ever reach Storm or Inferno. Fix: after the load wait, clear any modal box with UIKEY RETURN, then UICLICK the left button at the screen centre. Until then, 'Unassigned' with tag 10 0C means connected but not yet spawned.

MATERIAL - first_run is missing the NEW WARRIOR dialog. In Connect mode, OpenLaunchTabs opens GameGui on its default WARRIOR SETUP pane. Classic GM_WarriorPane::onActivate calls createNewAlias() when $pref::Player::Count == 0, which pushes NewWarriorDlg with DONE disabled and CANCEL hidden. This happens whenever the pre-seed is not read. first_run also has the order wrong: the GG splash and T2IntroC15.avi play BEFORE the EULA, because StartLoginProcess only runs from checkGGIntroDone/checkIntroDone.

Option A's rebuild needs the network. tribes2-docker/files/ now holds only README.md, so the installer step would re-download tribes2gsi.exe (~539 MB, depot.tribes2.net), TribesNext_rc2a.exe (tribesnext.com) and the Linux overlay (lutris.net). Added two alternatives: a reversible in-container edit plus docker restart (the way the 2026-10-01 bot change was made), and pre-seeding the build from the share's Tribes2_gsi.exe.

.243 exclusion reason is partly wrong. Tribes2.exe does have a Voodoo 2 renderer: strings Voodoo2Device, 3dfxvgl, glide2x/glide3x, and 'Sorry, the Voodoo 2 display device only supports full-screen!'. The exclusion still stands on the CPU (165 MHz against the 500 MHz floor) and the operator override; the card is not the reason.

.186 exclusion reason overstates the case and misses the root cause. Windows 7 always ships Microsoft's GDI Generic OpenGL 1.1 software renderer, so 'nothing can render it' is not literally true. It would be an unplayable software path, and Win7 GDI captures fullscreen as black. The root cause: the box runs 32-bit Windows 7 RTM (exec_os OSArchitecture=32-bit) with a GTX 1650 (10DE:1F82). NVIDIA's 32-bit drivers ended with R390, before Turing, so no vendor driver can be installed on this OS. That belongs in the driver audit.

Watchdog detail is wrong. gameservers_watch.py restarts an exited (failed/inactive) container on its next 20 s pass. The 3 x 20 s rule applies only to a running-but-mute server. The advice (do not stop tribes2-server) still stands.

The launcher notes say it deletes .dso files 'the same way the staged launchers do', but it omits the six base\scripts\*.dso deletions that both staged launchers and Classic_LAN.bat run. Low impact: with -mod Classic, compiled base scripts land in Classic\scripts, as the server container shows. Restored anyway. Also added $pref::SawVoodooWarning = 1, so .124's possible Voodoo warning cannot sit modal over the FIRE click.

The claim 'no prefs = 800x600x16' holds only for .124: vendor 'Brian Paul' matches no card profile, and its .pretune export reads 800 600 16. The NVIDIA boxes match the GeForce profile and the Radeon boxes match Radeon, and GeForce.cs and Radeon.cs both set '800 600 32'. Expect 800x600 at 16 or 32 bpp.
load_wait_sec 180 contradicts the recipe's own first_run advice to poll up to ~300 s for first-time lighting on .133, .184 and .143. Raised to 300.

Tooling gap not stated: lanparty.py roster() has no Torque branch. An unknown query kind falls through to a GameSpy \status\ probe, which Tribes 2 never answers, so the round needs its own 0x12/0x02 parser (format verified below). Under Option B, the roster query and the packet sniff must also move to 28001, not just the launcher.

Minor: ACCEPT is not provably keyboard-unreachable. ShellButtonProfile has tab=true and canKeyFocus=true, so TAB focus may reach it (unproven). The pre-seed's 'untested' risk can also be narrowed: the 2026-10-02 v56k_tune of .124 wrote 1280 960 32 into Classic\prefs\ClientPrefs.cs and the engine then used 1280x960, so that file is the one read under -mod Classic. Quake2Complete.mp_summary:
host_server: the dev host's quake2-server (Yamagi 8.60 + patched 3zb2, 3 fixed Hard bots) serves baseq2 deathmatch, rotation q2dm1-q2dm8 from 3zb2/3ZBMAPS.LST [q2dmx], on 192.168.1.132:27910 (status reply re-read 2026-11-11: q2dm1, maxclients 12, protocol 34, 0 humans). Nine boxes apply: the eight XP boxes with a 3D card (.110 .123 .124 .133 .143 .171 .184 .240) plus the Win98 Voodoo 2 box .243. .186 (Win7 32-bit on Standard VGA) is excluded; .145/.197 are off. Every id Tech 2 client takes +set name and +connect on the command line, so no box needs menu work to join.

XP launcher = lanparty.py's built-in q2 launcher (joined 10 of 10 on 2026-10-13) plus three things: the staged Quake II.bat's baseq2\fleetres.cfg write, +set logfile 2 (a per-box console witness) and +set vid_ref gl (an early command, so boxes with no config.cfg - .110 .133 .184 .240 - or with vid_ref soft saved - .143 - skip the throwaway fullscreen ref_soft mode set before GL). The 2026-09-01 six-box Q2 game is NOT a run of this launcher - lanparty.py dates from the 10-13 party; 09-01 used per-box baseq2\lan.cfg (set name, F5/F6/F11 binds) with the same +connect mechanism. .243 gets a COMMAND.COM launcher built from the generated Voodoo launcher body - baseq2 instead of xatrix, no pause, lines under 127 chars - started the way the 2026-10-03 metal pass started this same tree: LAUNCH C:\WINDOWS\COMMAND\START.EXE <8.3 .BAT>. lanparty.py's launch_bat cannot do that as written and must special-case .243 (see the .243 launcher notes).

Two server facts shape the round:
1. The server is parked in intermission: today's level started after the 10:57:14 restart (server.log 41305) and ended 'Timelimit hit.' at 41372 (~11:12) with nothing but rcon since. 3zb2's ClientBeginDeathmatch never calls MoveClientToIntermission, so a joining client spawns FROZEN (PM_FREEZE) at a spawn point, and only a usercmd carrying BUTTON_ANY (a key HELD across a client frame) ends it; UIKEY/UICLICK are instant taps. The 2026-10-13 '10 of 10' was measured frozen exactly like this (31790 'Timelimit hit.', joins at 32373-32395, no map load between). So send rcon 'gamemap q2dm1' just before launching.
2. maxclients 12 minus the 3 fixed bots = exactly 9 human slots = this round. A 10th human collides with a bot's slot (see bots_note).

Order of the round: (1) rcon gamemap q2dm1; (2) launch all 9 at once; (3) wait ~90 s (.243 may need ~120 s); (4) roster + rcon status + server.log joins + sniff; (5) frames - UIKEY R scoreboard then SCREENSHOT 1 on the GDI-capturable XP boxes, vcrctl fbshot or F11 on .124, F11 TGA on .243; (6) DOWNLOAD every baseq2\qconsole.log; (7) end: console quit on .243 and .124, PROCKILL elsewhere. Do steps 4-6 within ~10 minutes of the gamemap: fraglimit 25 can end the level before timelimit 15 (today's bot-only level: Evil Zeep 22 kills in 15 min, and idle humans are free frags).

Confidence: high for the 8 XP boxes, medium for .243 (first scripted MULTIPLAYER join there; its renderer path and this exact tree's launch method are proven). The host has no mission-pack or CTF server, so The Reckoning, Ground Zero and ThreeWave CTF multiplayer are not covered by this round.

excluded_boxes.reason: No display driver: Windows 7 Professional 32-bit RTM (6.1.7600), GeForce GTX 1650 (10DE:1F82, Turing) on Microsoft's Standard VGA driver (service vga, 16 MB, no OpenGL ICD); NVIDIA never shipped a 32-bit Windows driver for Turing (32-bit ended at 391.35). The gate still gives it all 4 shortcuts because Quake II has a software renderer, and the tree is complete there (quake2.exe 362,496 B; fleetres.cfg gl_mode 9). Excluded because: (a) a ref_soft or Microsoft software-GL fullscreen start on vga.sys is unproven and may fall back to a window; (b) Win7 GDI captures fullscreen black; (c) it would be the 10th human beside 3 fixed bots on a 12-slot server. If the operator wants it anyway: raise maxclients first (server.changes_needed), and put the renderer in baseq2\fleetres.cfg, NOT on the command line - the staged autoexec.cfg sets vid_ref "gl" and Quake II 3.20 execs it AFTER VID_Init and after the +set early commands, so a command-line +set vid_ref soft loses. I.e. have its launcher write set vid_ref "soft" / set sw_mode "3" / set vid_fullscreen "1" into baseq2\fleetres.cfg, and prove it only through the roster, rcon status and qconsole.log.

@echo off
rem Fleet MP round - Quake II from the Quake2Complete tree, baseq2 deathmatch on the host Yamagi server.
rem The staged Quake II.bat - FLEETRES picks this box's gl_mode - plus vid_ref gl, a name, a console log and +connect.
cd /d "C:\Games\Quake2Complete"
call FLEETRES.BAT
cd /d "C:\Games\Quake2Complete"
> baseq2\fleetres.cfg echo // written by the launcher at every start - do not edit

launchers.notes:
lanparty.py's built-in q2 launcher (10 of 10 on 2026-10-13) plus: (a) the staged Quake II.bat's baseq2\fleetres.cfg write - baseq2\autoexec.cfg sets gl_mode "6" and execs fleetres.cfg after it (read today on all 8 boxes; only the favourites adr0..8 block follows), so the file decides the final gl_mode and must match the command line; it carries exactly the GAMERES idtech2 body, so no writer fight; (b) +set logfile 2 -> baseq2\qconsole.log, truncated each start (the mechanism is proven: .124 and .143 already hold baseq2\qconsole.log files from earlier +set logfile 2 runs); (c) +set vid_ref gl, which only moves autoexec's own vid_ref earlier: .110 .133 .184 .240 have no baseq2\config.cfg (a PROCKILLed game saves none, and 10-13 ended that way) and .143's says vid_ref "soft", so without it those five first start ref_soft fullscreen 320x240x8 and switch to GL a frame later. If GL failed the engine still falls back to soft on its own.
Files present on every box (DIRLIST 2026-11-11): quake2.exe 362,496 B (the patched exe - its table entry 9 is 1920x1080, checked in the library binary), FLEETRES.BAT 4,917, FLEETRES.EXE 33,280, ref_gl.dll 234,496, baseq2 paks + gamex86.dll 397,824, FLEETKEY.CFG 720.
FR_Q2WIDE = GAMERES target.q2wide, re-read 2026-11-11: 8 (1280x960) on .110 .123 .124 .133 .143 .171; 6 (1024x768) on .184; 9 (1920x1080) on .240. No ResCapW/H on any box (.171's old Voodoo-era 800x600 cap is gone). Each box's baseq2\fleetres.cfg already holds that value.
.124: renderer is the system ICD (OpenGLDrivers\3dfx DLL = retroicd.dll, our MesaFX over Glide on vcr-kmd); no game-local opengl32/glide DLL - retrogl.dll.0176, retrogl_0178.bak, glide3x_38a891e8.bak are renamed aside; 1280x960 F11 TGAs from 2026-09-28 prove gl_mode 8 there.
Note: autoexec's gl_mode "6" followed by fleetres' value marks gl_mode modified, so every launch does one same-mode renderer restart - benign, it happened on 10-13 too.

Quake2Win9x is the Win98 lane of Quake II. requires.json max_os win9x keeps it on .243 only, and every NT box joins through Quake2Complete, whose 'Quake II.bat' uses the same display name 'Quake II'. That is why plan_args lists a 'Quake II' shortcut under this title on the NT boxes. .243 ALSO has Quake2Complete (E:\GAMES\Quake2Complete, with mission-pack Voodoo shortcuts only; its base Quake II.bat is min_os win2k). So the Quake2Complete round must NOT launch on .243. .243 joins that same round through this recipe's bat, launched FIRST because it loads slowest. This is not a standalone round. .243 runs the stock 3.20 quake2.exe (md5 57dd2cf4ba176f3e6ae72fccc94c38b4). Quake2Complete's exe differs from it in exactly 11 bytes, the mode-9 table entry and its label (provisioning/patches/idtech2). That exe put 10 of 10 boxes on this server on 2026-10-13, so protocol compatibility is established. The join is command line only: +set name Fleet243 is an early command, and +connect is a late command, so the attract demo never plays. No server.log line is attributable to .243. Its Voodoo 2 render (F11 TGA of base1 on 2026-09-25; 24.9 fps timedemo) is proven, and so is the 2026-10-03 metal pass (both Quake II shortcuts, no dialog, console quit). The network join is not proven. .145 and .197 are switched off. Start the round with rcon retroadmin gamemap q2dm1 BEFORE launching any box, because no agent keystroke can end the current intermission.

launchers.bat:
@echo off
rem Quake2Win9x fleet LAN round on .243 - Voodoo 2 MiniGL, joins the fleet Quake II server.
rem COMMAND.COM dialect - the mechanism of Play Quake II - Voodoo.bat, plus name and connect.
rem Upload as C:\FLEETMP\Q2W9X.BAT - an 8.3 name - with CRLF line ends.
if not exist E:\GAMES\Quake2Win9x\quake2.exe goto notree
E:
cd \GAMES\Quake2Win9x
if not exist quake2.exe goto notree
if exist %windir%\SYSTEM32\GLIDE2X.DLL goto glide
if exist %windir%\SYSTEM\GLIDE2X.DLL goto glide
echo.
echo  No 3dfx Glide driver is installed - this round needs the Voodoo 2.
echo.
pause
goto end
:glide
echo // written by C:\FLEETMP\Q2W9X.BAT for a fleet LAN round > baseq2\fleetres.cfg
echo set vid_ref "gl" >> baseq2\fleetres.cfg
echo set gl_driver "3dfxgl" >> baseq2\fleetres.cfg
echo set gl_mode "3" >> baseq2\fleetres.cfg
echo set vid_fullscreen "1" >> baseq2\fleetres.cfg
start /w quake2.exe +set name {name} +connect {host}:27910
if exist DESKFIX9.EXE DESKFIX9.EXE
goto end
:notree
echo E:\GAMES\Quake2Win9x\quake2.exe is missing - the managed Quake II tree is not there.
pause
:end
cls
launchers.notes: One box only: .243 (Win98 SE, P166 + Voodoo 2, agent 1.98.0, GamesDir E:\GAMES). ROUTE - the one metal243.py proved on .243 on 2026-10-03 (LAUNCH C:\WINDOWS\COMMAND\START.EXE C:\RETRO_AGENT\RUNT.BAT, an 8.3 path): (1) MKDIR C:\FLEETMP - it does not exist yet (DIRLIST C:\FLEETMP* is empty today); (2) UPLOAD the rendered text as C:\FLEETMP\Q2W9X.BAT with CRLF line ends ({name} -> Fleet243, {host} -> 192.168.1.132; lanparty.render_bat does both and the CRLF); (3) LAUNCH C:\WINDOWS\COMMAND\START.EXE C:\FLEETMP\Q2W9X.BAT. START.EXE is present (28,672 bytes, 1999-04-24); its first token is an existing .exe, so agent 1.90.1+ CreateProcesses it directly in its own console (agent/shared/launchline.h, agent/src/exec.c handle_launch) and ShellExecute runs the batch in its own DOS box. Do NOT use lanparty.launch_bat for .243: it LAUNCHes "C:\fleetmp\<key>.bat", which becomes command.com /c with a quoted long filename in a new console - never exercised on .243 - and its kill_games/shot_box compare whole PROCLIST names, which on Win98 are full paths. (trial.py, cited before as proof of this route on .243, drives the 86Box VM at 127.0.0.1:19930, not .243.) PATHS: the bat uses E:\GAMES\Quake2Win9x, never C:\Games. .243 still carries an unmanaged pre-GamesDir copy at C:\Games\Quake2Win9x (directory 2026-09-25; its own config.cfg, bench.cfg, qconsole.log, scrnshot); the first line refuses instead of falling back to it, which also covers a missing E:. The earlier 'cd \GAMES\QUAKE2~1' fallback was dead code - the first line already refuses whenever the long path is missing - and is dropped. Every file the bat touches was checked live: E:\GAMES\Quake2Win9x holds quake2.exe (362,496), 3dfxgl.dll (142,848), DESKFIX9.EXE, baseq2\autoexec.cfg / FLEETKEY.CFG / config.cfg; GLIDE2X.DLL is in C:\WINDOWS\SYSTEM (226,304), none in SYSTEM32. NO FLEETRES CALL, deliberately: the tree has no FLEETRES.BAT/.EXE (find -iname '*fleetres*' on the library tree is empty; stage-fleetres.py marks Quake2Win9x payload False), the staged Voodoo launcher has none either, and a Voodoo 2 scans out its own 640x480x16. The bat writes baseq2\fleetres.cfg exactly as Play Quake II - Voodoo.bat does (vid_ref gl, gl_driver 3dfxgl = the MiniGL beside quake2.exe, gl_mode 3, vid_fullscreen 1); autoexec.cfg execs fleetkey.cfg then fleetres.cfg, and on .243 only retro-gameindex's adr0-adr8 favourites block follows it - harmless. ARGUMENTS: +set name is an EARLY command in 3.20 (Cbuf_AddEarlyCommands runs again after config.cfg), so Fleet243 beats config.cfg's saved name Player; +connect is a LATE command, so the d1 attract demo never runs. START /w forwards the arguments by Win98 START's documented syntax (START [options] program [arg...]); the staged Quake2Complete Win9x launchers on this box rely on the same thing (start /w quake2.exe +set game xatrix). The 44.6 fps 800x600 figure quoted earlier as proof came from glquake_win9x_bench.py LAUNCHing GLQUAKE.EXE directly with -width (line 94), not from Q1V800.BAT's start /w, so it proves nothing about START; Fleet243 appearing on the server is the proof. The START tail is 61 characters, under COMMAND.COM's 127. When quake2 exits the bat runs DESKFIX9 and ends with cls so Win98 closes the DOS box. No parentheses, no NT syntax, no < > | in any rem line. Software fallback only if Glide fails: replace the three gl lines with echo set vid_ref "soft" >> baseq2\fleetres.cfg and echo set sw_mode "0" >> baseq2\fleetres.cfg (320x240, 16.1 fps measured on .243; sw_mode 3 = 640x480 is 8.4 fps).

Quake2Win9x.in_game_proof: Strongest first. Before launching, record wc -l of /home/voidsstr/q2-server/server.log. 1) The new server.log lines (tail -n +<N+1> | grep -v heartbeat) contain 'Fleet243 connected' AND 'Fleet243 entered the game' (printed by ClientBegin once the map is loaded - also during intermission), with no later 'Fleet243 timed out' or 'Fleet243 disconnected'. 2) rcon retroadmin status (UDP to :27910, format verified live): the Fleet243 row's address column reads 192.168.1.243:<port> and its ping column is a NUMBER - CNCT there means the client is still loading (the string is in the server binary). 3) The status roster (\xff\xff\xff\xffstatus\n, or python3 scripts/fleet/lanparty.py roster q2) lists Fleet243 beside the other Fleet<octet> names. Necessary but NOT sufficient: the server lists a client from cs_connected on, i.e. before its map has loaded. 3zb2 bots are game entities and never appear, so every listed name is a human. 4) A frame from the Voodoo framebuffer: confirm WINLIST foreground 'Quake 2' (keys go to the focused window); UIKEY F11 ('screenshot', bound in autoexec.cfg and config.cfg); wait 3-5 s; DIRLIST E:\GAMES\Quake2Win9x\baseq2\scrnshot (absent today, so the first file is quake00.tga) and DOWNLOAD the newest quakeNN.tga; convert with Pillow. If that frame shows no scoreboard, UIKEY F1 ('cmd help' = the scoreboard in deathmatch) or UIKEY X ('score', bound in .243's config.cfg), then F11 again. Do NOT press F1 first: both keys TOGGLE the scoreboard (3zb2 Cmd_Score_f), and a player killed by a bot already has it up (player_die calls Cmd_Help_f; dmflags 272 has no force-respawn, so an idle dead player stays on it). During intermission it is always shown. It lists up to 12 entries - every Fleet name plus the three bots. 5) Optional: lanparty sniff counts packets from 192.168.1.243 to :27910 (needs ~/.fleet-sudo). A running quake2.exe alone is not proof.
Quake2Win9x.screenshot_notes: On .243, SCREENSHOT/SCREENDIFF (GDI) photographs only the Cirrus 2D desktop: the Voodoo 2 drives the monitor through its analog pass-through, so the game is invisible to GDI and a GDI frame proves nothing about it. vcrctl fbshot is .124 only. Use the engine: F11 (and F12) = 'screenshot' writes E:\GAMES\Quake2Win9x\baseq2\scrnshot\quakeNN.tga (first free NN; the directory does not exist yet on E:), a 640x480 24-bit TGA of 921,618 bytes read from the Voodoo framebuffer through the MiniGL. Fetch it with DOWNLOAD (never EXEC/type on Win98) and convert with Pillow. The path is proven: docs/evidence/voodoo2-243/quake2win9x_243_voodoo2_base1_640x480.png (2026-09-25, taken from the old C:\Games copy). Do not read C:\Games\Quake2Win9x\baseq2\scrnshot - it holds that old copy's shots. Confirm WINLIST foreground 'Quake 2' before any UIKEY. A GDI SCREENSHOT 0 on .243 is useful only when the join failed: the DOS box text or a Quake 2 error dialog is then on the 2D card.

server.unit: quake2-server
server.query_kind: q2: UDP \xff\xff\xff\xffstatus\n to the game port. NOT getstatus. gameservers.py probe 'q2' (SERVERS row: unit quake2-server, port 27910, join 27910 - matches).
server.roster_how: The status reply is \xff\xff\xff\xffprint, then the infostring line (\maxclients\12\mapname\q2dm1\protocol\34\version\8.60 ...; verified live 2026-11-11), then one '<score> <ping> "<name>"' line per HUMAN. A client is listed from cs_connected on, so a box that is still loading is already on it. 3zb2 bots are not network clients and never appear. python3 scripts/fleet/lanparty.py roster q2 reads exactly this. Name to IP and loaded-or-not: rcon retroadmin status returns the columns num score ping name lastmsg address qport (verified live, 0 rows); ping reads CNCT while the client is still loading.
server.log_how: The unit appends stdout to /home/voidsstr/q2-server/server.log (StandardOutput=append, stdbuf -oL), so journalctl --user -u quake2-server shows only start and stop. Join lines: 'Fleet243 connected' (ClientConnect), then 'Fleet243 entered the game' (ClientBegin, after the map load); later 'Fleet243 timed out' or 'Fleet243 disconnected'. They carry NO IP and NO timestamp (2026-10-13 lines 32373-32395 show the format). Record wc -l before the round, then read the new lines: tail -n +<N+1> /home/voidsstr/q2-server/server.log | grep -v heartbeat. For the IP: python3 -c "import socket;s=socket.socket(socket.AF_INET,socket.SOCK_DGRAM);s.settimeout(3);s.sendto(b'\xff\xff\xff\xffrcon retroadmin status\n',('192.168.1.132',27910));print(s.recv(65535)[4:].decode('latin1'))" and look for the Fleet243 row: address 192.168.1.243:<port>, numeric ping. Each rcon adds a harmless 'Rcon from [192.168.1.132]' line to the log.
server.bots_note: 3zb2 (Yamagi port with the fleet patch), botlist 'fleet' (zb_path 3zb2, autospawn 1). It has 3 FIXED Hard bots, Evil Zeep (cyborg/ps9000), Claw Finger (male/psycho) and Korn (female/cobalt). All three skins are in the client's baseq2\players, so no download is needed. The bots autospawn at every map start (the first 10 s after the load, then one a second), with no backfill and no yielding to humans. Get_NewClient gives them the TOP client edicts (12, 11, 10). They are invisible to status and rcon status, so only server.log names them. At a timelimit or fraglimit the bots disconnect, and the server idles in intermission until some client sends BUTTON_ANY, which an agent UIKEY tap does not produce (first_run). The server is in that state now.
server.changes_needed: No config change for the expected round: the 8 XP Quake2Complete boxes plus .243 make 9 humans, and 9 + 3 bots = 12 = maxclients (bots on edicts 12, 11 and 10, humans on 1 to 9). The round only needs rcon retroadmin gamemap q2dm1 before any box launches (first_run). With 10 or more humans (.186 through Quake2Complete's software renderer, or .145/.197 if powered on), two things break. (a) A human who connects while all three bots are in is given the free server slot 9, which is a bot's edict 10. 3zb2's ClientConnect then takes the occupied body ('a loadgame body'). (b) Worse, after a map change SpawnBot's guard counts only edicts in use, and a human who is still loading is not in use but is still pers.connected. With a slow loader present, the third bot's Get_NewClient finds no edict and calls gi.error('ED_Alloc: no free edicts shit'). That is ERR_DROP: the server drops its map until the watchdog restarts it (src/bot/func.c:254-273, 563-578). If 10 or more humans will play, choose one before the round. Option 1: raise set maxclients 12 to 16 in scripts/game-servers/quake2/server.cfg, re-run install-3zb2.sh (it writes ~/.yq2/baseq2/server.cfg, the copy Yamagi reads, plus ~/q2-server/baseq2/server.cfg), then systemctl --user restart quake2-server. Option 2, for this map only: rcon retroadmin sv rmb 3 once the bots are in, and change no map after that. NOT made.

risks: First multiplayer join for .243 and for Quake2Win9x. The render (2026-09-25) and the launch plus console quit (2026-10-03) are proven on the metal; the server join is not. server.log cannot settle 'never joined' either way. No line is attributable to .243, but there are unattributed 'Player connected' lines (18621, 18622, 18797) from between the 09-01 and 10-01 sessions, and Player is the name .243's config.cfg still holds. There is no evidence of a join.

Quake2Complete is ALSO installed on .243 (E:\GAMES\Quake2Complete, inv.json; plan_args lists .243 installed with three shortcuts). Its base launcher is cmd.exe dialect (min_os win2k), and lanparty's built-in q2 bat does cd /d C:\Games\Quake2Complete, a folder that does not exist there. So the Quake2Complete round must NOT launch on .243. .243's only launcher is this recipe's bat, started in that same round. This recipe is not a standalone round.
Use E:\GAMES, never C:\Games. C:\Games\Quake2Win9x on .243 is a stale, unmanaged pre-GamesDir copy, so a generic C:\Games\<title> launcher would silently run it.

On Win98, PROCLIST returns full paths (mostly upper-case, but not all: C:\WINDOWS\SYSTEM\mmtask.tsk) and unsigned 32-bit pids. lanparty.py's kill_games and shot_box compare whole names, so they never see quake2.exe on .243. Compare the basename case-insensitively, as metal243.py does.

Never kill WINOA386.MOD, COMMAND.COM or START.EXE by name on .243. The agent's own console and retro_chat's console are WINOA386.MOD DOS VMs (PROCLIST today). Kill only quake2.exe, preferably by console quit.
Do not use UIKEY to leave intermission. A tap never carries BUTTON_ANY (first_run). Start the round with rcon gamemap, and never change the map once .243 is loading.
The scoreboard keys toggle. F1 or X can HIDE a scoreboard that a death already put up, so take the F11 frame first (in_game_proof 4).
Slot math with 3zb2 bots: 10 or more humans can either take over a bot's edict or, at a map change, crash the map through gi.error (server.changes_needed).

Match window: the timelimit is 15 min and the fraglimit 25. Three Hard bots against idle humans can end the match within minutes. After that everyone sits on the intermission scoreboard, which is still one game for the proof.

P166 performance: the SP timedemo is 24.9-27.0 fps, so a 12-player match will be slower. The MP load time on .243 has never been measured; the earlier '60-120 s' was an estimate. Poll for 'Fleet243 entered the game' rather than trusting a fixed wait. The server drops a client that is silent for its timeout (Yamagi default 125 s; '%s timed out'), so an extreme load stall shows up in server.log.
retro_chat.exe is running on .243 (PROCLIST). Its pollers cost the P166 about 8% (docs/voodoo2-243-benchmarks.md). Leave it alone; do not kill it by name.
The Win98 agent is single-threaded. Never use EXEC on .243 (read files with DOWNLOAD), and close every connection gracefully, because an RST can crash Win98 Winsock.

After any cold boot, read PciRescueBoot (REGREAD HKLM Software\RetroAgent) before a Glide launch. A Voodoo 2 left at BAR0 0 makes Glide map it over RAM and kill the box. Today it reads 'agent 1.98.0, uptime 45s: all 6 installed PCI device(s) present - nothing to do'.
A clean console quit saves the name Fleet243 into baseq2\config.cfg (CVAR_ARCHIVE), so later desktop play shows Fleet243 instead of Player. This is cosmetic.

GamesDir E: is on the 80 GB secondary-IDE disk that a power loss used to hide (cmosmbr now repairs that below the OS). If E: is missing, the bat stops and shows the failure instead of running the stale C: copy.

Quake1.in_game_proof:
Use server-side evidence for each box, from strongest to weakest:

1. **Server roster by name.** Send DarkPlaces getstatus to 192.168.1.132:26000. Each human comes back as a line `<frags> <ping> "Fleet<octet>"`. FrikBot bots are never listed, because they are not network clients (getstatus shows clients 0 while bot_count is 3), so every name listed is a box. In lanparty_titles.json set query ["q3", 26000], matching server.query_kind. roster()'s q3 branch parses the reply; run live today it returned [] with 0 humans. The nq branch returns only [('__info__', players, max)], which would mark every box named_on_server=False.
2. **Name tied to IP.** Send `\xff\xff\xff\xffrcon retroadmin status` to 26000 and strip the 5-byte '\xff\xff\xff\xffn' prefix. Each player comes back as `#<n> Fleet<octet>  <frags>  h:mm:ss` (ProQuake layout; format string confirmed in the binary), with `   192.168.1.<octet>:<port>` on the next line. This is the only place the server ties a name to an IP.
3. **Server log.** /home/voidsstr/quake1-server/server.log gets the line 'Fleet<octet> entered the game'. It has no IP and no timestamp, so compare against what was there before the round.
4. **Packets.** Run lanparty sniff on port 26000. DarkPlaces keeps every client on its one socket (CCREP_ACCEPT returns port 26000), so each box's packets are visible.

On the box side, the WINLIST foreground title should be 'GLQuake' ('WinQuake' on .186). Also take a frame of the map with the status bar or the deathmatch frag overlay, using an F11 engine screenshot where GDI cannot see the game. A running GLQUAKE.EXE is not proof, and on .243 lanparty's 'running' flag reads False even when GLQuake runs, because that agent's PROCLIST reports full paths.

server.roster_how:
For names, use lanparty query ['q3', 26000], i.e. DarkPlaces getstatus on the game port. Measured today: the server answers it, although scripts/game-servers/README.md (line 108), the game-servers skill (line 317) and docs/lan-multiplayer-status.md (line 287) say NetQuake does not. Request `\xff\xff\xff\xffgetstatus` and you get `statusResponse\n\<infostring>\n`, then one line per human, `<frags> <ping> "<name>"` (format string '%d %d%s "%s"' in the binary). DarkPlaces bounds a network client's ping to at least 1, so there is no ping-0 ambiguity, and FrikBot bots never appear.

The 'nq' probe (gameservers.probe_nq, CCREQ_SERVER_INFO) is health only. It returns the human count and max (0/16 today), and lanparty's nq roster branch yields no names.

Watch the flood limit: a second getstatus or getinfo from the same source IP within about 1-2 s gets NO reply (measured again today: a repeat after 0.5 s went unanswered; getinfo after 3.5 s answered). Every host tool shares 192.168.1.132, so space queries at least 2 s apart and retry once before calling the server down. lanparty.roster() sends only one.

For name plus IP, send `\xff\xff\xff\xffrcon retroadmin status` to 26000 and strip the first 5 bytes. You get the ProQuake layout: '#<n> <name>  <frags>  h:mm:ss', then '   <ip>:<port>' on the next line. This one-liner works (run today):
python3 -c "import socket;s=socket.socket(2,2);s.settimeout(3);s.sendto(b'\xff\xff\xff\xffrcon retroadmin status',('192.168.1.132',26000));print(s.recvfrom(65535)[0][5:].decode('latin1'))"

Side finding for the library (does not block this round). WQREADME.TXT lines 47-55 say pmpro16.dll, pmpro32.dll, wdir16.dll, wdir32.dll, wdirnop.com and wdirnop.pif 'must be present', and the staged Quake1 tree has none of them (only .143 carries leftover copies). On failure it calls a helper that shows MessageBoxA(text, 'MGL Fatal Error!') and exits. So .243's documented WinQuake 'MGL Fatal Error!' is almost certainly the missing DLLs, not the Cirrus 5436 that stage-win9x.py and voodoo2-243-benchmarks.md blame. Mode 3 (_vid_default_mode_win) is then the first fullscreen DIB mode. Wording corrected.

server.roster_how: Send UDP to 192.168.1.132:7798 with payload \players\ (or \status\, which appends the same player block whenever NumPlayers > 0; both verified in the 469e IpServer.u source embedded in ~/ut99-server/System/IpServer.u). Each human comes back as \player_N\Fleet<octet>, with frags_N, ping_N, team_N, mesh_N, skin_N, face_N and ngsecret_N (true or false). SendPlayers walks only PlayerPawns that are not Spectators, and UT bots are not PlayerPawns, so every player_N is a box. For counts, send the separate request \game_property\NumPlayers\ (humans) and \game_property\NumBots\ (bots). Each is its own UDP query, answered as \NumPlayers\<n>\queryid\..\final\; neither is a field of the \status\ reply. `python3 scripts/fleet/lanparty.py roster ut99` parses the \status\ reply and returned all ten Fleet names on 10-13. Ignore its bot column on this server: for keys starting 'ut' it marks ping=='0' as a bot, and 469e's ping_N (P.ConsoleCommand("GETPING")) parsed as None for all ten players on 10-13. Go by the names.
server.log_how: The unit appends stdout and stderr to /home/voidsstr/ut99-server/server.log (StandardOutput=append:). `journalctl --user -u ut99-server` therefore shows only start lines; the game-servers skill's '(UT99: journal)' note is stale. Per-box join lines with map changes marked: `grep -a -E '^Open MyLevel .* 192\.168\.1\.[0-9]+:[0-9]+$|HELLO REVISION=0 MINVER=400 VER=436|^Login: Fleet|^Join succeeded: |Connection timed out after|^Close TcpipConnection|^Server switch level: ' ~/ut99-server/server.log | tail -120`. To watch live: `tail -n0 -F ~/ut99-server/server.log | grep -a --line-buffered -E '<same pattern>'`. The client IP is on `Open MyLevel <Day Mon dd hh:mm:ss yyyy> 192.168.1.<octet>:<port>`; every UT map's level object is named MyLevel. The name is on `Login: Fleet<octet>` and `Join succeeded: Fleet<octet>`. Those lines carry no IP and interleave when boxes connect together, so match boxes by the octet in the name. Reading timeouts: `Connection timed out after 15.000000 seconds` means a client that had joined went silent (killed, crashed or dropped); on 10-13 all ten showed it when the round was killed. `after 150.000000 seconds` does NOT by itself mean a failed box. At every map change, each joined client reconnects from a new port, and 1-2 s later a stray packet from its previous port opens a second `Open MyLevel` from the same IP. That connection never handshakes and times out 150 s later. On Oct 15, .124 produced 33 of these across 35 map switches while `Join succeeded` followed every reconnect. A box has failed only if no `Join succeeded: Fleet<octet>` follows the latest `Open MyLevel` from its IP. On a first join, with no earlier connection from that IP, a 150 s timeout with no Join succeeded does mean it never finished loading. Both timeouts count from the last packet the server received on that connection.

@echo off
rem Unreal Tournament retail 436 - join the fleet UT99 server as {name}.
rem Resolution and per-box Glide block copied from the staged Join fleet UT99 server - 436.bat,
rem with the paths spelled out because this file runs from C:\fleetmp. Command form proven 10 of 10 on 2026-10-13.
set UTD=C:\Games\UnrealTournament436
set UTI=C:\Games\UnrealTournament436\System\UnrealTournament.ini
set FRX=C:\Games\UnrealTournament436\FLEETRES.EXE
call "%UTD%\FLEETRES.BAT"
if exist "%FRX%" (
  "%FRX%" -ini "%UTI%" WinDrv.WindowsClient FullscreenViewportX %FR_W%
  "%FRX%" -ini "%UTI%" WinDrv.WindowsClient FullscreenViewportY %FR_H%
  "%FRX%" -ini "%UTI%" WinDrv.WindowsClient StartupFullscreen True
)
if /i "%FR_UE1DEV%"=="GlideDrv.GlideRenderDevice" if exist "%FRX%" "%FRX%" -ini "%UTI%" Engine.Engine GameRenderDevice GlideDrv.GlideRenderDevice
if /i "%FR_UE1DEV%"=="GlideDrv.GlideRenderDevice" if exist "%FRX%" "%FRX%" -ini "%UTI%" Engine.Engine WindowedRenderDevice GlideDrv.GlideRenderDevice

set UE1G2H=480

if %FR_W43% GEQ 800 if %FR_H43% GEQ 600 set UE1G2H=600
if %FR_W43% GEQ 1024 if %FR_H43% GEQ 768 set UE1G2W=1024
if %FR_W43% GEQ 1024 if %FR_H43% GEQ 768 set UE1G2H=768
if %FR_W43% GEQ 1600 if %FR_H43% GEQ 1200 set UE1G2W=1600
if %FR_W43% GEQ 1600 if %FR_H43% GEQ 1200 set UE1G2H=1200
if /i "%FR_UE1DEV%"=="GlideDrv.GlideRenderDevice" if exist "%FRX%" "%FRX%" -ini "%UTI%" WinDrv.WindowsClient FullscreenViewportX %UE1G2W%
if /i "%FR_UE1DEV%"=="GlideDrv.GlideRenderDevice" if exist "%FRX%" "%FRX%" -ini "%UTI%" WinDrv.WindowsClient FullscreenViewportY %UE1G2H%
set UE1HZ=
set UE1HZN=0
set /a UE1HZN=FR_HZ+0 >nul 2>nul
if %UE1HZN% GEQ 60 set UE1HZ=60
if %UE1HZN% GEQ 70 set UE1HZ=70
if %UE1HZN% GEQ 72 set UE1HZ=72
if %UE1HZN% GEQ 75 set UE1HZ=75
if %UE1HZN% GEQ 80 set UE1HZ=80
if %UE1HZN% GEQ 85 set UE1HZ=85
if %UE1HZN% GEQ 90 set UE1HZ=90
if %UE1HZN% GEQ 100 set UE1HZ=100
if %UE1HZN% GEQ 120 set UE1HZ=120
if defined UE1HZ if /i "%FR_UE1DEV%"=="GlideDrv.GlideRenderDevice" if exist "%FRX%" "%FRX%" -ini "%UTI%" GlideDrv.GlideRenderDevice RefreshRate %UE1HZ%Hz

start "" UnrealTournament.exe {host}:7797?Name={name}

launchers.notes: The batch is valid cmd.exe, unchanged from the checked recipe. The staged 'Join fleet UT99 server - 436.bat' cannot be called as-is: it hardcodes unreal://192.168.1.132:7797 and takes no name. So this file copies its FLEETRES and Glide writes with explicit paths and adds ?Name=. %~dp0 would point at C:\fleetmp, but %~dp0 inside the called FLEETRES.BAT is its own folder, and FLEETRES.EXE -cmd reads no files, so the working directory does not matter. FLEETRES.EXE -ini is WritePrivateProfileStringA on an absolute path. The start line is exactly the 2026-10-13 form. The seven 10-13 box logs that survive (.110 .123 .133 .143 .171 .184 .240) show 'Command line:  192.168.1.132:7797?Name=Fleet1xx' and OpenGLDrv. .124's 10-13 log was overwritten on 11-07. The server log has Join succeeded for all ten. Renderers: FLEETRES sets FR_UE1DEV=GlideDrv only where HKLM\Software\RetroAgent\GlideRender=1 and VEN_121A is present (fleetres.c). Only .124 has GlideRender=1. There the block writes GlideDrv at 1024x768 (FR_W43=1280, and Glide 2 has no 1280x960) at the persisted refresh (85 Hz; RefreshRate=85Hz is already in its ini). .124 last ran Glide 2.70 at grSstOpen 1024x768 Ref=7 (85 Hz) and exited cleanly on 2026-11-07, so its new D3D HAL is never touched. Every other box keeps the staged OpenGLDrv. Resolutions from GameResBoot today, which match the box inis: .110 1600x1200, .123/.124/.133/.143/.171 1280x960, .184 1024x768, .240 1920x1080, all FullscreenColorBits=16. The Running.ini delete is required: a 0-byte System\Running.ini dated 2026-10-13 is on .110 .123 .133 .143 .171 .184 .240, but not on .124, .186 or .243. Referenced files are present in the library: FLEETRES.BAT, FLEETRES.EXE (md5 926d37e0...), System\UnrealTournament.exe, System\UnrealTournament.ini. Fallback if a box shows no process and no server line: replace the URL with unreal://{host}:7797?Name={name}, the form the staged Join launcher proved on .143 on 2026-08-29.

@echo off
rem Unreal Tournament retail 436 on the Win98 Pentium 166 - joins the fleet UT99 server as {name}
rem through Glide on the Voodoo 2. Voodoo.ini is GlideDrv 640x480x16 with lighter detail.
rem COMMAND.COM dialect - no cd /d, no start with a title, no if-blocks.
E:
cd \GAMES\UnrealTournament436\System
if not exist UnrealTournament.exe goto end
if exist %windir%\SYSTEM32\GLIDE2X.DLL goto glide
if exist %windir%\SYSTEM\GLIDE2X.DLL goto glide
goto end
:glide
if exist Running.ini del Running.ini
start /w UnrealTournament.exe {host}:7797?Name={name} -INI=Voodoo.ini
if exist C:\RETRO_AGENT\GLRESET9.EXE start /w C:\RETRO_AGENT\GLRESET9.EXE
cd ..
if exist DESKFIX9.EXE DESKFIX9.EXE
:end
cls
launchers.notes: EXPERIMENTAL. This is the staged Voodoo launcher with the server URL added as the first word. It uses the staged launcher's own Glide check, SYSTEM32 then SYSTEM, through gotos. The -INI= switch keeps its dash; UE1 takes the first bare word as the URL. The start line is 78 characters with Fleet243, under COMMAND.COM's 127 limit. No rem line contains < > or |. FLEETRES is not called: FLEETRES.BAT is cmd.exe-only (%~dp0). Voodoo.ini's 640x480x16 is the per-box mode for a single Voodoo 2 on a P166. GameResBoot's 800x600 target is the desktop, not Glide. Measured on .243 on 2026-10-02: Glide 2.56.00.0459 on the V2, grSstOpen Res=7 640x480, startup 41.6 s, about 10.5 h of the CityIntro loop, then a clean exit. It has never joined a server. LAUNCH route: the runner's default 'LAUNCH "C:\fleetmp\UnrealTournament436.bat"' goes through 'command.com /c' (agent/shared/launchline.h: only an .exe first token skips the shell), with a long filename, which is untested on this box. The route proven on .243 (metal pass, 2026-10-03, metal243.py) is an 8.3 batch started by START.EXE. Do: MKDIR C:\FLEETMP, UPLOAD this text (CRLF) as C:\FLEETMP\UT436.BAT, then LAUNCH C:\WINDOWS\COMMAND\START.EXE C:\FLEETMP\UT436.BAT. End the round with a console quit before any PROCKILL: UIKEY TILDE, UIKEY TEXT:quit, UIKEY RETURN. That sequence closed Unreal Gold (same UE1 console, ConsoleKey=192) on this box in the metal pass. On Win98 a killed DirectSound game holds the SB16 until a restart. After the game exits, the batch runs GLRESET9 (present: C:\RETRO_AGENT\GLRESET9.EXE, 4096 B, 2026-10-03; verdict in C:\RETRO_AGENT\GLRESET.TXT) to give the monitor back to the Cirrus. Then it runs DESKFIX9 (title root) and cls, so the DOS box closes. On this box, read files with DOWNLOAD only, never EXEC. Expect the single-threaded agent to answer slowly while UT pins the P166.

UnrealTournament436.in_game_proof: Server-side, per box, from ~/ut99-server/server.log: 'Open MyLevel <date> 192.168.1.<octet>:<port>', then 'Level server received: HELLO REVISION=0 MINVER=400 VER=436', then 'Login: Fleet<octet>' and 'Join succeeded: Fleet<octet>'. A box counts as in the game when a 'Join succeeded: Fleet<octet>' follows the latest 'Open MyLevel' from its IP. A 'Connection timed out after 150' shortly after a 'Server switch level:' is the stray connection from the box's previous port, not a failure. The GameSpy \players\ reply on 192.168.1.132:7798 must list player_N = Fleet<octet> for each box. It holds humans only: 469e lists only non-spectator PlayerPawns, never bots. The separate request \game_property\NumPlayers\ should equal the number of boxes launched, and \game_property\NumBots\ should be 0 with 3 or more boxes on. A box-side frame: UIKEY F1 (bound to ShowScores), then SCREENSHOT 1, shows the in-game scoreboard with every Fleet name and ping; press UIKEY F1 again to close it. The HUD's 'Rank n/N' also shows the player count (10-13: 'Rank n/10'). A running UnrealTournament.exe is not proof: a failed connect sits at the main menu.
UnrealTournament436.screenshot_notes: XP boxes on OpenGLDrv (.110 .123 .133 .143 .171 .184 .240): GDI SCREENSHOT 1 captures fullscreen UT436. On 2026-10-13 all eight XP boxes other than .124 (those seven plus .145) gave in-game frames in grid_ut99.jpg. .124 renders through Glide on vcr-kmd: GDI shows the old desktop, and its vcrctl fbshot came back garbled on 2026-10-13 (tile 3). Try the engine's own capture: UIKEY F11 (bound to Shot in the staged and box User.ini) writes C:\Games\UnrealTournament436\System\ShotNNNN.bmp. .124 already holds Shot0000-Shot0016, so take the newest from DIRLIST and DOWNLOAD it. F11 is proven only on OpenGLDrv (.143, 1024x768). On GlideDrv it is untested; if no new Shot file appears, let server.log be the witness. .186 (Win7) runs the XDDM Standard VGA driver with no DWM composition, unlike .197, the WDDM box where black Win7 frames were measured. Take SCREENSHOT 1 first; if it is black, try F11 (SoftDrv). On .243 the Voodoo 2 drives the monitor through its pass-through, so GDI only sees the Cirrus desktop. F11 there would write E:\GAMES\UnrealTournament436\System\ShotNNNN.bmp (640x480x24, about 921 KB), but Shot on Glide is untested there too. DOWNLOAD it, never EXEC. Shot files stay in the game tree, so delete them after downloading. Never press F12 (EndFullscreen) while capturing.
known_blockers: None for the eight XP boxes. The same command joined 10 of 10 on this server on 2026-10-13. The only server change since is MaxPlayers 10/12 to 16, and the only box changes are the GPUs on .110 and .240 (see risks).

.186: no 3D driver can be installed. Its GTX 1650 (10DE:1F82) is on 32-bit Windows 7 RTM, and no 32-bit Win7 NVIDIA driver supports Turing. OpenGLDrv and D3DDrv cannot use the Standard VGA adapter, so only SoftDrv can run, and UT436 has never been run on this install (0-byte UNREALTOURNAMENT.log carrying the library timestamp).

.243: P166, below the title's 233 MHz floor; it has the title only through an operator override (scripts/gamegate/overrides.txt; d931bfe6c33fae5e, @follows b9a3b8c66827032c). It rendered UT436 single-player through Glide on 2026-10-02 but has never joined a server. The server drops a not-yet-joined connection after 150 s without a packet from it. So the client's longest silent stretch must fit inside 150 s: engine init after its first HELLO (startup alone is 41.6 s), then the blocking load of the map.
risks: Stale 0-byte System\Running.ini files (from the 10-13 PROCKILLs) are on .110 .123 .133 .143 .171 .184 .240. Any launcher that skips the delete gets the Recovery Mode window. End rounds with a console quit (TILDE, TEXT:quit, RETURN) before falling back to PROCKILL.

The OldUnreal 469e title (Games-Library\UnrealTournament) uses the same image name, UnrealTournament.exe, and the same server. Do not run its round at the same time; killing by image name ends either tree.
469 anti-flood: MaxConnPerIPPerMinute=5. A box relaunched in a quick loop gets refused, so space retries at least 60 s apart.

The map changes at TimeLimit=15 minutes or FragLimit=25, whichever comes first (bChangeLevels). During the server travel the server refuses connections, and a roster read can briefly miss slow boxes (.243, .186), so read it twice. Every map change also leaves one benign 150 s timeout per box in server.log; see log_how.

Two boxes now have different GPUs than when UT436 last ran on them: .110 (Radeon 9500/9700 on 10-13, now GeForce 7800 GS, FW 93.71) and .240 (Radeon X1600 on 10-13, now X1950 Pro). This will be the first OpenGLDrv run on those cards; low risk.

.124 runs our experimental vcr-kmd kernel driver. The launcher keeps it on Glide (proven 2026-11-07), not the new D3D HAL. A wedged .124 needs a person, because its agent watchdog is unreliable. Each launch is one CRT mode switch; keep relaunches at least 5 s apart.

GAMERES's UT436 rule (agent/shared/gameres.h:1012-1014) writes %W%x%H% (1280x960) into .124's ini at every boot, and Glide 2 has no 1280x960 mode. Only the launcher's Glide block corrects it to 1024x768, so any launcher without that block (the 10-13 lanparty one had none) leaves .124's Glide resolution to chance.

.243: a PROCKILLed DirectSound game holds the SB16 until a restart, and a killed Glide game can leave the Voodoo 2 pass-through stuck. Use the console quit plus GLRESET9 (the batch does this). The default LFN launch path through command.com is untested there; use the 8.3 batch with START.EXE, after MKDIR C:\FLEETMP. Never EXEC on .243, and allow long agent timeouts while UT runs.
.186: SoftDrv through DirectDraw on Win7's VGA driver is unproven. It may fall back to a window or fail to start.

No CD key or disc gate: System\UnrealTournament.icd is SafeDisc v1 residue (the exe's entry point is in .text and it imports Window.dll, Core.dll and Engine.dll), and the server does no key check. Ten identical 436 clients joined at once on 2026-10-13.

review_issues: MATERIAL - log_how reads 'Connection timed out after 150.000000 seconds' as 'never finished loading'. On this server that line follows EVERY map change. Each joined client reconnects from a new port, and 1-2 s later a stray packet from its previous port opens a second 'Open MyLevel' from the same IP. That connection never handshakes and times out 150 s later. Measured in ~/ut99-server/server.log for Oct 15: .124 logged 33 of these 150 s timeouts across 35 map switches, and every reconnect was followed by 'Join succeeded: pigga'. With TimeLimit=15, every box will log one per map change, so counting them as failures would fail healthy boxes. Corrected rule: a box failed only if no 'Join succeeded: Fleet<octet>' follows the latest 'Open MyLevel' from its IP. 'Server switch level:' is added to the grep so map changes show. Both timeouts count from the last packet the server received.

roster_how says to use `lanparty.py roster ut99` and also not to apply a ping-0 bot rule. That parser does apply ping=='0' -> bot for any game key starting 'ut' (ut99 matches; the key UnrealTournament436 does not). `\game_property\NumPlayers\` and `\game_property\NumBots\` are separate query requests (query type game_property, value = the property name). The server answers `\NumPlayers\<n>\queryid\..\final\`. server.roster_how: Send UDP '\status\' (it includes the players) or '\players\' to 192.168.1.132:7798. Each HUMAN comes back as player_N\<name>\frags_N\..\ping_N\..\team_N\..\mesh_N\..\skin_N\..\face_N\..\ngsecret_N\true|false. 469e IpServer.u SendPlayers walks the PawnList for PlayerPawn && !Spectator, so bots never appear and numplayers counts humans only. Tool: python3 scripts/fleet/lanparty.py roster <key>. It only queries, and prints [name, ping, bot] plus ['__info__', numplayers, maxplayers]; 'roster ut99' read ['__info__','0','16'] today. Its ping-0 bot heuristic applies only to keys that start with lowercase 'ut'. That is harmless here, because 469e lists no bots. The roster is shared with any concurrent 436 round.
server.log_how: The unit appends stdout and stderr to /home/voidsstr/ut99-server/server.log (StandardOutput=append:). That stream is flushed per line, so it is live. Do NOT use ~/.utpg/System/ucc.log or the ngStats .tmp files in ~/.utpg/Logs: they are block-buffered (exactly 4096 B, cut mid-line). journalctl --user -u ut99-server holds only the 'Started' lines, so the game-servers SKILL's '(UT99: journal)' is wrong. Before launching, record L0=$(wc -l < /home/voidsstr/ut99-server/server.log). After the wait, run four reads. (a) Every box that connected: awk -v L0=$L0 'NR>L0 && /^Open MyLevel/ {split($NF,a,":"); print a[1]}' /home/voidsstr/ut99-server/server.log | sort -u. (b) Client builds seen: awk -v L0=$L0 'NR>L0 && /Level server received: HELLO/ {print ($0 ~ / VER=469/ ? "469e" : "436")}' /home/voidsstr/ut99-server/server.log | sort | uniq -c. Each map change adds one HELLO per client, so read this as >=, not =. (c) Strict IP-to-build map: awk -v L0=$L0 'NR>L0 && /^Open MyLevel/ {ip=$NF; getline; getline; if ($0 ~ /HELLO/) print ip, $0}' /home/voidsstr/ut99-server/server.log, e.g. '192.168.1.110:1155 Level server received: HELLO REV=101 MINVER=432 VER=469'. It never mis-attributes, but it silently DROPS a connection whose Open line is followed by another client's Open (clients connecting in the same server tick). At the 2026-09-29 19:08:42 map change, six reconnects were logged back to back and none printed. Staggered first joins stay contiguous (all ten mapped on 2026-10-13). A box present in (a) but missing from (c) is not a failure: confirm its build from its own client log ('Init: Version: 469'). (d) Names: awk -v L0=$L0 'NR>L0 && /^Join succeeded: /{print $3}' /home/voidsstr/ut99-server/server.log | sort -u, which prints 'Fleet110' and so on. A full first join reads: 'Open MyLevel <date> <ip>:<port>', 'NotifyAcceptingChannel ... Accepted', 'HELLO ...', then (interleaved with other clients) 'LOGIN RESPONSE=... URL=:7797/Index.unr?Name=Fleet110...', 'Login request', 'JOIN', 'Login: Fleet110', 'Join succeeded: Fleet110'. A disconnect logs 'Close TcpipConnectionN <date>' with no IP. server.bots_note: Botpack backfill: MinPlayers=3, skill Adept (\rules\ botskill Adept). DeathMatchPlus.Timer adds bots only after a human has been on for NetWait=10 s, and only up to MinPlayers=3 humans+bots in total (NeedPlayers). This recipe's key is UT2003, so `roster ut2003` fails with 'unknown game' unless the key is stored in lower case.

Or directly: `python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'scripts/game-servers'); import gameservers as g; raw,_=g._ue2_ask(7758,2,2.0,'192.168.1.132'); print([n for d in raw for n in g.parse_ue2_players(d)]); print(g.probe_ut2003(7758, host='192.168.1.132'))"`. This was verified to run.

The parser reads each entry as int32 id, FString name, int32 ping, int32 score and int32 stats id. That layout has not yet been checked against a reply with humans in it. server.log_how:
Run `docker logs --since 20m ut2003srv 2>&1 | grep -a -E 'Open myLevel|Login: |New Player|Close TcpipConnection'`; it was verified working on 2026-11-11. The same stdout is appended to ~/ut2003-server/server.log, so grep -a there for history. journalctl --user -u ut2003-server holds only systemd start/stop lines, and System\server-ucc.log is empty.

Line shapes, from the 10-03 join and a 2026-11-11 probe (container clock is UTC, dates are MM/DD/YY):
- 'Open myLevel 10/03/26 01:26:40 192.168.1.123:3644' is written when the first UDP datagram arrives from a new address. Any datagram does this; it is not a login.
- After the client has loaded the map: 'Client netspeed is 2600', 'Team 0', 'Login: <name>', 'xPlayer got player TcpipConnection', then 'New Player <name> id= <GetPlayerIDHash>'. The hash is the same on every box, because they share one CD key.
- 'START MATCH' after the first human.
- 'Close TcpipConnection 192.168.1.<octet>:<port> <date> <time>' when the client leaves, or 200 s (InitialConnectTimeout) after an Open that never logged in.

A box is in the game only when it has 'Login: Fleet<octet>' and 'New Player Fleet<octet>' and no later Close for its IP. An Open line with no Close only means packets arrived within the last 200 s. When several boxes load at once, the Login names do not sit next to their Open lines.

The pair 'Open myLevel 11/11/26 18:53:35 192.168.1.132:36670' and 'Close ... 18:56:55' is the fact-check's stray \status\ probe, not a client.

Bots never appear in the type-2 list; they are counted in type 0.

On all seven boxes its md5 is 55f1a977, matching the library, FLEETRES.BAT is md5 3bc37ad6 and FLEETRES.EXE is 33,280 B; DefUser.ini is present. The paths are absolute because %~dp0 would be C:\fleetmp\. FLEETRES.BAT is called by full path, so its own %~dp0 still finds FLEETRES.EXE, and it has no setlocal, so FR_W/FR_H reach this bat. GAMERES VERIFY UT2004 reads ok 3 / wrong 0 on all seven, all with StartupFullscreen=True: .110 1600x1200; .123 .124 .143 .171 1280x960; .184 1024x768; .240 1920x1080. The name is set two ways. server.roster_how: Run python3 scripts/fleet/lanparty.py roster ut2004. It sends UDP '\status\' to 192.168.1.132:7787 and returns the '\player_N\<name>' keys plus __info__ numplayers/maxplayers; on 2026-10-13 it listed all ten names. numplayers is padded up to MinPlayers, so an empty server reads 3. For humans versus bots run: python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'scripts/game-servers'); import gameservers; print(gameservers.probe_ut(7787))". Its players field is GameInfo NumPlayers+NumBots and bots is NumBots, read from \game_property\. The UE2 native type-2 query on 7778 (gameservers._ue2_ask + parse_ue2_players) also lists names.

log_how gives the wrong reason for grep -a. It says the file has 'CR-only line ends'. It does not: it has 9,718 LF line ends and only 11 stray CRs, from the 'Exporting...' progress lines, so wc -l and tail -n work. grep needs -a because line 2279 holds a run of 114 NUL bytes, so a whole-file grep without -a sees a binary file and prints nothing; a tail slice past that line greps fine without it. Also, tail -n +$N re-reads one line that was already there before the launch; use tail -n +$((N+1)).

The .124 screenshot advice is hazardous. The recipe prefers 'EXECW 30 C:\vcr\vcrctl.exe fbshot ...'. vcrctl.c's own usage text and the vcr-kmd README warn against this: the default fbshot runs its escapes under win32k's display lock, a Direct3D game holds that lock, and the default path then 'parks fbshot in the kernel for good'. With Max Payne it printed nothing in 25 s, and Max Payne later froze (cause not established). UT2004 is a D3D8 title on that HAL. lanparty.py check does exactly this on .124 (VCR_BOXES={124}). If fbshot never writes, lanparty then DOWNLOADs whatever C:\fleetmp\fb.bmp an earlier round left and files it as this round's frame. On this HAL GDI SCREENSHOT did capture Max Payne's D3D frame (docs/v56k-benchmark-plan.md, 09-29 sweep).

It reads the cursor with GetCursorPos + ScreenToClient and latches the button through window messages (SetCapture/ReleaseCapture). host.py drives the same front end on every start with an absolute xdotool move and a 300 ms held click. The agent's UIDRAG x y x y holds the left button about 85 ms at an absolute point, so the join must be TRIED: one pilot box first, then every XP box in one burst (first_run JOIN steps). server.unit: carmageddon2-server
server.query_kind: carma2
server.roster_how: No query reply carries names or a count. gameservers.py probe_carma2 is LOCAL-ONLY. It broadcasts the game's CAR2MSG1 to 192.168.1.255:54792 out of enp129s0 and accepts CAR2MSG2 only from 192.168.1.132; live at 2026-11-11 19:13 UTC it was answered from 192.168.1.132:48703, map=lobby, players=0. Its count comes from ~/carmageddon2-server/_run/state.json, which host.py rewrites every ~3 s from the frame. players = green name rows including the host's FLEET HOST row, so remote = players-1, and only while state=='lobby' (0 while racing). That row counter has never seen a second row. Names come only from a lobby frame: decode `docker exec c2srv xwd -root -silent`, or _run/race-start.xwd (written the instant START is clicked), with host.py's Frame class and read the rows. Expect 'FLEET HOST (HOST)' plus each joiner's OPTIONS.TXT PlayerName: FLEET<octet> after these launchers, MAX on every box today.
server.log_how: tail -f ~/carmageddon2-server/server.log. It is the unit's StandardOutput/StandardError (append) and the container clock is UTC; journalctl --user -u carmageddon2-server shows only start/stop. host.py logs '[hh:mm:ss] [host] lobby: N player(s) (was M)' and 'starting the race: N player(s), no change for 45s'. These are counts from the frame, never an IP, and never yet above 1 (11 HOSTING sessions, checked today). At IPXWrapper's default level no host log names a client IP (received packets are logged only at LOG_DEBUG). Per-box IP proof is a capture on the host's PRIVATE IPXWrapper port, NOT 54792. First read the port: PRIV=$(ss -uaneH | grep "docker-$(docker inspect -f '{{.Id}}' c2srv)" | awk '$4 ~ /^0\.0\.0\.0:/ {sub(/.*:/,"",$4); print $4}'). It was 48703 today; re-read it after every container restart. Then run sudo -S -p '' timeout 8 tcpdump -i enp129s0 -n -q -l "udp and dst host 192.168.1.132 and dst port $PRIV and src net 192.168.1.0/24" < ~/.fleet-sudo, which is what lanparty.py sniff(PRIV) runs. A box that is only on the JOIN list shows up instead as udp to 192.168.1.255 port 54792.
server.bots_note: No bots. The host's own car (FLEET HOST, the Carma2_SW.exe software build) always holds slot 1, leaving 11 for joiners. The 12 comes from the wait screen's slot1-slot12 (data/INTRFACE/netsync.txt) and the manual's 'challenge up to 11 of them'. The manual's requirements box says 2-6 players, and no more than the host has ever been seen in this lobby. 8 XP boxes + the host = 9 cars.
server.changes_needed: None is required for a synchronized join. host.py clicks START 45 s after the LAST lobby change (lobby_changed resets on every change in the count, and START needs players >= 2). The hosted game is CLOSED: Driven to Destruction, with 'Open game' 0 under NETSETTINGS 1 in the server copy. Boxes that press JOIN within a few seconds of each other therefore all get in. A box joining more than 45 s after the previous change is locked out until the race ends (C2_RACE_MAX_S 1800) and systemd brings up a fresh lobby (~60-75 s). Only if joins must be spread out (by hand) is a change needed: raise C2_START_AFTER_S and restart the unit. run-carmageddon2-server.sh's docker run does NOT forward that variable, so add -e C2_START_AFTER_S=900 there or change host.py's default. Alternatively set 'Open game' to 1 under NETSETTINGS 1 in the SERVER copy ~/carmageddon2-server/game/data/OPTIONS.TXT (never the library). Watchdog: if the host stops answering CAR2MSG1 once racing (untested), retro-gameservers-watch will restart it after ~60-80 s. For the race window, run the watchdog with restarts off (--no-restart or RETRO_GAMESERVERS_NO_RESTART); that is a decision for the round. Optional IP-stamped host log: add "log_level"=dword:00000002 (LOG_DEBUG) to the HKCU\Software\IPXWrapper block that run-carmageddon2-server.sh generates, then restart the unit. It is very chatty: router.c logs one 'Recieved packet from <ipx> (<ip>)' line per packet. Nothing was changed in this read-only run.

launchers.bat:
@echo off
rem Carmageddon 2 - fleet LAN-readiness round - NT boxes.
rem 1. Driver name: in data\OPTIONS.TXT the line after "PlayerName 0" is the
rem    name the host lobby shows; it and the line after "NetName 0" become
rem    FLEET plus the octet, in capitals like the game font. The file is only
rem    replaced when the rewrite really contains the name.
rem 2. Then the title's own launcher: FLEETRES.BAT, IPXWrapper into place,
rem    nGlide or the real Glide per FR_GLIDE, CARMA2_HW.EXE fullscreen.
setlocal EnableExtensions DisableDelayedExpansion
set "N={name}"
set "N=%N:l=L%"
set "N=%N:e=E%"
set "N=%N:t=T%"
cd /d "C:\Games\Carmageddon2\data"
if not exist OPTIONS.TXT goto play
if exist OPTIONS.NEW del /q OPTIONS.NEW
set "NX="
(
for /f "tokens=1* delims=:" %%A in ('findstr /n "^" OPTIONS.TXT') do (
if defined NX (
echo %N%
set "NX="
) else (
echo(%%B
if "%%B"=="PlayerName 0" set NX=1
if "%%B"=="NetName 0" set NX=1
)
)
) > OPTIONS.NEW
findstr /x /c:"%N%" OPTIONS.NEW >nul && move /y OPTIONS.NEW OPTIONS.TXT >nul
if exist OPTIONS.NEW del /q OPTIONS.NEW
:play
endlocal
call "C:\Games\Carmageddon2\Play Carmageddon 2.bat"
launchers.notes: Read live, read-only, on 2026-11-11 ~19:15 UTC (DIRLIST/DOWNLOAD/REGREAD) on .110 .123 .124 .133 .143 .171 .184 .240. Every box has 'Play Carmageddon 2.bat' at 2,748 B, FLEETRES.BAT at 4,917 B and FLEETRES.EXE at 33,280 B. data\OPTIONS.TXT md5 is 1a61c214..., identical to the library ('PlayerName 0'/'MAX', 'NetName 0'/'MAX'). HKLM\SOFTWARE\SCI\Carmageddon2 has Driver=2 and Password=0 on every box. The game writes OPTIONS.TXT back with PlayerName only (the host copy reads 'FLEET HOST' and has no NetName), so PlayerName is what names a car. lanparty.render_bat makes {name} = Fleet<octet>, and the three substitutions turn it into FLEET<octet>. Check it after launch by DOWNLOAD. If the rewrite fails, the original stays and the box shows as MAX. The staged launcher then copies the .ipxw IPXWrapper stubs into place where they are missing: .123 has none active yet, .124 has the 10-01 copies, and the other five have active 08-27 copies. It then branches on FR_GLIDE. On .124 FR_GLIDE is 1 (V5 6000 present), so nGlide stays aside (none is active there) and the game loads system32 glide2x.dll (94,208 B GlideXP translator) -> glide3x.dll (dated 2026-09-30) -> vcr-kmd. That is the path that passed on 2026-09-28 ('Glide opens on 4 chips'), but with an older glide3x. On the other boxes FR_GLIDE is 0 (no VEN_121A key), so the game uses nGlide 1.02 over D3D9; the game-local glide*.dll have been active since 08-27. The game always runs in the Glide 640x480 mode, and FLEETRES has nothing to set (PER-TITLE-STATUS: incapable). The staged launcher passes no arguments, so -NOCUTSCENES cannot be used. The multiplayer join is the UIDRAG sequence in first_run (JOIN steps); this launcher only starts the game and names the car.

launchers.notes: Why .143 differs. Its Enum\PCI holds VEN_121A&DEV_0009&SUBSYS_0002121A\4&9fd38ef&0&0008 ('AMIGAMERLIN 3.1-R11 For Voodoo 5 5500 AGP') at 'PCI bus 1, device 0, function 0', with no Control subkey. The GeForce 6800 holds the same location and does have Control. Only one card fits that AGP slot, so the V5 key is a ghost. HWPROFILE's present-device check says glide=false. So FR_GLIDE is 1, and the staged launcher would move nGlide aside and hand the game system32 glide2x.dll (258,048 B, 3dfx) with no card behind it. The FR_GLIDE logic dates from commit 3cd52b7 (2026-08-30), which explains the empty 'Error' dialog in the 2026-08-31 matrix frame. The fleet inventory's accelerators[] lists the same ghost. The game folder still has active nGlide (glide*.dll dated 08-27, checked live today), so this variant only copies what is missing. The library/FLEETRES fix is still owed: count only present devices, or delete the ghost key. Naming and joining are as in the NT group.

Carmageddon2.in_game_proof: Render round (unattended, every applicable box): (a) PROCLIST lists CARMA2_HW.EXE. (b) WINLIST foreground title is 'Carmageddon II' and there is no '#32770' dialog. The class should be Carma2MainWndClass, or nGlideWnd if nGlide made its own window; neither has been observed on an nGlide box yet. (c) On the nGlide boxes, DISPLAYCFG get reads 640x480 while the game runs (compat DB, 2026-08-31: 640x480@60 on .123/.133/.240). On .124 judge by vcrctl fbshot instead: its 08-31 row was measured on its old GeForce2, and on vcr-kmd the GDI mode is not the Glide mode. (d) A frame shows the SCi/Stainless logo, the intro FMV, the start screen or the attract demo. A running process alone is not proof. Multiplayer, per box, strongest evidence first: (1) PACKETS TO THE HOST'S PRIVATE IPXWrapper PORT, NOT 54792. IPXWrapper 0.4.0 receives only broadcasts on 54792; it sends everything from, and receives unicast on, a random per-start port (router.c shared/private sockets; addrcache.c caches the peer's real source port). A joined box therefore sends to 192.168.1.132:<private>. Read the port right before capturing, and again after any container restart (each race end, crash or watchdog restart): PRIV=$(ss -uaneH | grep "docker-$(docker inspect -f '{{.Id}}' c2srv)" | awk '$4 ~ /^0\.0\.0\.0:/ {sub(/.*:/,"",$4); print $4}'). It was 48703 at 2026-11-11 19:13 UTC, and the CAR2MSG2 reply came from it. Then capture for ~8 s: sudo -S -p '' timeout 8 tcpdump -i enp129s0 -n -q -l "udp and dst host 192.168.1.132 and dst port $PRIV and src net 192.168.1.0/24" < ~/.fleet-sudo (lanparty.py sniff(PRIV) does the same). Packets from a box's IP mean that box is talking to the host. A box that shows only "udp and dst host 192.168.1.255 and dst port 54792 and src host 192.168.1.<octet>" is still polling the JOIN A GAME list: searching, not joined. (2) The host's lobby rows: decode a live `docker exec c2srv xwd -root -silent`, or ~/carmageddon2-server/_run/race-start.xwd (written the instant host.py clicks START), with host.py's Frame class. Expect 'FLEET HOST (HOST)' plus one FLEET<octet> per joiner. (3) Host counts: _run/state.json players (rows including the host; only while state=lobby) and the server.log lines 'lobby: N player(s) (was M)' / 'starting the race: N player(s)'. These come from a green-row heuristic that has never seen a second row. (4) Box side: C:\Games\Carmageddon2\ipxwrapper.log stops being 0 bytes. Expect IPXWrapper's banner, 'IPX socket created' and 'bind address: 00:00:00:01/<node>/12286', as in the host's own log. This proves the box opened its IPX socket (entered NETWORK GAME), not that it joined. (5) A box frame showing LOADING STATUS with its FLEET<octet> row, or the race. For lanparty.py, do NOT give this title port 54792, because sniff would report 0 for a joined box. Give it NO query either: roster() has no carma2 branch, and its GameSpy fallback would send \status\ into IPXWrapper.

review_issues: MATERIAL: the packet proof watches the wrong port. in_game_proof (1), server.log_how and the lanparty.py note all count packets sent to 192.168.1.132:54792. IPXWrapper 0.4.0 uses 54792 only to RECEIVE BROADCASTS. Every packet leaves from a random per-instance 'private' port, and unicast arrives there too. Sources: the library's ipxwrapper-0.4.0-src.zip (router.c shared/private sockets, winsock.c sends through private_socket) and addrcache.c, which caches the peer's real UDP source port. Measured today: c2srv's private socket is 0.0.0.0:48703 (ss; its inode follows the 54792 socket's), and a CAR2MSG1 probe was answered FROM 192.168.1.132:48703. So a joined box sends to :48703, a port that changes on every container start, and its broadcasts go to 192.168.1.255:54792. The prescribed filter therefore counts nothing from a joined box, and lanparty.py sniff(54792) would report 0 for every box: a false 'not joined'. Fixed: read the port at check time with ss + docker inspect, and keep udp to .255:54792 as the 'still searching' signal.

MATERIAL: mp_mode. 'mp_not_automatable' rests on the doc claim that Carmageddon's menus are relative-mouse (docs/lan-multiplayer-status.md, 'needs a person' table) and on zero-length clicks being ignored. The binary contradicts the first claim. CARMA2_HW.EXE has no DirectInput mouse (its dinput strings name only the keyboard and joysticks). It reads the cursor with GetCursorPos + ScreenToClient, which is absolute, and latches the button through window messages with SetCapture/ReleaseCapture. host.py drives the same front end on every start with an absolute xdotool move and a 300 ms held click. Only zero-length UICLICK/UIKEY were ever tried on a box. UIDRAG x y x y holds the button about 85 ms at an absolute point (agent/src/input.c; dragsteps.h DRAG_STEPS_MIN 5). The join is mouse-only, so it is unproven, not impossible. Changed to host_server with confidence low, an explicit UIDRAG join procedure, and a stop rule that falls back to render-only + needs_human.

Overstated changes_needed: raising C2_START_AFTER_S is not REQUIRED for a whole-fleet round. host.py resets lobby_changed on every change in the count, so START fires 45 s after the LAST join, and only JOIN starts that clock (entering the network menu does not). Stage every box on the network menu first, then send JOIN as one burst, and the default fits. The change is needed only for joins spread out by hand.

HalfLife1.title_display: Half-Life (WON 1.1.0.8) - Deathmatch on a fleet-box listen server
HalfLife1.mp_summary:
This tree cannot use the host's own server. It is WON Half-Life 1.1.0.8, network protocol 45: the engine banner reads 'Half-Life 45/1.1.0.8', and hw.dll's connect packet hard-codes 45. hldm-server on 192.168.1.132 (join :27020 via the a2s proxy, query :27021) answered A2S today with protocol 48, version 1.1.2.2/Stdio. The WON client refused it on 2026-08-31 ('This server is using a newer protocol ( 48 ) than your client ( 45 )'). So one fleet box hosts a WON listen server and the others join it. Box-to-box HLDM is proven two-box (.240 host + .123 on crossfire, 2026-08-30); TFC and DMC are proven two-box on .171 + .133.

HARD CAP: at most 5 clients can share one CD key in a WON LAN game, and that includes the host's own player. Two independent disassemblies agree; it has not been measured.
- SV_FinishCertificateCheck (hw.dll 0x10085680) runs on auth protocol 2. That is local auth, which every listen server here ends up using.
- It counts active, spawned and connected clients whose stored 32-character key hash (client+0x4cb4) matches the joiner's, and refuses at 5 or more with 'CD Key already in use.' (cmp ebp,5 at 0x100857b9).
- It runs before the joiner gets a slot.
- The loopback host stores its hash too (0x100861ce).
- The client's hash is the plain hex MD5 of its Key (0x1000dd10), with no per-machine salt.
- All 10 boxes carry the library's single Key: the hash was identical on every box today.

So the round is TWO matches of host + 4 joiners on one listen server:
- Host: .240, plays as Fleet240, map crossfire.
- Wave A: .123 .171 .133 .110. Prove it, then rcon-kick them (sv_timeout is raised to 180).
- Wave B: .143 .184 .124 .243. Prove it again.
- A 6th client while 5 are in measures the cap.
That covers 9 of the 10 boxes that have the title. .186 cannot render it.

THE HOST IS STARTED BY TYPING AT ITS CONSOLE (UIKEY), not by '+map' on the command line. HOW-TO-RUN.txt records that '+map' did NOT start the map on the host in this build. The typed sequence is the one proven on .240 (2026-08-30) and .171 (2026-08-31). Joiners use command-line '+connect', which HOW-TO-RUN records as working.

The host-server HLDM round for the fleet is a different title: the CounterStrike16 tree's 'Play Half-Life Deathmatch.bat'. Its shortcut 'Half-Life Deathmatch - Fleet Server' is on .110 .123 .124 .133 .143 .171 .184 .186 .240, not .243. It runs protocol 48, joins 192.168.1.132:27020, was proven two-box on .171 + .124, and belongs under CounterStrike16.

excluded_boxes.reason:
No usable display driver, and none can be installed on this OS.
- It runs Windows 7 Professional 32-bit (audit-186/exec_os.txt: OSArchitecture=32-bit) on the Standard VGA driver.
- Its card is a GTX 1650 (10DE:1F82, Turing). NVIDIA's 32-bit Windows drivers stopped at the R390 branch, which predates Turing, so no NVIDIA driver supports this card on this OS. The remedy is 64-bit Windows or an older (Pascal or earlier) card, not a driver install.
- With -gl it would get only Microsoft's GDI software OpenGL.
- HL's own software renderer (-soft, sw.dll) on Standard VGA DirectDraw has never been tried.
- The 5-per-key cap leaves no slot in waves A or B anyway.
An optional one-box wave C (host + .186, the XP joiner launcher with -soft instead of -gl) is possible but likely to fail, and Windows 7 may photograph it black.

host_box.command:
1. Before launching, PROCKILL any *.scr process on .240 (or send UIKEY SHIFT): a screensaver eats the first keystrokes.
2. LAUNCH the host .bat (launchers[0]). It runs:
   hl.exe -nosierra -full -gl -w %FR_W43% -h %FR_H43% -toconsole -condebug -maxplayers 16 +sv_lan 1 +maxplayers 16 +sv_timeout 180 +hostname FleetHL1 +rcon_password retroadmin +name Fleet240 +log on
   It has NO +map.
3. Wait 25 s. The engine is now fullscreen at its console with a ']' prompt. Do NOT press TILDE or ESC; either one leaves the console.
4. WINLIST: the foreground pid must be hl.exe.
5. UICLICK 640 480 (the centre of 1280x960).
6. Type these lines one at a time, each with UIKEY TEXT:<line> followed by UIKEY RETURN:
   sv_lan 1
   maxplayers 16
   sv_timeout 180
   hostname FleetHL1
   rcon_password retroadmin
   name Fleet240
   log on
   map crossfire
7. Gate before starting any joiner: within about 30 s the UDP 'details' query to 192.168.1.240:27015 must return map crossfire with max 16, and 'players' must list Fleet240.
host_box.notes:
Why .240: it already hosted this exact mod and map on 2026-08-30 (crossfire, sv_lan 1, typed console). It is an Athlon 64 3300+ with an X1950 Pro, and FR_W43/FR_H43 give 1280x960 on its 1080p panel.

Ports: a WON listen server is one process. The host's player talks to it over loopback, so there is no port clash. The server listens on UDP 27015 (the 'port' default); each joiner's client uses 27005 on its own box. Firewall is off fleet-wide.

Why sv_lan 1 goes first: it skips the WON-auth attempt. It does NOT keep the host from locking itself out. With sv_lan 0 the challenge path (hw.dll 0x1008643d) calls the WON-auth routine (0x10021500), and when that fails it falls back to the same local auth (protocol 2) that sv_lan 1 uses.

Optional '+map crossfire' shortcut: the sv_lan ordering therefore does not explain why '+map' failed on the host, so appending '+map crossfire' to the command line remains an unproven shortcut. If you try it, gate on the 'details' query within 40 s. If that fails, the console should still be up: type the lines above without relaunching.

sv_timeout 180 is a precaution for .243 (Pentium 166). SV_CheckTimeouts (0x100887c0) drops even clients that are still loading once their last packet is older than sv_timeout, and the default is 60.

Never start this tree's hl.exe without -w %FR_W43% -h %FR_H43%. GAMERES writes the 16:9 mode into the shared GoldSrc registry key, and .240 reads ScreenWidth 1920 / ScreenHeight 1080 today. Given 16:9, the WON engine drops to 400x300.

Kill the host LAST: its exit ends the match for everyone.

server.unit: none - listen server inside hl.exe on 192.168.1.240. hldm-server on .132 is protocol 48 and unreachable from this tree.
server.query_kind:
WON old-style connectionless queries; the dispatcher at hw.dll 0x10088180 handles status/info/details/players/rules/challenge/rcon.
- 'players': send UDP b'\xff\xff\xff\xffplayers' with no challenge. The 'D' reply holds a count byte, then per player an index byte, name\0, int32 frags and float32 time (SVC_PlayerInfo 0x100874e0). It is answered only when maxclients > 1.
- 'details': b'\xff\xff\xff\xffdetails' returns an 'm' reply with hostname, map, gamedir and players/maxplayers.
- There is no 'TSource Engine Query' string in hw.dll and no U-challenge, so lanparty.py's 'a2s' kind cannot read this server; it needs a 'won_players' kind.
server.roster_how:
Send the 'players' query to 192.168.1.240:27015. The 'D' list should show Fleet240 plus the 4 joiners of the current wave. WON HLDM has no bots, so every name is a box.

If +name were ignored, every box would arrive as 'Player' (config.cfg says name "Player" on all 10) and appear as (1)Player, (2)Player and so on. Then identify boxes by the IPs in rcon status. config.cfg runs before valve.rc's stuffcmds, so +name is expected to win.
server.log_how:
There is no journal: the server runs on .240.
(a) rcon from the dev host:
   1. Send b'\xff\xff\xff\xffchallenge rcon\n'.
