review_issues: HOST START PATH CONTRADICTS THE PRIMARY RECORD. The recipe's main host launcher relies on '+map crossfire' on the command line. HalfLife1\HOW-TO-RUN.txt, the tree's own measured record, says: '"+map" and "+connect" on the COMMAND LINE work for the joiner but "+map" did NOT start the map on the host in this build - type it at the console instead.' The recipe says 'single-player +map crossfire and +map c0a0 both ran', but I found no primary source for that. Half-Life.bat mentions '+map c0a0' only as a rejected alternative. The hl.exe code at 0x417dc0 shows only that +map skips the launcher dialog, not that a server starts. The only recorded command-line '+map' listen servers in this tree never loaded a map: .124 on 2026-09-28, lan_check.py WonHLMod '+map dmc_dm2' / '+map 2fort' gave maps_loaded 0. Those runs are confounded by a video-init crash. FIXED: the host .bat no longer carries +map. The proven typed-console sequence (.240 2026-08-30, .171 2026-08-31) is now the primary host path; command-line +map is mentioned only as an optional, gated shortcut.

THE sv_lan RATIONALE IS CONTRADICTED BY THE CODE. The recipe says that with sv_lan 0 the host's own player cannot get in, because WON auth is dead. In hw.dll the challenge path (0x1008643d) does call the WON-auth routine (0x10021500) when sv_lan is 0. When that fails, the routine sets [0x10695ff4]=1, and the path falls back to 'Server requiring authentication', auth protocol 2. That is the same local-auth path sv_lan 1 takes. So sv_lan 0 costs at most the WON-auth attempt and does not lock the host out, and the sv_lan ordering does not explain the measured +map failure. Setting sv_lan 1 first is still correct. FIXED in host_box.notes.

.124 RISK IS MISSTATED AS 'untested'. On 2026-09-28 WON HalfLife1\hl.exe was run on .124's retroicd.dll (our MesaFX system ICD) without MESA_FORCE_SSE, and both runs failed. DMC gave 'FAIL: Dr. Watson entry; never entered the game'; TFC gave 'did not exit; never entered the game; log_bytes 0'. Source: .claude/worktrees/v56k-bench/scripts/benchmarks/results/v56k_lan_192.168.1.124/day/20260928_104632/. C:\retrogl.log (copy at .claude/evidence-refresh/hl1-cs16/live/files/124_C_retrogl.log) shows HalfLife1\hl.exe creating a 1280x960x32 context and the process exiting right after. That matches the GoldSrc/Mesa SSE-probe crash. So MESA_FORCE_SSE=1 is load-bearing, and WON-on-.124 with it is unproven, not merely untested. I re-confirmed today that OpenGLDrivers\3dfx\DLL=retroicd.dll on .124. FIXED in risks.

.186's REMEDY CANNOT BE DONE. The recipe says to re-include .186 'once its NVIDIA driver is installed'. .186 runs Windows 7 Professional 32-bit (audit-186/exec_os.txt: OSArchitecture=32-bit), and its card is a GTX 1650 (10DE:1F82, Turing). NVIDIA's 32-bit Windows drivers ended with the R390 branch, which predates Turing, so no NVIDIA driver supports this card on this OS. The remedy is a 64-bit Windows or an older (Pascal or earlier) card. The exclusion itself is correct. FIXED in excluded_boxes and known_blockers. This also matters for the readiness driver audit.

SLOW-LOADING CLIENTS TIME OUT AT 60 s. SV_CheckTimeouts (hw.dll 0x100887c0) drops any client that is active, spawned or merely connected once its last packet is older than sv_timeout. A client still loading the map counts, and the default sv_timeout is 60. .243 (Pentium 166, a load estimated at ~120 s by the recipe itself) can therefore be dropped mid-load. FIXED: the host sets sv_timeout 180 on the command line and in the typed lines. Wave changes now rely on rcon kick, because a PROCKILLed client would hold its slot and key count for 180 s.
load_wait_sec 60 is too short for wave B, which contains .243; the recipe's own .243 note says to allow about 120 s. FIXED: set to 120 (wave A alone can use 60).

THE SNAPSHOT CLAIM IS OUT OF DATE. The recipe says the F11/snapshot route 'wrote no file'. Two GoldSrc snapshots already exist, both 3,686,454 bytes (1280x960x24): c0a0a0000.bmp on .133 (2026-08-31) and 2fort0000.bmp on .123 (2026-09-02). Both are in the HalfLife1 tree root, i.e. the working directory, not the mod directory, so valve\autoexec.cfg's comment ('lands in this mod directory') is wrong. .240's 'no file' may have been a look in the wrong folder. This gives an optional frame route for .243, whose Voodoo 2 output GDI cannot see: console 'snapshot', then E:\GAMES\HalfLife1\crossfire0000.bmp via DOWNLOAD. It is unproven on the 3dfx MiniGL. FIXED in screenshot_notes and in_game_proof.

LOG FORMAT DETAIL. In the engine log line '"%s<%i><%u><>" connected, address "%s"' (hw.dll), the second field is the USERID, which increments per connection, not the slot. The wonid prints as 4294967295 because the protocol-2 client sends unique=-1 (0x1000de4b). Minor; FIXED in in_game_proof.

lanparty.py PITFALLS NOT COVERED. 'run' PROCKILLs and relaunches the hosting box on every invocation unless --no-host is passed, so running wave B the obvious way would kill the host. lanparty has no host keystroke step, so the typed host start must be done before 'run --no-host'. Its 'a2s' roster cannot read a WON server: there is no TSource string in hw.dll, and the 'U' challenge is ignored. Sniff only runs when the host is .132. FIXED in risks and known_blockers.

MINOR IMPRECISION, not material. SV_CheckKeyInfo (0x100857f0) only extracts the 32-character 'raw' hash; the copy into the per-client field client+0x4cb4 is in SV_ConnectClient (0x100861d3-0x100861e0). Everything else in the cap analysis held up on re-disassembly. The check runs before the joiner gets a slot, so the 6th client in total is refused. The loopback client stores its hash too. The client hash is plain hex MD5 of the Key (0x1000dd10). All 10 boxes carry the identical library Key (same SHA-256 prefix as install.reg).

JediKnightMotS.title_display: Jedi Knight: Mysteries of the Sith
JediKnightMotS.mp_summary:
There is no MotS server on 192.168.1.132, and none can exist. The Sith engine has no dedicated server, no rcon and no connect switch. JKM.EXE's only switches are -path -fail -devMode -dispStats -frameRate -windowGUI -displayConfig -? -debug -verbose -noHUD -record -fixed -coglog (.data 0x57d15c-0x57d28c). In gameservers.py SERVERS the only Jedi title is jka-server; no jk/sith/mots unit or container exists. docs/staged-title-server-matrix.md row 19 says 'peer by design'.

Play is peer-hosted DirectPlay over TCP/IP. It was verified with two boxes on 2026-08-31: .123 hosting, .240 joining (docs/lan-multiplayer-status.md; compat_mp verified_two_box).

PLAYER LIMIT 32, NOT 8. The host screen reads 'Max players (up to 32):' (GUI_MAXPLAYERS), and JKM.EXE clamps the field to 1..32 (0x414131). The manual's 'up to eight players over LANs' is only the level tested to be stable; it adds that 'the game can possibly accommodate more players' (README.TXT 5a agrees). The default is 4 (0x401019), and the host .123 stores no maxPlayers value. Its launcher therefore writes maxPlayers=10 (REG_BINARY 0a000000; read at 0x413b5a and pre-filled into the box at 0x413d5d). That covers the 8 boxes plus 2 spare slots, so a failed join cannot lock the 8th box out.

The launcher cannot connect by itself; every box needs a scripted GUI walk. The walk is automatable:
- The menus are a fixed 640x480 16-bit DirectDraw GUI, and absolute UICLICK already drives it. On .240 (2026-09-29): logo, ESC, Players, main menu, Setup, Display, 3D list (.claude/evidence-1080p/dark-sith-review/240_mots_0*.png). On .124: the 2026-09-28 fbshots.
- RETURN presses OK on the Players, provider, choose-a-game, host and Load Character screens (setters 0x4133a6, 0x415e92, 0x415fc9, 0x413f0c, 0x420212).
- Every rectangle used here comes from JKM.EXE's GUI element tables.

The intro always plays (jmp at 0x401349), but ESC skips it (README 3b; proven on .240). The Players screen then appears on EVERY launch (flag 0x57f634), with no Cancel button.

Host path (.123): ESC on the intro; Players RETURN; Multiplayer (320,280); 'Host Game' (460,100; string id GUI_STARTGAME); the TCP/IP provider row, then RETURN; Host Configuration RETURN (Max players pre-filled 10, name 'Fleet123's Game'); Load Character RETURN; in the level.

Joiner path: ESC on the intro; Players RETURN; Multiplayer (320,280); Join Game (180,100); the TCP/IP row, then RETURN; DirectPlay 'Locate Session' dialog: UIKEY TEXT:192.168.1.123, then RETURN; first session row (330,160), then RETURN; Load Character RETURN; 'Contacting host computer...'; in the level. Joiners commit one at a time (the host also queues joins itself: 'Host is busy - waiting for our turn to join').

Each box joins as its own pilot Fleet<octet>:
- The launcher creates player\Fleet<octet>\Fleet<octet>.plr.
- It copies the MP character as fleet.mpc. That name is its decryption key, so it must not change.
- It sets HKLM playerShortName=Fleet<octet>. The game loads that value at start-up (0x4155e0), and the Players list highlights the matching pilot (0x4132d2).

The names appear in the host's Multiplayer Tally (~), in console 'players' output and in each HUD's '<name> has joined the game'.

There is no network roster. lanparty.py has no query or sniff for this title, and its check photographs only boxes with a joiner launcher, so it skips .123. The proof is therefore: host netstat per joiner IP, each joiner's legible 16-bit 'Players: n of 10' frame, and host tally and console frames taken by hand.

excluded_boxes.reason: No usable display driver, so not attempted this round. Win7 32-bit ADMIN-PC runs its NVIDIA 10DE:1F82 (Turing, GTX 1650-class) on the Standard VGA Graphics Adapter (display.inf 6.1.7600, DRIVERS STATUS 'generic', 1920x1080x32). NVIDIA's 32-bit driver line ended before Turing, so no vendor driver can fix it. MotS would get only unaccelerated DirectDraw, and whether that offers the 640x480x16 menu mode and an 8-bpp software mode is unmeasured. Win7 GDI cannot photograph exclusive fullscreen. Its DirectPlay list has only 3 providers (no IPX; REGREAD 2026-11-11). Its MotS key has no Version value, so the game has never started there. The player limit is NOT the reason; it is 32.

Not installed and no shortcut. compat.db marks it gated by the operator override 'not wanted on .243'. Its P54C at 166 MHz is below the title's 200 MHz floor (requires.json). MotS has no Glide renderer (DirectDraw/D3D/software only), so the Voodoo 2 is no use to it.
Switched off this session. MotS is deployed there (compat.db, gate run). If it comes up it can join: the host's Max players 10 leaves room, and the engine allows 32.
Switched off this session (Win7). MotS is deployed there (probe) but has never been tested there; not part of this round.

host_box.command:
Before launch: WINLIST. Every XP box currently has the ssstars.scr screensaver in the foreground; the launcher taskkills it, and leftover game or dialog windows must be PROCKILLed by PID. Then LAUNCH C:\fleetmp\JediKnightMotS-host.bat (lanparty.py run does this). At about 30-45 s, take SCREENSHOT 0; if the LucasArts logo or the crawl is showing, UIKEY ESCAPE once. Then:
1. Players screen: check that 'Fleet123' is highlighted, then UIKEY RETURN.
2. Main menu: UICLICK 320 280 (Multiplayer).
3. UICLICK 460 100 ('Host Game').
4. Provider screen: SCREENSHOT 0, UICLICK at x 320 on the row reading 'Internet TCP/IP Connection For DirectPlay' (rows near y 190/205/220/235), check the highlight, then UIKEY RETURN.
5. Host Configuration: confirm that Max players at (225,150)-(290,170) reads 10, then UIKEY RETURN.
6. Load Character: UICLICK 440 110 (the 'fleet' row), then UIKEY RETURN.

host_box.notes:
Why .123: it hosted the verified 2026-08-31 two-box game, it is the strongest XP box (Athlon 64 4000+, Radeon HD 3850), and its GDI SCREENSHOT captures the 16-bit menus (perbox 123_JediKnightMotS_JKM.EXE.png). The host also plays: in DirectPlay the hosting JKM.EXE is the session, so there is no separate server process.

Host-ready check before the first joiner commits: EXEC netstat -n -a -p tcp shows TCP 0.0.0.0:47624 LISTENING (DPLAYSVR.EXE appears in PROCLIST), plus JKM.EXE ports around 2300.

The joiners may be LAUNCHed together with the host, because each waits at its own Players screen. Do their final 'choose a game - OK' one box at a time, and wait until each reaches the level.

The host must not shoot: README 1j warns that a player killed mid-join may crash.

lanparty.py check does NOT photograph .123, so take its tally and console frames (SCREENSHOT 0) and its netstat by hand.

lanparty_titles.json entry: host={box:123, bat:<host bat>, wait:45, exe:'JKM.EXE'}, exe:'JKM.EXE', boxes=[110,123,124,133,143,171,184,240]. Box 123 must NOT appear in 'bats'.

server.unit: none - peer-hosted inside JKM.EXE on 192.168.1.123
server.query_kind: none - the Sith engine answers no server query
server.roster_how:
There is no network roster: lanparty.py roster() returns None, and sniff only works when the host is 192.168.1.132. Names are readable only on the HOST's screen, taken by hand, because lanparty.py check skips .123:
(1) In the level on .123, UIKEY TILDE opens the Multiplayer Tally ('Multiplayer Score': name, score, kills; manual p.32). Take SCREENSHOT 0 within about 2 s.
(2) Console: UIKEY T, UIKEY TAB, UIKEY TEXT:players, UIKEY RETURN. This prints 'Maxplayers = 10' and one 'Player N:  Name: FleetNNN  Flags: ..  ID: ..' line per slot (0x53d760). 'session' prints '%d players in session' and 'Player %x (%S) is in the session' (0x53ca20). Both are registered with no devMode check, in the same block as the documented ping and kick (0x53c710-0x53c7a8). Untried on hardware.
(3) Every box's HUD prints '<name> has joined the game' (misc\sithstrings.uni).
In-game frames on every box except .124 are 8-bpp DirectDraw and photograph with wrong colours; read the text shapes.
server.log_how:
There is no server log.
- On host .123, EXEC netstat -n -p tcp shows one or more ESTABLISHED lines per joiner IP, in the form 'TCP 192.168.1.123:23xx  192.168.1.<joiner>:<port>  ESTABLISHED'. DirectPlay TCP/IP uses 47624 for enumeration and 2300-2400 for the session; the DF2 README measured 'TCP 2300 connections both ways'.
- Each joiner's own netstat shows ESTABLISHED to 192.168.1.123.
- Before committing, each joiner's 16-bit 'Choose one of these games to join' frame shows 'Players: n of 10'. Joined one at a time, the count climbs from 1 to 7.
server.bots_note: No bots. The Sith engine has none in MP, so every name in the tally is a real box.
server.changes_needed: The host launcher writes REG_BINARY 0a000000 (10) to maxPlayers in the HKLM MotS key before start. The game reads it with a 4-byte query that ignores the value type (0x561ad0) and pre-fills the Max players box. The engine accepts 1..32. Nothing changes on 192.168.1.132.
server.join_port_note: DirectPlay TCP/IP: TCP/UDP 47624 for enumeration (DPLAYSVR.EXE), TCP/UDP 2300-2400 for game traffic. The firewall is off fleet-wide.

launchers.bat:
@echo off
rem Jedi Knight - Mysteries of the Sith: fleet LAN HOST, DirectPlay TCP/IP, Max players 10.
rem No dedicated server and no connect switch exist: after the intro the round drives
rem Players - Multiplayer - Host Game - Internet TCP/IP - OK - OK - OK with UICLICK and UIKEY.
taskkill /f /im ssstars.scr >nul 2>&1
cd /d "C:\Games\JediKnightMotS"
if exist FLEETRES.BAT call FLEETRES.BAT
cd /d "C:\Games\JediKnightMotS"
if exist JKMODE.EXE if defined FR_W JKMODE.EXE mots %FR_W% %FR_H% > JKMODE.LOG 2>&1
if not exist "player\fleet\fleet.mpc" echo MISSING player\fleet\fleet.mpc - the game will answer No Valid Characters
if not exist "player\{name}" mkdir "player\{name}"
if not exist "player\{name}\{name}.plr" copy /y "player\fleet\fleet.plr" "player\{name}\{name}.plr" >nul
if not exist "player\{name}\fleet.mpc" copy /y "player\fleet\fleet.mpc" "player\{name}\fleet.mpc" >nul
reg add "HKLM\SOFTWARE\LucasArts Entertainment Company LLC\Mysteries of the Sith\v1.0" /v playerShortName /t REG_SZ /d {name} /f >nul
reg add "HKLM\SOFTWARE\LucasArts Entertainment Company LLC\Mysteries of the Sith\v1.0" /v maxPlayers /t REG_BINARY /d 0a000000 /f >nul
start "" JKM.EXE
launchers.notes:
Write as C:\fleetmp\JediKnightMotS-host.bat (lanparty.py key '<game>-host'). host={box:123, bat:..., wait:45, exe:'JKM.EXE'}; box 123 must NOT be in 'bats'.
- taskkill: every XP box has ssstars.scr in the foreground right now (WINLIST 2026-11-11; ScreenSaveTimeOut 600, not password-protected). A synthetic click would only dismiss it.
- FLEETRES.BAT and JKMODE.EXE are not in the staged tree (case-insensitive check), so both guarded lines do nothing today. The title is registered resolution-incapable (gameres.h gr_incapable; PER-TITLE-STATUS.md). jk-helper's JKMODE.EXE (argument 'mots'; written against this exact JKM.EXE, md5 192d2be2...) is built but not published. The cd, FLEETRES, JKMODE, start order matches apply.py's reference launcher.
- The GUI is always 640x480. In game each box keeps its stored displayMode. Only .124 has one (D3D HAL, 0x25); the others start the default 640x480 8-bpp software mode.
- The pilot is player\Fleet123\Fleet123.plr: plain text, named by its folder and file name. The MP character MUST stay fleet.mpc. Its lines are decrypted with a rolling key = 5 + sum of toupper(basename) (0x434dd0, decoder 0x4355e0); keyed on 'Fleet110.mpc', the staged file's 'version 2' turns into 'fgioqhe30'.
- maxPlayers is 10, not 8: the box accepts up to 32, and spare slots absorb a failed join.
- Never write 'Version'. Any value other than "0.1" makes the game delete the whole key at start-up, CD Path included (0x5618e1-0x561990).
- No parentheses anywhere.

JediKnightMotS.in_game_proof:
Machine-checkable evidence first, then the names.

(1) HOST NETSTAT: EXEC netstat -n -p tcp on .123 shows ESTABLISHED connections (DirectPlay 2300-2400 / 47624) to each of the seven joiner IPs. This is the per-IP witness, since no server log exists.

(2) JOINER COUNT FRAMES: each joiner's 16-bit 'Choose one of these games to join' frame, taken before it commits, shows 'Players: n of 10'. With commits made one at a time, the count climbs from 1 to 7. The 7th joiner's frame reading 'Players: 7 of 10' proves seven players were in the session before it; its own entry makes 8. These menus are 16-bit and photograph legibly.

(3) NAMES, on the host, by hand (lanparty.py check skips .123):
- UIKEY TILDE opens the Multiplayer Tally. Expect 8 names and no bots: Fleet110, Fleet123, Fleet124, Fleet133, Fleet143, Fleet171, Fleet184, Fleet240. Take SCREENSHOT 0 within about 2 s.
- Console: UIKEY T, UIKEY TAB, UIKEY TEXT:players, UIKEY RETURN prints 'Maxplayers = 10' and one 'Player N:  Name: FleetNNN ...' line per box. The command is registered without devMode but is untried on hardware.
- The in-game frame is 8-bpp, so its colours are wrong; read the text shapes.

(4) PER JOINER: its own netstat shows ESTABLISHED to 192.168.1.123, and its HUD shows '<name> has joined the game' lines.

A running JKM.EXE, or DPLAYSVR.EXE on the host, is not proof.
JediKnightMotS.screenshot_notes:
MENUS: MotS draws its GUI in 640x480 16-bit, and XP GDI 'SCREENSHOT 0' captures it: see the perbox 2026-08-31 frames for .123/.133/.143 and the dark-sith-review 2026-09-29 frames for .240 and .145. Use SCREENSHOT 0, not lanparty.py's SCREENSHOT 1, which halves a 640x480 mode to 320x240, too small for the info lines.

IN GAME: every box except .124 has no stored displayMode and starts the default 640x480 8-bpp software mode (provisioning/patches/jk-helper/apply.py). An 8-bpp DirectDraw exclusive game photographs with the right geometry and the wrong colours (CLAUDE.md names Jedi Knight). .124 stores D3D HAL (3DDeviceGUID = IID_IDirect3DHALDevice, displayMode 0x25) and renders 1280x960 in true colour.

PER BOX:
- .124 (vcr-kmd Voodoo 5 6000): GDI photographs the old desktop. Use EXECW 30 C:\vcr\vcrctl.exe fbshot C:\fleetmp\fb.bmp, then DOWNLOAD; lanparty.py does this for .124. Its 2026-09-28 fbshots show the Players screen, Setup and the game.
- .240: its 2026-08-31 perbox frame was black (an earlier card), but on 2026-09-29 GDI photographed every MotS menu there (dark-sith-review 240_mots_01..09, ATI on Catalyst 8.593.100.0, the driver it still runs). The X1950 Pro itself is untried with MotS.
- .123 (host): lanparty.py check never photographs it. Take its tally and console frames by hand.

lanparty.py check has no roster query or sniff for this title, so its joiner frames are the only automatic evidence. Add the host tally frame and the host netstat.
known_blockers: No dedicated server on any platform and no connect switch (JKM.EXE switch table at .data 0x57d15c-0x57d28c). Every box needs a scripted GUI walk; lanparty.py run on its own only gets each box to its intro and Players screen.

No DirectPlay lobby route today. JKM.EXE imports DPLAYX ordinal 4 (DirectPlayLobbyCreateA) and has lobby-launch handling (state 0x8d48f8; 'Waiting for host to select options'). But HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\DirectPlay\Applications is EMPTY on all nine boxes (REGREAD 2026-11-11), so lobby-launching straight into a session would need a new registration plus a new lobby-client tool.

The host's Max players defaults to 4 (0x401019), and .123 stores no value. The host launcher must therefore pre-set maxPlayers (10 here), or the 5th joiner gets 'That game is full'. The engine limit is 32 ('Max players (up to 32):', clamp 0x414131); 8 is only the manual's tested LAN level.

No FLEETRES.BAT and no JKMODE.EXE in the staged tree (case-insensitive check). The title is registered resolution-incapable (gameres.h gr_incapable; PER-TITLE-STATUS.md). jk-helper's JKMODE.EXE is built but not published (apply.py --publish is marked FUTURE). In game, every box except .124 runs 640x480 8-bpp software.

JediKnightDF2/README-FLEET.txt says the profile files are plain text and can be renamed per box, and MotS's README-FLEET.txt imports that note ('Everything in JediKnightDF2/README-FLEET.txt applies'). It is true for DF2, whose fleet.mpc is plain text ('version 1'). It is false for MotS: the .mpc is encrypted with a rolling key = 5 + sum of toupper(own basename) (0x434dd0, 0x4345c0, 0x56c7f0; decoder 0x4355e0). The host queues concurrent joins itself ('Host is busy - waiting for our turn to join'), but serial commits keep each frame and netstat line attributable. review_issues: PLAYER LIMIT IS 32, NOT 8. The host screen itself reads 'Max players (up to 32):' (GUI_MAXPLAYERS in ui\jkstrings.uni, extracted from Resource\JKMsndLO.goo). JKM.EXE clamps the field to 1..32 (0x414131), which the recipe itself quotes. Manual p.24 calls 8 the level 'tested to be stable' and says 'the game can possibly accommodate more players'; README.TXT 5a says the same. So the mp_summary claim, the known_blocker ('leaves no room for .145/.197 or a 9th box') and the exclusion reasons for .145, .197 and .186 ('cap already filled', '9th player') are wrong. Corrected: the host writes maxPlayers=10 (0a000000), which leaves two spare slots so a ghost slot from a failed join cannot lock the 8th box out.

The ESC intro skip IS proven in this binary, against the recipe's 'not proven'. On .240 on 2026-09-29, one ESC on the LucasArts logo went straight to the Players screen (.claude/evidence-1080p/dark-sith-review/240_mots_01_after_launch.png -> 240_mots_02_after_esc.png). README.TXT 3b also says 'To skip cutscenes, press the Escape key'. An ESC that lands on the start-up Players screen does nothing, because that screen is opened with no ESC element (0x4133bf-0x4133d0). load_wait_sec lowered from 150 to 45: wait for the intro, then send ESC.

The Players screen appears on EVERY launch, whether or not playerShortName is set. The flag at 0x57f634 starts at 1 and is cleared at 0x412bce after the first showing (0x412bc0-0x412bd8). So the rationale 'No box stores playerShortName today, so it appears' is wrong, and the 'if the main menu shows instead' branch never happens. At start-up the screen has no Cancel button: its visible flag is set at 0x41338f. The buttons are New Player, Remove and Ok.

False factual claims about the registry. .124 DOES store maxPlayers=04 00 00 00 and playerShortName='fleet' (live REGREAD 2026-11-11; written by an earlier clean quit). This contradicts 'no box has the value stored' and 'No box stores playerShortName today'. It is harmless: .124 is a joiner, and its launcher overwrites playerShortName.

On-screen labels are wrong. The button the recipe calls 'Start Game' reads 'Host Game' (GUI_STARTGAME = "Host Game"; the manual also says Host Game). 'Synchronizing' is really 'Contacting host computer...' (GUI_SYNCHRONIZING); 0x5857d8 is the waiting-menu struct, not that string. 'Game is full' is really 'That game is full'.

The host defaults are misdescribed. gameFlags 0x90 decodes (0x413cd6-0x413cf8) to Score limit ON at 100, Time limit OFF, Single-level ON, Personalities. No 30-minute time limit is active (30 is only the value in the unticked box), so the level ends only at 100 points.

The recipe never deals with the screensaver. On all 8 XP boxes the foreground window right now is the ssstars.scr screensaver (WINLIST class WindowsScreenSaverClass and PROCLIST, 2026-11-11; ScreenSaveTimeOut 600, ScreenSaverIsSecure 0). The first synthetic click or key would only dismiss it. Added 'taskkill /f /im ssstars.scr' to both launchers, plus a WINLIST foreground check before each box's next key: during the serial walk, an idle box can bring the saver back after 10 minutes.

lanparty.py check never photographs the HOST. applicable() keeps only boxes that bat_for() gives a joiner launcher, and .123 must not have one. So the box carrying the tally and console proof is skipped. Its frames and netstat must be taken by hand. shot_box also uses SCREENSHOT 1, which halves a 640x480 menu to 320x240, too small to read the 'Players: n of N' line. Use SCREENSHOT 0.

roster_names_available=true overstated what tooling can get: there is no machine-readable roster. roster() returns None (no query), sniff only runs when the host is 192.168.1.132, and names exist only in host screenshots. Set to false; roster_how keeps the screen route.

README attribution was wrong. The 'plain text, can be renamed per box' claim is in JediKnightDF2/README-FLEET.txt, where it is TRUE: DF2's staged fleet.mpc is plain text, 'version 1'. MotS's README-FLEET.txt only imports it ('Everything in JediKnightDF2/README-FLEET.txt applies'). The substance is verified for MotS: decoding the staged fleet.mpc with the key taken from its name 'fleet.mpc' (0x434dd0, decoder 0x4355e0) gives 'version 2'; keying it on 'Fleet110.mpc' turns the first line into 'fgioqhe30'.

The .240 claim was stale: MotS screenshots there are not 'untried'. GDI photographed every MotS menu on .240 on 2026-09-29 (dark-sith-review 240_mots_01..09, an ATI card on Catalyst 8.593.100.0, the same driver version it runs now). Only the 2026-08-31 perbox frame was black.

Join timing was misframed. Launch timing does not matter, because every box waits indefinitely at its own Players screen. lanparty.py run launches all joiners after the host's wait anyway, which contradicts 'launch only after the host is in the level'. What matters is the commit: the host queues concurrent joins itself ('Host is busy - waiting for our turn to join', GUINET_JOININGBUSY). Commits are still done one box at a time, so each frame and netstat line can be attributed to one box.

The provider row is not derivable from the binary. The game appends providers in the order dplayx's EnumConnections calls back (0x434290) and preselects row 0 (0x415e8c). XP's registry order is Internet TCP/IP, IPX, Modem, Serial (REGREAD, all 8 boxes). The only evidence for 'TCP/IP is the 4th row' is the DF2 README's word order. Changed to: read the frame, then click.

Stale environment fact: IPX is now active on all 8 XP boxes (HWPROFILE ipx.state=active, winsock=true). So the DF2 README's 'no IPX protocol is installed' no longer holds. The IPX provider lists sessions with no Locate Session dialog (manual); recorded as an UNTESTED fallback only. TCP/IP stays the proven route.

The .186 exclusion reasoning is corrected. Its GPU is NVIDIA 10DE:1F82, a Turing GTX 1650-class card, running on the Standard VGA driver under 32-bit Win7. NVIDIA's 32-bit driver line ended before Turing, so no vendor driver can fix it. DirectDraw there is unaccelerated, and whether it offers MotS's 640x480x16 menu mode is unmeasured. The '9th player' reason is dropped.

Smaller fixes. The console commands 'players' and 'session' are registered with no devMode check, in the same block as the documented ping and kick (0x53c710-0x53c7a8; the devMode test comes after, at 0x53c7ad). They should therefore work in a normal MP game; noted as untried on hardware. The lanparty_titles.json host entry needs exe 'JKM.EXE' (exes_of reads host.exe) and an explicit 8-box 'boxes' list. At probe time .124 had cmd.exe and ping.exe running, so confirm it is free before the round.

RainbowSix.mp_summary: No host server can exist. RainbowSix.exe is GOG v1.04, the same 4,899,328-byte build on all 9 boxes. Its command-line parser takes only setup, shelljump, precalc, keymap, -server and -client, so there is no dedicated-server switch. 192.168.1.132 has no R6 unit and no gameservers.py entry. The 1.02A patch note 'Fixed an error launching a server from the command line' refers to the lobby-launch switches, which are verified in the binary. '-server <port>' starts a listen server, and the host also plays in it. It shows a 'Multiplayer Starting' screen first, then the Multiplayer Sessions screen: 0x4FE3F5 sets mode 13 once the server object is up, the same object and mode as the UI's Create Game at 0x519EAF. '-client <host> <port>' connects straight to that server and joins the same screen once its login is accepted. Both skip the intro FMV and the main menu. The parser is at 0x40AC80 and matches tokens with _stricmp, so case does not matter. The token order, host then port, is fixed by three things: the accessors 0x4141E0 (host) and 0x4141F0 (port); the 16-slot LIFO stack (ctor 0x40E740, push 0x40F330, pop 0x40F390); and mode 19's Set(1, host, atoi(port)) at 0x40EF8E. Ports: TCP 2346 is the join port and the Lighthouse TCP listener (backlog 5); 2347 is announce; 2348 is info. The player name is the HKLM REG_SZ value MultiplayerPlayerName, default 'JOHN DOE' from Constants.txt. Each launcher sets it to Fleet<octet> with reg add before starting the game. It also sets a distinct MultiplayerCharacter, so a COOPERATIVE lobby cannot collide on Chavez.act. The host is .123: it is the strongest box and has a verified ddraw 640x480 render. .124 also reached the menu on 11-08, but its vcr-kmd D3D HAL is the riskiest. The host plays and 7 clients join, which makes 8 players, exactly the co-op cap in the manual. The proof is on the host box: the CONNECTED PLAYERS list in a screenshot, plus one netstat ESTABLISHED row on :2346 per client IP. One START MISSION click on the host moves the lobby into the 3D action phase.

excluded_boxes.reason: No display driver. Windows 7 runs its GTX 1650-class card (PCI 10DE:1F82) on the in-box Standard VGA Graphics Adapter: service vga, 16 MB, DRIVERS STATUS 'generic'. This is a driver gap, not a hardware limit. R6's software renderer sets the gate floor to 'gpu none', so the shortcut exists, but nobody has seen this build draw on a driverless adapter. The only measurement, docs/win10-compatibility.md row 27, is a solid black surface on Windows 11's Basic Display driver, a different driver model. Also, the 8 XP boxes already fill the 8-player co-op cap. Test it on its own once a display driver is installed. Note: 'Win7 GDI cannot photograph fullscreen' was measured on .197 and .246, which run WDDM drivers with DWM; it is unproven for this XDDM driver.

Not deployed and has no shortcut. An operator gate override says 'not wanted on .243' (scripts/gamegate/overrides.txt line 50, profile d931bfe6c33fae5e; compat DB shows 'gated'). R6 would be software-only there anyway: it has no Glide path, so the Voodoo 2 adds nothing. Its launchers would also have to be written in COMMAND.COM dialect.

launchers.bat:
@echo off
rem Rainbow Six 1998 LAN round - HOST {name}. RainbowSix.exe -server PORT is a listen server: this box plays as the host player.
rem No FLEETRES call: the tree has no FLEETRES.BAT - the shell is fixed at 640x480 and the 3D mode is the registry value VideoResolution.
rem Guard: if RainbowSix.exe already runs here this box is already hosting - never start a second -server instance.
tasklist /fi "imagename eq RainbowSix.exe" | find /i "RainbowSix.exe" > nul
if not errorlevel 1 exit
cd /d "C:\Games\RainbowSix"
set R6KEY=HKLM\SOFTWARE\Red Storm Entertainment\Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six
reg add "%R6KEY%" /v MultiplayerPlayerName /t REG_SZ /d {name} /f > C:\fleetmp\RainbowSix.log 2>&1
reg add "%R6KEY%" /v MultiplayerOnLan /t REG_SZ /d TRUE /f >> C:\fleetmp\RainbowSix.log 2>&1
reg add "%R6KEY%" /v MultiplayerRandomTeams /t REG_SZ /d TRUE /f >> C:\fleetmp\RainbowSix.log 2>&1
reg add "%R6KEY%" /v MultiplayerCharacter /t REG_SZ /d Chavez.act /f >> C:\fleetmp\RainbowSix.log 2>&1
start "" RainbowSix.exe -server 2346
exit
launchers.notes: HOST, .123 only. Register this entry as the title's lanparty `host` (box 123, wait 45 or more) and keep .123 out of the client entry. If this text also ends up in `bats` for .123, lanparty's client phase relaunches it with kill-first skipped for the host box; the tasklist guard then turns that second launch into a no-op instead of a second -server instance. Launch it FIRST. Then poll 'EXECW 20 netstat -an -p tcp' on .123 every ~10 s, for up to 120 s, until '192.168.1.123:2346 ... LISTENING' appears; only then start the clients. Booleans are REG_SZ TRUE/FALSE, the game's own format: 0x459D10 upper-cases the value and matches only the strings TRUE and FALSE (0x89DF90/0x89DF94). In a team variant, MultiplayerRandomTeams=TRUE assigns the BLUE/GOLD sides, so nobody has to click a team. The host keeps Chavez.act, which no client uses. Fallback host if .123 fails: give .110 this same text, remove .110 from the client entry, add .123 to it, and set {host} to 192.168.1.110.

RainbowSix.in_game_proof:
This title is peer-hosted: there is nothing on .132 to query, and the dev host cannot see box-to-box traffic. The proof therefore lives on the host box, .123.

(1) Strongest, and names each box: .123's Multiplayer Sessions screen. CONNECTED PLAYERS lists every joined player under the name its launcher wrote: Fleet110, Fleet124 and so on, plus the host, Fleet123. The shell font may show the names in capitals, so compare case-insensitively. The COMMUNICATIONS box also prints '<name> has connected' (sherman_networking.txt). Take SCREENSHOT 0 on .123; XP GDI photographs R6's 640x480x16 fullscreen, as /home/voidsstr/lan-proof/rainbowsix/r6_123_main_menu.png shows (2026-09-01).

(2) Names each box by IP: 'EXECW 20 netstat -an -p tcp' on .123 should list one 'TCP 192.168.1.123:2346 192.168.1.<octet>:<n> ESTABLISHED' row per client. The listener binds the host's own address, not 0.0.0.0. Before the clients start, the same command must show '192.168.1.123:2346 ... LISTENING' (host readiness). On 2026-11-11, .123 had nothing on TCP or UDP 2346-2348.

(3) Each client's own frame of the same session screen, plus its own netstat ESTABLISHED row to 192.168.1.123:2346.

(4) After START MISSION on the host, every box's frame shows the 3D action phase. In the action phase, F12 on the host opens the Server Control dialog (manual key card: 'Activate Server Control Dialog'; buttons LOCK SERVER / USE PASSWORD / EJECT PLAYER), whose player list names everyone connected.

A running RainbowSix.exe proves nothing. A client that failed to connect sits with its process alive at an in-game dialog: either 'Connection to the server could not be established' (MPMenuError.txt) or 'Connection to the game server ...' (MPConnectionFailure.txt). After any failure, DOWNLOAD C:\Games\RainbowSix\Sherman.log from that box; Lighthouse socket, bind and listen errors are written there.

first_run.symptom: CLIENT: 'Connection to the server could not be established' (MPMenuError.txt, the command-launch screen's own failure), or 'Connection to the game server could not be established / timed out during login' (MPConnectionFailure.txt)
first_run.keys: Do not try to click through it: dismissing the command-launch dialog appears to end the game (0x4FE050 calls DestroyWindow). first_run.notes: Causes, most likely first: the client started before the host was listening; the host died; the connect was refused because the host's 5-deep backlog was full (it accepts one connection per poll, 0x4290B0), so stagger the clients. R6's own dialogs are drawn by the game, not Windows MessageBoxes.

first_run.notes: The exe imports no DirectInput, no GetAsyncKeyState and no GetKeyState, and loads no dinput by name. Input arrives only as window messages, with GetCursorPos/SetCursorPos for the cursor, so the agent's absolute clicks and keys should land, unlike id Tech 3 or relative-mouse titles. This is not yet proven. In a team variant, the host bat's MultiplayerRandomTeams=TRUE assigns BLUE/GOLD. If the lobby is COOPERATIVE, the per-box MultiplayerCharacter keeps every roster pick distinct. After the click, Constants.txt's MAX_NETWORK_START_GAME_DELAY 180 gives slow clients up to 180 s to load.

known_blockers: Nothing blocks the lobby itself. There is no CD key, no disc check (InstallType=Full) and no SafeDisc (sections .text/.rdata/.data/.rsrc only, no BoG_ marker), and all 8 boxes have the same v1.04 tree. All 8 players can be connected and named in the session with no person present. The missing MPCommandLaunch.txt is not a blocker, because compiled fallback text is used.
Moving from the session lobby into the 3D action phase needs one START MISSION click on the host. Clicks should work, because input is window messages only, but this has not been shown.
risks: The -server/-client direct-launch path is verified only in the binary and has never been run on this fleet; Rainbow Six multiplayer is 'untested' on every box in the compat DB. Only the server's switch into the Multiplayer Sessions screen (mode 13) has been traced. The client's switch on login is inferred from it using the same client object as the UI's join.

.124 runs the vcr-kmd D3D HAL with Diag D3D32=1 and D3DBigTex=7 armed (read back 2026-11-11). R6 reached its intro and main menu there by hand on vcrdd 95678704 (2026-11-08), but the lobby and the D3D action phase have never run there, and this HAL has stalled games before. Join .124 last, close it with WM_CLOSE (taskkill without /f; lanparty's kill uses PROCKILL), and pace relaunches: it has a 1998 CRT, so allow one mode switch per launch. The roster line in scripts/fleet/fleet-roster.txt saying 'Rainbow Six fails with them' has been stale since 11-08.

Host .123 (ATI HD 3850, Catalyst 8.970) has only been seen at the 2D main menu. The D3D action phase of a 1998 DX6 title on a 2013 ATI driver is untested. If the host's 3D fails at mission start, every client is dropped. Fallback host: .110 (GeForce 7800 GS).

The default game type is unknown. MultiplayerGameType is DWORD 0 (Constants.txt MP_OPTIONS_GAME_TYPE 0), and AdversarialGame, MissionMapCoop and MissionMapAdvr are empty. Whether 0 means ADVERSARIAL or COOPERATIVE has not been traced; mpsessio.txt lists ADVERSARIAL first. Co-op caps at 8 players (manual, Appendix A), exactly the 8 applicable boxes, so powering on .145 or .197 as a 9th would exceed it. The adversarial cap is not stated in the local manual or readme. Some maps fail with 'No insertion zone for cooperative play'. The per-box MultiplayerCharacter removes the Chavez collision in co-op.

Double launch on the host is guarded, not impossible. Each bat exits if RainbowSix.exe already runs on its box. A tool that kills R6 and relaunches with no pause can therefore have the guard skip the launch, which is a visible failure: no :2346 LISTENING. lanparty sleeps 4 s after a kill, which covers this.

The host accepts one TCP connection per poll into a backlog of 5 (0x4290B0, listen at 0x429338). Seven clients connecting in the same instant can see refusals, so stagger the client launches. A refused client needs one relaunch.

R6 has never been started on .110, .133, .143, .171, .184 or .240 (GeForce 7800 GS, GeForce4 Ti, GeForce 6800, FX 5500, GeForce2, X1950 Pro). The slow boxes, .133 (P3-700 dual) and .184 (P3-845), may need more than the 90 s wait.

Library finding, not changed: install.reg writes FullScreen and SoftwareOnly as REG_DWORD, but the game reads booleans as REG_SZ TRUE/FALSE (0x459D10). The DWORDs are ignored, and the compiled defaults FullScreen TRUE and SoftwareOnly FALSE (0x41458E/0x414595) are what actually apply. This is harmless, but install.reg's comment claiming it sets fullscreen is wrong. On .124 the game has already rewritten FullScreen as REG_SZ 'TRUE'.

After the round, MultiplayerPlayerName, MultiplayerCharacter, MultiplayerOnLan and (on the host) MultiplayerRandomTeams stay changed in HKLM. That is harmless, and GAMESYNC will not revert them because install.reg does not carry them.
ESC quits the game from the shell and from the intro; never send it.

review_issues: Double launch on the host box. The .123 host bat appears both as host_box's launcher and as a `launchers` entry for .123. Mapped onto lanparty.py's model (`host` + `bats`), applicable() keeps .123, and the client phase relaunches that entry with kill-first deliberately skipped for the host box. That starts a second `RainbowSix.exe -server 2346`, which cannot bind 2346 and fights the first for DirectDraw exclusive mode. Fixed: both bats now exit if RainbowSix.exe is already running (tasklist and find are present on all 8 boxes, checked live), and the host notes say to register that entry as `host` only.

Wrong count: '7 of the 8 boxes have never started R6'. .123 and .124 both have Sherman.log and 110 values under the HKLM key, 68 of them written by the game. Six boxes have never started it: .110 .133 .143 .171 .184 .240. The recipe's own risks list already said six, so the two parts disagreed.

Wrong claim: '.123 is the only box where R6 has been seen rendering'. .124 reached the intro and main menu on 2026-11-08 on vcrdd 95678704 (vcr-kmd/evidence/d3dtune_1014/sweep_1108_fixed/RainbowSix_intro_then_menu_z16in32.png, commit be58b7d), and the recipe's own risks section says so. .123 is still the right host: strongest box, a verified ddraw 640x480 render in the compat DB, and a safer D3D path than .124's HAL.

Team names: v1.04 shows BLUE / GOLD / UNAFFILIATED (mpsessio.txt; data\bitmap\el_mp_adv_bluebtn.RSB and el_mp_adv_goldbtn.RSB). ALPHA/BRAVO is the pre-patch manual's wording, so anyone checking a lobby frame for ALPHA/BRAVO would not find it.

The first screen is not the lobby. Modes 19/20 build their own class, 0x4FDB70, and those two modes are its only callers. That class loads data\text\interface\english\MPCommandLaunch.txt, which is absent from the tree and from GOG's galaxyFileList and hashdb (searched case-insensitively). This is non-fatal: 0x4FE460 falls back to compiled text, 'Multiplayer Starting' (host) or 'Multiplayer Connecting' (client), shown over mp_bg. Added to first_run.

The host half of 'straight to the lobby' is now proven from the binary, and there is a failure dialog the recipe missed. Once the server object (0x69C800) starts, 0x4FE3F5 sets next mode 13. Mode 13 is the Multiplayer Sessions class 0x50B1C0, which loads mpsa_plyrop, mpsa_gameop, mpsa_connplyrs and mp_chatbox. That is the same server object and the same mode the UI's own Create Game uses at 0x519EAF. If the server fails to start, the host shows an in-game MPMenuError 'Failure' dialog; that is now in first_run. The client's switch to mode 13 on login was not traced and is listed as a risk.

'No usable log' was too strong. Sherman.log is opened on the same log object (0x8B3DA8, stream 0x8B3DB4) that receives every 'Lighthouse: TCP/IP listening port socket()/bind()/listen() error <code>' line and every UDP socket error, even with LOG_NETWORK_MESSAGES 0. Joins are not logged, but a failed host or join is. log_how and in_game_proof now say to DOWNLOAD Sherman.log after a failure.

The co-op character collision was left as 'optional insurance'. Every box defaults to Chavez.act (Constants.txt MP_OPTIONS_CHARACTER), the manual makes co-op characters first-come-first-served, and the default game type is unknown. Both launchers now write a distinct MultiplayerCharacter. The host keeps Chavez; clients are keyed on {name}: Burke, Lofquist, Bogart, Beckenba, Arnavisc, DuBarry, Filatov, Haider. All of these files are in data\actor, and the mapping stays collision-free if .110 becomes the fallback host.

Incomplete client-failure text. The command-launch screen's own connect failure (0x4FE150 into MPMenuError.txt) reads 'Connection to the server could not be established'. The 'Connection to the game server ...' strings (MPConnectionFailure.txt) cover failures during login. Dismissing the command-launch dialog appears to end the game (handler 0x4FE050 calls DestroyWindow at 0x40A7A0), so 'do not click through, relaunch' is right either way.

Unmentioned host accept limit. The Lighthouse TCP listener uses listen backlog 5 (0x429338), and accept() fills a single slot per poll (0x4290B0), so clients connecting in the same instant can be refused. The notes now say to stagger client launches a few seconds apart.

Unmentioned screensaver. ssstars.scr was running on all 8 boxes at probe time (PROCLIST, 2026-11-11). On XP the screensaver runs on its own desktop, so a first_run step now ends it before LAUNCH. This is a precaution only: the 10-13 party's launches did take the foreground.

.186 exclusion reasoning, partly unproven. 'Win7 GDI cannot photograph exclusive fullscreen' was measured on .197 and .246, which run WDDM drivers with DWM. .186 runs the XDDM Standard VGA driver (service vga), where DWM is off. Win10-compat row 27 was measured on Windows 11's Basic Display driver, a different driver model. The exclusion still stands on two other grounds: the GTX 1650-class 10DE:1F82 has no driver (DRIVERS STATUS 'generic'), and the 8-player co-op cap is already filled. It is a driver gap, not a hardware limit.
Incomplete fallback-host instruction. If .110 hosts, .110 must come out of the client entry and .123 must go into it. Otherwise .110 runs two instances and .123 runs none.

Unmeasured timings stated as fact. Shogo.title_display: Shogo: Mobile Armor Division - LithTech 1, patch 2.2
Shogo.mp_summary: A host server is already running: shogo-server (ShogoSrv 2.2, the staged tree's own binary, under Wine in docker container shogosrv on 192.168.1.132, UDP 27888). Its ShogoSrv.exe, server.dll and all six REZ files have the same md5 as the library. A GameSpy \status\ query on the game port itself was answered again at about 14:00 on 2026-11-11: hostname 'NSC Retro Fleet Arena - Shogo', gamever 'shogo 2.2', map MCA_12FLOZ, 0 of 16 players. ss shows only UDP 0.0.0.0:27888 open and no DirectPlay ports, so the server uses LithTech's own 'internet' TCP/IP driver. Shogo has no bots. Each box starts the engine (Client.exe) directly, with the staged -rez chain in the same last-wins order as 'Play Shogo - direct engine.bat', plus these arguments: +NetHost 0 +NetPlayerName Fleet<octet> +UpdateRateInitted 1 +UpdateRate 20 +HaveSettingInfo 1 +DontDisplaySettingsDialog 1 +NetJoinRetry 10 +Connect {host}. Independently re-verified in the disassembly of CShell v3 (carved from SHOGOP3.REZ at 0x2bca8, md5 eb0286632a78bd488bd0f41f37114c4d) and Client.exe (md5 4e6a063fcdc6f39d9f26022faa0a2d09): (1) Client.exe sets console variables in pass 2 (autoexec.cfg first, then the '+' arguments, so the command line wins) before it calls the shell's OnEngineInitialized. (2) OnEngineInitialized calls NetStart (0x1001f560) when Connect is set and is not '0'. (3) The wizard's command-line handler (0x10022a30) returns 2 for Connect, copies NetPlayerName (default 'Sanjuro') as the player name, and skips every wizard page. (4) The NET_SETTINGS gate (0x100237b0, dialog 'Shogo Multiplayer Settings') is skipped when HaveSettingInfo and DontDisplaySettingsDialog are both set and Shift is not held. (5) StartGame type 3 (TCP address) goes through the engine's 'internet' driver, whose ConnectTCP parses ip[:port] with a default of 27888 (0x6cf0). (6) NetJoinRetry retries up to 10 times with Sleep(1000). (7) After success, OnEngineInitialized jumps past runworld, the intro movies and the menu (0x100303ca). +UpdateRateInitted 1 is required: without it, CShell's first-init block forces UpdateRate 6 on the six boxes whose autoexec.cfg lacks the flag. No CD is needed for multiplayer (retail Readme), and Client.exe/Shogo.exe have no SafeDisc marker. This route has NEVER been run. No two-box Shogo join has ever completed on this fleet (compat DB: needs_human). Smoke-test it on ONE box first (.143 or .171, where Shogo D3D is verified): confirm player_0 = Fleet<octet> in \status\, then launch the other seven. No host log records a join, so the proof that each box is in the game comes from the player_N names in the GameSpy roster, a tcpdump count of packets per source IP to port 27888, and a read-only xwd capture of ShogoSrv's Players list.

excluded_boxes.reason: No display driver. Windows 7 is running its NVIDIA PCI\VEN_10DE&DEV_1F82 card (a GTX 1650-class part) on the Standard VGA driver (display.inf; the DirectX registry reads 4.09), so there is no Direct3D. Shogo IS installed at C:\Games\Shogo. The gate gave the box 0 shortcuts (requires.json puts requires_capabilities disc_mount at title level and .186 has disc_mount=false), but the C:\fleetmp launcher does not need a shortcut, so that is not the blocker. CShell would fall back to 640x480x16 and then soft.ren on Standard VGA, which has never been tried, and Win7 GDI frames come back black. Re-evaluate if this readiness pass installs the GeForce driver; the roster and sniff would then be the only proof.

Not installed. The published gate verdict carries an operator override: 'not wanted on .243: the user kept Quake/Quake II/UT, flight sims and 3D-noteworthy titles only (2026-09-29)'. The box is also below the title's 200 MHz floor (P166) and has disc_mount=false. Shogo ships only d3d.ren and soft.ren, with no Glide renderer, so the Voodoo 2 could not help.

server.unit: shogo-server
server.query_kind: gamespy
server.roster_how: GameSpy \status\ to UDP 192.168.1.132:27888. With players connected, the reply should add \player_N\<name>\frags_N\<n>\ping_N\<ms> (the player_%i/frags_%i/ping_%i keys are in ShogoSrv.exe's responder, but none have been seen live), and numplayers is the count. In the titles file, list these eight IPs explicitly rather than '*'. lanparty renders {name} as Fleet<octet> and {host} as 192.168.1.132, converts to CRLF and ASCII, uploads to C:\fleetmp\<key>.bat and LAUNCHes it. host_box.command:
@echo off
rem SiNGold LAN round - LISTEN SERVER on this box: deathmatch on spry, 16 slots, and this box plays too as {name}.
rem Never start a second sin.exe here - this box's player is the in-process loopback client of this server.
rem sin.exe splits its command line at every space and ignores quotes, so no +set value may contain a space.
cd /d "C:\Games\SiNGold"
call FLEETRES.BAT
cd /d "C:\Games\SiNGold"
> "C:\Games\SiNGold\base\fleetres.cfg" echo // written by the launcher at every start - do not edit
>>"C:\Games\SiNGold\base\fleetres.cfg" echo set gl_mode "%FR_Q2WIDE%"
>>"C:\Games\SiNGold\base\fleetres.cfg" echo set vid_fullscreen "1"
start "" sin.exe +set gl_mode %FR_Q2WIDE% +set vid_fullscreen 1 +set logfile 2 +set name {name} +set deathmatch 1 +set maxclients 16 +set timelimit 0 +set fraglimit 0 +set timeout 300 +set hostname NSC_Retro_Fleet_SiN +set rcon_password retroadmin +name {name} +map spry
exit

A joiner started early keeps resending its connect request every few seconds, so it does no harm.

Why .123: it is the proven SiN host (2026-08-31 listen server on spry, .240 joined) and the strongest XP box with a 3D driver (Athlon 64 4000+, Radeon HD 3850, 2 GB). SiN is verified fullscreen there at 1280x960 (perbox frame 123_SiNGold_Play_SiN_Gold.png); today's FR_Q2WIDE is 8.

Port handling: no juggling is needed. In a listen server the host's own player talks to the server in-process over loopback, so this single sin.exe owns UDP 22450 (plus its own client port). .123 must get NO client launcher; a second sin.exe there would collide.

How the command line reaches the engine, read from sin.exe:
- WinMain's parser (0x469660) splits at every space and IGNORES QUOTES. So no +set value may contain a space. The old `+set hostname "NSC Retro Fleet SiN"` became `set hostname "NSC`, which the console discards ('Line has unmatched quote, discarded.'). The hostname is now NSC_Retro_Fleet_SiN.
- Qcommon_Init (0x4286c1-0x42870d) runs the +set pass twice. The first runs before exec default.cfg and exec players/<player>/config.cfg, the second AFTER them. So every +set here beats any archived value; the archived config on .124 holds name Blade, maxclients 1 and hostname noname.
- autoexec.cfg runs later still, at the end of CL_Init. It sets none of name, deathmatch, maxclients, timelimit, fraglimit, timeout, hostname or rcon_password, so those +set values hold. `+name` (late buffer) is belt-and-braces only.

What each cvar is for:
- maxclients 16: SiN's SV_InitGame (0x463c3f) turns deathmatch maxclients <= 1 into 8, and caps it at 256. SERVERS-fleet.txt's listen-server example `+set maxclients 8` would turn away 2 of 10 boxes.
- timelimit 0 / fraglimit 0: spry never rotates mid-round. sv_maplist comes from autoexec.
- timeout 300: the server drops a client that is silent for `timeout` seconds. The default is 125 (sin.exe), and a P166 loading spry plus 10 players can take longer. The cost is that a crashed box holds its slot for up to 300 s; with 16 slots for 10 boxes that is harmless, and a relaunched box reuses its old slot from the same IP.
- rcon_password retroadmin: the fleet's public rcon convention. It lets the dev host read the status table with IPs.
- logfile 2: writes and flushes base\qconsole.log.

The match lives and dies with .123's client: never PROCKILL sin.exe on .123 during the round. Fallback host: .240 (Athlon 64 3300+, X1950 Pro). It is the 2026-08-31 SiN joiner, but that join was on a Radeon 9800 XT and its X1950 Pro has not run SiN yet. A host started there gets the same text with .240 as {host} everywhere.

The staged ds_deathmatch.bat is a dedicated, non-playing alternative, but it is not usable as is (library, NOT changed):
- it passes no maxclients, so it gets 8 slots;
- its quoted hostname is discarded;
- line 11 ends in a bare LF, so the next line `   ->  UDP <host>:22450` runs as a cmd command.

Optional untested follow-up: a Wages of SiN deathmatch. Use the same texts with `+set game 2015` on the host and every joiner, `+map 2015dm1`, and 2015\fleetres.cfg. 2015\pak0.sin ships 2015dm1-8 and hbdm1-5.

(1) Name to IP. From the dev host:

This returns the 'num score ping name lastmsg address qport' table, one row per client, with 192.168.1.<octet>:<port> beside Fleet<octet>.
- The host's own row reads 'loopback'.
- CNCT in the ping column means still connecting; ZMBI means dropped.
- Row regex: ^\s*\d+\s+-?\d+\s+(\d+|CNCT|ZMBI)\s+(Fleet\d+)\s+\d+\s+(\S+)
The table goes ONLY to the requester. While an rcon is answered, SiN's Com_Printf writes into the redirect buffer and returns (sin.exe 0x425495-0x42551c), so the table is never in qconsole.log.

(2) Transcript. DOWNLOAD C:\Games\SiNGold\base\qconsole.log from .123 (agent DOWNLOAD, no EXEC). It shows:
- 'Fleet<octet> connected' (gamex86 gi.dprintf to the server console);
- 'Fleet<octet> entered the game' and later 'Fleet<octet> disconnected' (broadcasts, printed by the host's own loopback client);
- 'Rcon from 192.168.1.132:' followed by the rcon COMMAND text, not its output.
Every joiner also writes its own base\qconsole.log; on .243 it starts at autoexec time. Read it on any box that never appears.

lanparty sniff (dev-host tcpdump) cannot see this traffic, because it flows box to box and lanparty only sniffs when the server is the dev host.

review_issues: Host `+set hostname "NSC Retro Fleet SiN"` never takes effect. sin.exe's WinMain parser (0x469660) splits the command line at every space and ignores quotes, so the early pass queues `set hostname "NSC`, which the console discards ('Line has unmatched quote, discarded.'). An emulation of the early pass on the original host line confirms this. The serverinfo keeps hostname 'noname', so roster_how's 'hostname NSC Retro Fleet SiN' can never appear. Fixed to `+set hostname NSC_Retro_Fleet_SiN`. rcon_password on the next +set is unaffected, because a newline always ends a console line (Cbuf_Execute 0x4213ff). The library's ds_deathmatch.bat has the same defect.

The init-order explanation is wrong. SiN's Qcommon_Init runs the +set pass twice: before AND after `exec default.cfg` and `exec players/<player>/config.cfg` (0x4286c1-0x42870d, Quake II's design). So `+set name` and `+set maxclients` already beat any archived value. Only autoexec.cfg runs later, and it sets none of name, deathmatch, maxclients, hostname or rcon_password. Behaviour is unchanged (`+name` is kept as belt-and-braces); the notes are corrected.

'Every box's players\blade\config.cfg archives maxclients 1' is false. Only .124 has a players\blade\config.cfg. The host .123, and .133/.143/.240, hold only save\; .110 and .186 have no players dir; .171 and .184 have an empty blade dir. This is harmless. sin.exe confirms that deathmatch turns maxclients <= 1 into 8 (SV_InitGame 0x463c3f, cap 256), so 16 is valid. SERVERS-fleet.txt's listen example (`+set maxclients 8`) would refuse 2 of 10 boxes.

'.110 and .184 have never run SiN' is false for .184. The machine at .184 today (NSC-CABE14B7486, P3 845, GeForce2 GTS) answered at .124 on 2026-08-30/31 (fleet inventory, git 4f3ed03). The compat/perbox '.124' SiN frame (1024x768 HARDCORPS logon) is that machine, and .184's own tree corroborates it: base\fleetres.cfg written by the launcher 2026-08-31 16:47:42, players\blade created 16:47:44. Likewise, 'rendered on .124 back when it had a GeForce2' describes a different computer. Today's .124 (NSC-C543575F526) is proven instead by the 2026-09-29 vcr-kmd sweep (Play SiN Gold.bat PASS at 1280x960) and its 2026-10-03 config.cfg.

'That launcher rendered fullscreen on .133 and .171 in 2026-08-31 frames' is false. .133's frame shows the desktop with a BF1942 'Cannot locate the CD-ROM' dialog, not SiN. Its own 2026-08-30 qconsole.log (downloaded today and saved) does prove GL init plus a map load on the GF4 Ti. .171's frame is 800x600 noise, taken on its old Intel 82865G. .240's 2026-08-31 join and frame were on a Radeon 9800 XT (qconsole_240.log). So the boxes whose current GPU has never run SiN are .110, .171 (FX 5500, ForceWare 175.19) and .240 (X1950 Pro), not .110 and .184. first_run, risks and the fallback-host note now say so.

.243's drop risk was named but not mitigated. SiN's server timeout cvar defaults to '125' (in sin.exe), so a client whose map load takes longer than 125 s is dropped. Added `+set timeout 300` to the host (early buffer; autoexec does not touch it). Raised load_wait_sec from 120 to 240 so the check pass does not run before the P166 can be in.

log_how wrongly says that 'Rcon from 192.168.1.132:' is followed by the status table in qconsole.log. While answering an rcon, SiN's Com_Printf appends to the redirect buffer and returns before reaching the console or logfile (0x425495-0x42551c). The log shows the rcon command text, and the table reaches only the requester.

'No server ... and none is possible' is overstated. SiN has a Windows dedicated mode (`+set dedicated 1`, the tree's ds_deathmatch.bat). This host already runs Windows server binaries under Wine (Descent 3, Deus Ex, DOOM 3, Far Cry, both Serious Sams, Shogo, UT2003, Unreal Gold) plus a hosting client for Carmageddon 2, and Hyperion shipped a Linux SiN port. peer_box_host is still right for THIS round: no SiN unit exists, and a read-only run may not add one. The blocker now says 'none today, untried'.

The recipe did not state two lanparty integration gaps. DEFAULT_BOXES omits .186 and .243 (and still lists the powered-off .145 and .197), so the title entry must carry an explicit boxes list or those two never get launchers. The host's default wait is 30 s, so the host entry needs wait 45.

.243's launcher ended silently (goto end) when Glide or the tree was missing, leaving only an absent Fleet243. It now writes C:\fleetmp\SINLAN.ERR with the reason. Re-rendered through lanparty.render_bat: longest line 114, start line still 106 (under 127), ASCII only, no parentheses.

ThiefGold.mp_summary: Thief Gold has no multiplayer. The staged THIEF.EXE is the vanilla Dark engine, version 1.37 (md5 8dd515df75176bcd1caaf65a93f47d81, linked 1999-09-24). It imports only KERNEL32, USER32, GDI32, WINMM, ole32 and ADVAPI32; ddraw, dinput and dsound are loaded at run time. It has no winsock import and no DirectPlay strings; 'NetPlayer' and 'net_abstract_player' are engine leftovers. intrface.crf does carry NETPLAY.STR ('Host a Game', 'Join a Game') at its root, but the exe never names it, and english/MAIN.STR offers only New Game, Load Game, Options, Credits, Intro and Quit. docs/staged-title-server-matrix.md row 40 says 'no multiplayer'. None of the 27 SERVERS in scripts/game-servers/gameservers.py is a Thief server, and there is no matching ~/.config/systemd/user unit or docker container. So there is no shared game. The round is a single-player fullscreen render check run in parallel on the 8 XP boxes. The results list should record multiplayer as 'n/a - no multiplayer', not leave compat's 'untested'. BEFORE LAUNCHING, arm a 6-hour PXE hold for every applicable box not in pxe_config.json never_offer (see risks). Steps: (1) Launch C:\fleetmp\ThiefGold.bat, which calls the staged 'Play Thief Gold.bat'. (2) At 30 s, take a frame and read WINLIST, PROCLIST and DISPLAYCFG get. Expect the intro movie, THIEF.EXE in the foreground, and 640x480 at 16 bpp. (3) Only if that frame shows the movie, press UIKEY ESCAPE once, then take a frame of the six-button main menu. If ESC does not skip it, wait; the menu appears by itself about 135-150 s after launch. (4) Optional: the in-mission 3D check in first_run. (5) Quit with ONE UICLICK 398 420 on the main menu, then a frame plus PROCLIST. If THIEF.EXE is still running, PROCKILL it and do not click again. Then DISPLAYCFG get must read the box's own mode. The resolution is 640x480x16 fullscreen on every box. The tree has no FLEETRES, and gameres.h lists ThiefGold in gr_incapable. Live checks 2026-11-11: all 9 deployed trees match the library (root file sizes, the 24 movies, and md5 of CAM.CFG, USER.CFG, DARK.BND, install.cfg and the Play bat). No box is running THIEF.EXE. Every box has Indeo 5 (ir50_32.dll plus Drivers32 vidc.iv50), which the IV50 intro needs. The intro plays at EVERY launch: THIEF.EXE sets skip_intro only in its in-memory config table after the first play (0x515dc2, then 0x54a0f0, then 0x549540; no file write), so a fresh process always plays it.

excluded_boxes.reason: Not counted. Windows 7 RTM 32-bit (OSArchitecture=32-bit, 6.1.7600, no SP) runs its GeForce GTX 1650 (10DE:1F82, TU117) on the Standard VGA fallback (display.inf, service vga; DRIVERS STATUS 'generic'), so there is no Direct3D HAL. No driver can fix that on this install: NVIDIA's last driver branch for 32-bit Windows is R390, and the GTX 1650 needs R430 or later. .186 can only get Direct3D from a 64-bit Windows reinstall or a different card. Thief Gold's software renderer needs an exclusive 8 bpp mode; its software list is 400x300 to 800x600, all at 8 bpp. Whether the Win7 VGA fallback offers 8 bpp is unknown, because GAMERES lists only modes of 16 bpp or more (agent/src/gameres.c:124,143). The tree, the 24 movies, Indeo 5 and the shortcut are all present. This machine has never run the title. It is not the old ADMIN-PC that passed as .246 on 08-31: that was an i5-2400 with a Radeon HD 5450, MAC 78-2B-CB-A5-B4-70, now at .197. This one is an E5300, MAC E0-CB-4E-26-EC-A0, Windows installed 2026-10-26. At most, run it as an uncounted best-effort software-renderer probe.

Not deployed and has no shortcut, by operator override: 'not wanted on .243: the user kept Quake/Quake II/UT, flight sims and 3D-noteworthy titles only (2026-09-29)'. The override line is scripts/gamegate/overrides.txt:65, keyed on the old hash d931bfe6c33fae5e. It reaches today's hash b9a3b8c66827032c through line 19 (@follows). The published /mnt/retro-share/Files/Games-Library/_gamegate/b9a3b8c66827032c.txt says 'no ThiefGold ... [override]'. The override is the reason. Disk space is not: GamesDir E: has 64,204 MB free against the title's 860 MB disk_mb. The P166 (165 MHz) sits under the title's 200 MHz floor, in the gate's marginal band. Whether the Voodoo 2's Win9x Direct3D driver could carry Thief's DX6 renderer has never been tested; the override makes that moot.

launchers.bat:
@echo off
rem Thief Gold - single-player fullscreen render check; the title has no multiplayer.
rem The tree has no FLEETRES: vanilla Dark 1.37 opens 640x480x16 fullscreen by itself.
rem The Play bat is the shortcut's own launcher: cd /d to the tree, start thief.exe, exit.
rem Its exit also ends this console, so nothing may follow this call.
call "C:\Games\ThiefGold\Play Thief Gold.bat"
launchers.notes: No {name} or {host}: Thief has no player name and nothing to connect to. 'Play Thief Gold.bat' exists in the library (checked case-insensitively), md5 6a840fd7b395bf9b07c6fdc94a690193, identical on all 9 boxes. Its lines are: cd /d "%~dp0", start "" thief.exe, exit. That exit ends this console as well, so nothing may follow the call. %~dp0 resolves from the absolute path given to call. The same shape (cd /d plus call of this bat, wrapper C:\RETRO_AGENT\lansweep.bat) started THIEF.EXE on .124 in the 2026-11-08 lan_sweep. The 08-31 perbox sweep launched this bat on .123, .124, .133, .143, .171, .240 and the old ADMIN-PC .246: 640x480x16 fullscreen every time, at 100 Hz on .143. There is deliberately no FLEETRES call. The tree has none (checked case-insensitively), and stage-fleetres.py puts a FLEETRES call, with its per-title arguments, inside the title's own launcher, so a wrapper-level call could only be a no-op or an argument-less duplicate. This is the same call-the-title's-launcher shape as lanparty's ssam-tfe and ut2004 entries. Fullscreen is the engine default: the default ScrnMode is 640x480 with screen_flags 13 (hardware bit set), at 16 bpp under Direct3D. The bat is plain ASCII with no parentheses; lanparty.render_bat makes it CRLF.

first_run.symptom: The intro movie MOVIES\INTRO.AVI plays at EVERY launch: Indeo 5 (IV50), 320x240 shown at 640x480, 1930 frames at 15 fps = 128.7 s. The deployed CAM.CFG has no skip_intro, and the engine sets skip_intro only in memory after playing it. On .124 on 11-08 the 30 s frame read 'LEST YE BE STRUCK DOWN...' and the 60 s frame still showed the movie.
first_run.keys: Take the 30 s frame first. Send UIKEY ESCAPE once, and only if (a) that frame shows the movie, not the six-button menu, and (b) WINLIST foreground is class LookingGlassTechnologies_WindowsGameShell_v2 with title 'Thief  1.37 ' (two spaces) and pid = THIEF.EXE. Then take a frame.
first_run.notes: Whether ESC skips the movie is unverified on this fleet. The 11-08 sweep pressed no key before 60 s and was still in the intro. If ESC does not skip it, do NOT click to skip. (320,240) is inside the main menu's New Game button (MAINR.BIN rect 0 = 165-473 x 219-255), so a click that lands after the movie ends opens New Game. Just wait: the menu appears by itself about 135-150 s after launch. Send ESC once only, because what ESC does at the main menu is unknown.

first_run.symptom: Main menu: six buttons. New Game, Load Game, Options and Credits are stacked; Intro and Quit sit side by side on the bottom row. This is the end state of the basic render check. Nothing else is expected to be modal: no CD prompt, no key, no config wizard (no dialog appeared in the 08-31 or 11-08 runs).
first_run.keys: Clean exit: ONE UICLICK 398 420 (Quit), then a frame plus PROCLIST. If THIEF.EXE is still running, PROCKILL it. Never click a second time.
first_run.notes: The coordinates are 640x480 screen pixels from the game's own MAINR.BIN in intrface.crf, read in natural order because DARK.CFG has no rect_main and MAIN.STR lists the six buttons in that order. UICLICK is SetCursorPos plus mouse_event with no motion (agent/src/input.c:164-166). Whether vanilla 1.37's menu follows the OS cursor at 640x480 is unverified. If it does not, a click lands where the game's own cursor is: at the screen centre that is New Game, and a repeat click on the New Game panel hits Start Training, which loads a mission. Hence one click, then a frame. Do not open Options, because leaving it through Done can write the box's config. If a click lands in Options, PROCKILL instead of leaving it.

first_run.symptom: Optional in-mission 3D check: New Game panel, then a briefing movie if any, then the loadout screen, then the mission.
first_run.keys: UICLICK 319 237 (New Game), then a frame. UICLICK 215 177 (Normal, already the default). UICLICK 338 236 (Start Training; Skip Training is 338 291), then a frame. After that, take a frame every ~10 s. If a movie is showing (a B*.AVI briefing, 97-135 s): UIKEY ESCAPE. If the loadout screen's three item columns are showing: UICLICK 534 456 (Play Mission). Then wait 30-90 s for the level; .133 and .184 take longest.
first_run.notes: UNVERIFIED path. The coordinates come from NEWGAMER.BIN and LOADOUTR.BIN plus DARK.CFG rect_newgame 4,5,6,7,0,1,2,3 and rect_loadout 8,13,9,12,6,3,4,5,0,1,2,7,10,11, applied as rects[i]=file[order[i]]. That reading lines up with NEWGAME.STR and LOADOUT.STR. If the frame after a click shows the panel unchanged, the cursor is not following the OS cursor: stop clicking and PROCKILL. Mission start writes C:\Games\ThiefGold\startmis.sav, which is the proof; today only .143 has one, dated 2026-08-29 17:17. The file stays on the box afterwards, harmlessly, because GAMESYNC never deletes.

first_run.symptom: Thief ignores WM_CLOSE and ALT+F4. On .124 on 11-08, lan_sweep sent WM_CLOSE, then ALT+F4 (while focused), then TILDE/quit/RETURN during the intro, and had to taskkill /f it. docs/v56k-benchmark-plan.md lists both Thiefs as ignoring WM_CLOSE and force-closed.
first_run.keys: Main menu: one UICLICK 398 420. In mission: UIKEY ESCAPE opens the sim menu (DARK.BND binds ESC to sim_menu). Quit is probably bottom-left at 205 389 and Continue bottom-right at 446 389 (SIMR.BIN with rect_sim; unverified). Otherwise PROCKILL THIEF.EXE.
first_run.notes: After any kill, require DISPLAYCFG get to equal the box's own mode; get reads the live mode (ENUM_CURRENT_SETTINGS, agent/src/display.c:26). The 11-08 sweep always got 1280x1024x32@85 back on .124. Kill THIEF.EXE by PID or by quoted name.

first_run.symptom: 'Missing CD! / Please insert Thief CD #2', or the free-disk-space dialog. NOT expected.
first_run.keys: UIKEY RETURN dismisses it, but treat it as a defect.
first_run.notes: CAM.CFG has skip_starting_checks, install.cfg has cd_path .\, and thief\convict.osm (1,194,340 B) is present on all 9 boxes today. If the dialog appears, the tree has lost one of these. Fix it with GAMESYNC, not with clicks.

first_run.symptom: A message box before the intro: 'DirectSound is not installed. You will not be able to hear any sound or music while playing Thief ... Continue Anyway?' It is a THIEF.EXE startup check. NOT expected.
first_run.keys: Take a frame and read WINLIST, and record it as a defect. It is a Yes/No box; answer Yes only if the render check should still continue.
first_run.notes: Every applicable box has a working wave-out device today: .110 and .171 SoundMAX, .123 Realtek AC97, .124 nForce, .133 and .240 SB Live!, .143 VIA, .184 AWE64. A box that shows this box has lost its sound driver, which is a driver-audit finding rather than a Thief one. The sibling 'DirectX version 6 or higher is not installed' box cannot appear on XP SP3, which has DirectX 9.

ThiefGold.in_game_proof: There is no server roster, so the proof is per box, in increasing strength. (1) WINLIST foreground is class 'LookingGlassTechnologies_WindowsGameShell_v2', title 'Thief  1.37 ' (two spaces), and its pid is THIEF.EXE in PROCLIST; this exact class and title were recorded on .124 on 11-08. (2) DISPLAYCFG get while the game runs reads 640x480 at 16 bpp. get reports the LIVE mode (ENUM_CURRENT_SETTINGS), so this shows the box has left its own desktop mode (1600x1200, 1280x1024, 1024x768 or 1920x1080 today), i.e. exclusive fullscreen. The 08-31 perbox sweep measured 640x480x16 on every box, at 100 Hz on .143. (3) A frame of the game's own content: the intro movie at ~30 s, then, after one ESC, the six-button main menu. (4) Strongest, optional: an in-mission 3D frame plus a DIRLIST of C:\Games\ThiefGold showing startmis.sav with an mtime inside the round. The engine writes it at mission start; before the round only .143 has one, dated 2026-08-29 17:17. A running THIEF.EXE alone is not proof. Nor is the intro alone proof of the 3D path: the 1080p review found that the 08-31 'verified' rows are intro-movie frames.
ThiefGold.screenshot_notes: The hardware mode is 640x480 at 16 bpp, so XP GDI SCREENSHOT gives correct colours. The 08-31 perbox sweep captured the intro on .123, .124, .133, .143, .171, .240 and .246. lan_sweep's SCREENSHOT 0 captured it on .124 under vcr-kmd on 11-08 (voodoo-cleanroom/vcr-kmd/evidence/d3dtune_1014/sweep_1108_fixed/20261108_020841/Thief_Gold_30s.png and Thief_Gold_60s.png). lanparty.py's check uses SCREENSHOT 1 everywhere except .124, where it uses vcrctl fbshot. For an in-mission Direct3D frame on .124: EXECW 30 C:\vcr\vcrctl.exe fbshot C:\fleetmp\fb.bmp, then DOWNLOAD it (vcrctl.exe is present, 326,480 B). If that never finishes, as happened with Max Payne, fall back to SCREENSHOT 0. The staged DARK.BND carries a 2026-08-29 note that SCREENSHOT captured a fullscreen Dark engine frame as black. Both plain F10 (vanilla) and CTRL+F11 (fleet) are bound to screen_dump. It writes dump000.pcx (then dump001.pcx and so on) in C:\Games\ThiefGold, and only in mission, where binds apply. Plain F11 is quick_save, so a CTRL+F11 whose CTRL does not register writes a quicksave instead. Send it only while the game has focus, DOWNLOAD the new .pcx, then DELETE it, because GAMESYNC never deletes files. Frames are 640x480 on every box, even on the 1080p .240, whose monitor stretches or pillarboxes them. If a box ever falls back to the software renderer it runs at 8 bpp, and GDI colours would be wrong while the geometry stays right.
known_blockers: Thief Gold has no multiplayer of any kind (single-player Dark engine 1.37; staged-title-server-matrix row 40; no Thief server among the 27 host SERVERS). A shared-game round is impossible, so this title is a per-box single-player render check, and its multiplayer result is 'n/a'.

.186 has no Direct3D: Windows 7 RTM 32-bit on the Standard VGA fallback. No 32-bit Windows driver exists for its GTX 1650 (NVIDIA's 32-bit drivers end at R390; Turing needs R430 or later). It needs a 64-bit reinstall or a different card before it can join.

.243 does not get the title, by operator override: scripts/gamegate/overrides.txt:65, carried to today's hash b9a3b8c66827032c by line 19 (@follows); published _gamegate/b9a3b8c66827032c.txt says 'no ThiefGold'.
risks: PXE reimage on an unplanned reboot. A bugcheck auto-reboot bypasses safe-reboot.py, fleet boxes boot from the network first, and only .110 and .186 are in scripts/pxe/pxe_config.json never_offer. Before the round, arm a 6-hour hold (boot_hold_seconds 21600) for each other box: python3 scripts/pxe/pxe_server.py --arm <MAC>. MACs: .123 00:13:d4:a4:a4:13, .124 00:d0:b7:40:96:a9, .133 00:0c:41:e8:4f:ce, .143 00:08:a1:03:52:c4, .171 00:13:20:7b:2d:45, .184 08:00:09:eb:d1:a5, .240 00:11:2f:e4:77:f5.

.143 (GeForce 6800 on ForceWare 71.89, driver 7.1.8.9) had nine nv4_disp-involved 0xEA THREAD_STUCK_IN_DEVICE_DRIVER bugchecks between 08-20 and 08-31, eight of them in Unreal.exe (audit-143/minidump-summary.txt; none since in that folder). Thief Gold has reached a mission on .143 before (startmis.sav, 08-29 17:17). A hang during the in-mission step there points at that driver first.

.124 (V5 6000 on vcr-kmd): only the intro has been seen there (11-08 sweep; agent alive, board healthy, desktop restored after the kill). Thief Gold's in-mission DX6 Direct3D on our HAL has never been seen (stage-fleetres.py newdark_display_swap docstring). Thief II's NewDark DX6 path did play in mission on vcr-kmd on 2026-09-28, which is encouraging. The HAL has stalled other games. D3D32=1 and D3DBigTex=7 are armed today (vcrmp Diag); Thief Gold renders at 16 bpp. It needs one mode switch in and one out on the 1998 CRT, so do not relaunch it rapidly.

.133 is a dual Pentium III, the only multi-CPU applicable box; .110 and .171 report one processor. The pre-NewDark Dark engine is widely reported as unstable on multi-processor systems, and the community fix is single-CPU affinity or NewDark. This is unverified here. XP's start command has no /affinity switch, and only the intro was ever seen on .133 (08-31). A hang at mission load there is more likely this than a driver fault.
The game ignores WM_CLOSE and ALT+F4. Quit from the main menu (one click at 398,420) or PROCKILL, then confirm DISPLAYCFG get on each box. A game left running strands the desktop at 640x480x16.

Every menu click is unverified. The coordinates come from the game's own rect files, and vanilla 1.37's cursor mapping at 640x480 is unknown. The recipe this replaces said NewDark Thief II on .145 follows the absolute OS cursor; no source for that was found in docs/ or the evidence. If the game's cursor ignores the OS cursor, each click lands where the game's cursor already is: New Game on the main menu, then Start Training on the next panel. One click, then a frame; on any surprise, PROCKILL.

Resolution is 640x480 on every box. There is no FLEETRES, gameres.h lists the title in gr_incapable, and PER-TITLE-STATUS marks it 'incapable', so 640x480 is not a test failure. The library could do better, but that is out of scope: verify-dark-sith.json found that vanilla does read game_screen_size, with 1024x768x16 as the largest mode in its hardware list.

.110 (GeForce 7800 GS) and .184 (GeForce2 GTS, P3-845) have never been seen running this title; their compat cells are 'untested'. Their trees, movies and codecs match the passing boxes, so expect a pass. On first launch THIEF.EXE registers its own DirectShow filter (LGVID.AX, CLSID {9f711c60-0668-11d0-94d4-0000c02ba972}), so no install.reg is needed.
.240's card has changed since its 08-31 pass: it had a Radeon X1600 on 10-03 and has a Radeon X1950 Pro today. Expect the same result.
Opening Options and leaving through Done can make the Dark engine write the box's config, so keep the round out of Options.

Optional: the same launcher could be tried on .186 as an uncounted best-effort software-renderer probe. It may show a 'video hardware not supported' dialog or a black screen.
