Turok2.mp_summary:
There is no Turok 2 server on 192.168.1.132: no row among the 27 in gameservers.py SERVERS (its 't2' probe is Tribes 2), no unit, nothing bound on UDP 12800-12888, and no standalone Turok 2 GameManager or RTIME package on the share (case-insensitive search). So one fleet box hosts the in-process Integrated Server and also plays: a GameManager answering queries on UDP 12888 plus an RTIME server on 12800-12806. Hosting has worked twice (.171 on 2026-08-31, .124 on 2026-09-28; integrated.log reads 'Accepting queries @ ---------> <ip>:12888 ... Startup successful'), both times on Glide. No switch sets the host flag 0xb6a474 (-Server only sets 0xb6a468, which the net-open routine never reads), so hosting needs the launcher menu: LAN > HOST A GAME > OK > START GAME.

Why the recorded join failed, verified in Turok2MPEnglish.exe: the switch parser splits lpCmdLine on single spaces, so '+connect X' takes X verbatim, quote marks included, and only writes 'connect X' into gspylite.cfg. GetGameConfiguration (0x4d61b0) and GetPermission (0x4d5dc0) split that string at ':'. With no port, the host buffer is never filled and the port stays 0. .184's attempt used :12806, RTIME's beacon port, and timed out. The GameManager answers gm_configuration and gm_permission on its query socket, port 12888. That is also the default of the exe's own INTERNET > JOIN AT IP dialog (0x4bea66 reads turok2.ini [Player] IPAddress/Port, default 0x3258 = 12888, and writes 'connect %s:%d'). The staged gspylite.cfg 'connect 202.72.177.79:12888' matches the staged [Player] IPAddress/Port, so that path wrote it, not GameSpy Lite. The integrated server's ServerIP is '(local)', so the GameManager leaves \ServerIP\ out of its reply, and the client then uses the connect host as the RTIME address (0x4d70dd). ip:12888 is therefore all a joiner needs.

So joiners run '+connect <host>:12888' with no quotes. The launcher contacts the GameManager and stops on its INTERNETSTARTGAME page with only JOIN GAME enabled, and one click on JOIN GAME is needed: the menu ignores WM_KEYDOWN, but absolute clicks work. A fallback with the same effect: INTERNET > JOIN AT IP > RETURN (the joiner bat prefills the dialog) > JOIN GAME. D3D boxes show a 'Direct3D Properties' dialog (OK is the default and does not validate the card), and .143 also shows '3Dfx hardware not detected!'. The player name comes from turok2.ini [Player] Names, because the NAME box overwrites +name at JOIN/START, so each launcher writes Fleet<octet> there. The host's MaxPlayers must go from 4 to 16: the Host a Game list offers 2-16, and the GameManager accepts 2-32.

Plan: .110 hosts and 8 boxes play one Rok Match. lanparty.py cannot click, so bring the host up by hand and confirm \status\ on 192.168.1.110:12888. Then launch the joiners (lanparty.py run Turok2 --no-host) and click JOIN GAME on each. Proof is the GameManager's \status\ player list, read from the dev host. A join has never succeeded end to end here, so smoke-test the host plus one joiner first.

excluded_boxes.reason: No display driver. This Windows 7 box's NVIDIA card (PCI 10DE:1F82) runs on the 'Standard VGA Graphics Adapter' stub: DRIVERS STATUS calls it 'generic', and VIDEODIAG shows display.inf. Turok 2 has no software renderer (the tree ships only Video_D3D.dll = T2-Direct3D6 and Video_3DFx.dll = T2-Glide3), and with no D3D HAL the exe stops at 'No 3D-accelerated hardware cards or drivers found'. Its 3 shortcuts exist only because the gate classifies the card by PCI id as sm3.0.

host_box.command: Upload the host launcher as C:\fleetmp\Turok2-host.bat (lanparty.py names a host launcher <game>-host.bat) and LAUNCH "C:\fleetmp\Turok2-host.bat". Then: (0) UIKEY SHIFT first. ssstars.scr was the foreground window on .110 when read on 2026-11-11, and ScreenSaverIsSecure=0. (1) Wait until WINLIST shows TurokWinClass titled 'Turok 2 Game Launcher  v1.04  (T2-Direct3D6 v1.0)' and a SCREENSHOT shows the INTERNET / LAN / OPTIONS / QUIT menu. The launcher shows a logo splash first, and its title has no renderer suffix until the video driver is chosen. If the WINLIST foreground is 'Direct3D Properties', UIKEY RETURN. (2) From the TurokWinClass rect: cx = left + (right-left-632)/2, cy = bottom - (right-left-632)/2 - 453. The client area is 632x453, from AdjustWindowRect of WS_CAPTION|WS_SYSMENU|WS_MINIMIZEBOX. (3) UICLICK (cx+316, cy+240) = LAN. Wait 2 s, and SCREENSHOT to confirm FIND A GAME / HOST A GAME. (4) UICLICK (cx+316, cy+240) = HOST A GAME. (5) In 'Host a Game' (dialog 124), confirm Max Players shows 16, then UIKEY RETURN (OK is the default push button). On the LAN path no 'limit an Internet game to 4 players' notice follows. (6) UICLICK (cx+315, cy+365) = START GAME. On .110's 1600x1200 desktop the window is created at (480,370), so the clicks are LAN (799,639), HOST A GAME (799,639) and START GAME (798,764). The host is ready when integrated.log shows 'Accepting queries @ ---------> 192.168.1.110:12888' and 'Startup successful', or when UDP \status\ to 192.168.1.110:12888 answers hostname 'NSC Retro Fleet'.
host_box.notes: Why .110: P4 2.8 GHz, 1150 MB, NVIDIA GeForce 7800 GS on the D3D path, 224 GB free, and one NIC, so the GameManager binds 192.168.1.110. RT_Logsrv.txt grew to 338 MB in about 10 minutes of hosting on .171. Alternate host: .123 (Athlon 64 4000+, 2 GB, HD 3850, 180 GB free, one NIC). Avoid as host: .124 (T2-Glide3 access violation 63 s into a hosted game), .240 (8.8 GB free), .133/.184 (P3 700/845), .143 (extra error dialog every launch). The host plays inside the server's own process. lanparty.py run would upload and LAUNCH the host bat, then only sleep host.wait seconds. It never clicks. So do the host UI steps first, then run 'lanparty.py run Turok2 --no-host'. The title entry needs host.box=110 and query ['gamespy', 12888]; roster() then queries the host box with no code change.

server.unit: none: the Integrated Server (GameManager + RTIME server) runs inside Turok2MPEnglish.exe on the host box 192.168.1.110
server.query_kind: GameSpy v1 '\status\' or '\players\' on the GameManager query port. The same socket and dispatcher (command table basic/info/rules/players/status/echo/gm_permission/gm_configuration/secure) serve gm_configuration and gm_permission.
server.roster_how: From the dev host, send UDP '\status\' to 192.168.1.110:12888 and read several datagrams. The reply has hostname 'NSC Retro Fleet', numplayers, maxplayers and, for each player, \player_<i>\<name>\frags_<i>\..\deaths_<i>\..\skill_<i>\..\ping_<i>\..\color_<i>\..\character_<i>\..\team_<i>\.. (format string in the exe). lanparty.py roster()'s GameSpy branch parses this as is, and the worktree version already sends the query to the host box when the title entry has host.box. Names are Fleet<octet> because each launcher writes turok2.ini [Player] Names. The host is listed too. Remote queries are answered: .124's GameSpy Lite browse listed the .171 host on 2026-08-31.
server.log_how: Logs are files on the host box; there is no journal or docker log. C:\Games\Turok2\integrated.log has 'Accepting queries @ ---------> 192.168.1.110:12888 (...)' and 'Startup successful.  Game: "NSC Retro Fleet".  Mode: "Rok Match".'. C:\Games\Turok2\RT_Logsrv.txt has one line per client, 'New client (ip <a.b.c.d>) assigned id N, connected on socket id M!'; the host's own in-process client shows as ip 0.0.0.0. A remote client's line has never been seen yet, because no join has succeeded. Read it with EXECW 120 cmd /c findstr /c:"New client" C:\Games\Turok2\RT_Logsrv.txt; never DOWNLOAD it whole, since it grows by tens of MB per minute. On each joiner, read C:\Games\Turok2\connect_log.txt.
server.bots_note: Turok 2 multiplayer has no bots (no bot strings in the exe), so every roster entry is a real box. RTIME supports up to 30 sockets.
server.changes_needed: Staged MaxPlayers is 4 in integrated.cfg and in turok2.ini [Config]. The host launcher raises both to 16 with FLEETRES.EXE -ini. The Host a Game dialog lists 2-16, reads turok2.ini [Config], and rewrites ./integrated.cfg itself on OK; the GameManager accepts 2-32. Later, in the library (not done now): MaxPlayers=16 in both files, and fix 'Join Turok 2 - LAN.bat' to use +connect %HOSTIP%:12888 unquoted and to write [Player] Names.

Turok2.in_game_proof:
Primary: the host's own player list, read from the dev host. Send UDP '\status\' (or '\players\') to 192.168.1.110:12888. The in-process GameManager replies GameSpy-v1 style with hostname 'NSC Retro Fleet', numplayers, maxplayers and one \player_<i>\Fleet<octet>\frags_<i>\..\ping_<i>\.. entry per player, the host included. A box counts only when its Fleet<octet> is listed. lanparty.py roster()'s GameSpy branch parses this as is when the title entry names host.box 110.

Per-box witness: DOWNLOAD C:\Games\Turok2\connect_log.txt on each joiner. It is truncated every run and is about 1 KB. It must contain 'Getting permission from GameManager (192.168.1.110:12888).', 'Connected to RTime server.', 'Net is open.' and 'Loading level <n>.' (the server's current level index, 0 only at the start of the rotation). 'Address = 192.168.1.110.' in the configuration block confirms the RTIME address fallback. A crash shows up in C:\Games\Turok2\errorlog.txt.

Host-side witness: RT_Logsrv.txt lines 'New client (ip 192.168.1.<octet>) assigned id N ...' (read with findstr, never DOWNLOAD the whole file). A running Turok2MPEnglish.exe proves nothing: the windowed launcher alone keeps that process alive, and the .124 sweeps' 'PASS' was only the launcher menu.

known_blockers: The staged 'Join Turok 2 - LAN.bat' can never join. It passes +connect "%HOSTIP%" with no port. GetGameConfiguration (0x4d61b0) and GetPermission (0x4d5dc0) copy the host and read the port (%hd) only after a ':', so the port stays 0 and the host is unset. It also wraps the address in quotes, which the exe keeps because its parser splits the raw lpCmdLine on spaces and sscanf %s takes the token verbatim. Use the fleetmp joiner (+connect <host>:12888, no quotes). The library fix is pending and was not made.

No command-line switch starts hosting. The host flag (0xb6a474) is set only by the LAN/INTERNET > HOST A GAME handlers (0x4beb65/0x4be7e9), so the host needs 4 UI steps: LAN, HOST A GAME, OK, START GAME. A '-Server' switch exists, but it only sets 0xb6a468, which the net-open routine (0x481eb0) never reads, so do not try it.

After +connect the launcher stops on its INTERNETSTARTGAME page, and JOIN GAME must be clicked once per box. -SkipConfig would skip that click, but it also skips GetPermission and the copy of the server's level set (0xb6a2dc into 0xb69c74), so the client would load 'Seeds of Evil.lss'. -LevelSet and -DatFile cannot replace it, because the space-split parser cuts 'Rok Match Levels.lsm' at the spaces.
lanparty.py run cannot do the host's 4 UI steps or the joiners' JOIN GAME click. The round is driven by hand or by a small UICLICK script around lanparty.py run --no-host.

The single-player exe (Turok2English.exe) is CD-blocked on every box, and there is no Turok 2 disc image on the share (case-insensitive search, depth 5: only the installed rar and two demos). .123 showed 'No CDROM Drive Found!' and .143 an Error box on 2026-08-31. There is no host-side server: nothing on 192.168.1.132, and no standalone Turok 2 GameManager or RTIME package on the share.
risks: A join has never succeeded on this fleet. The +connect host:12888 fix comes from the binary (the parser, both gspylite.cfg readers, the JOIN AT IP default of 12888, and the RTIME address fallback) plus .184's log, not from a test. Smoke-test the host and one joiner before launching all 8.

Joiners reached through +connect (or JOIN AT IP) land on the INTERNET page. JOIN there calls GetPermission with LAN=0, so they run as Internet clients against a LAN-hosted game. This is the game's own join-by-IP design, but it is untested here.

review_issues: (evidence, minor) The recipe attributes the staged gspylite.cfg 'connect 202.72.177.79:12888' to GameSpy Lite. It actually matches turok2.ini [Player] IPAddress=202.72.177.79 / Port=12888, which is what the exe's own INTERNET > JOIN AT IP handler (0x4bea66) writes: it reads [Player] IPAddress/Port, default Port 0x3258 = 12888, and fprintfs 'connect %s:%d'. The 12888 conclusion stands and is stronger. The recipe also missed this documented join-by-IP path as a fallback; it is added now, and the joiner bat prefills [Player] IPAddress/Port so the fallback is INTERNET > JOIN AT IP > RETURN > JOIN GAME.

(procedure) host_box.command names the host launcher C:\fleetmp\Turok2.bat, but lanparty.py launch_bat() uploads a host launcher as C:\fleetmp\<game>-host.bat (Turok2-host.bat). lanparty.py run also cannot do the 4 host UI steps or the per-joiner JOIN GAME click; it only sleeps host.wait, so joiners launched by 'run' would hit 'Unable to contact the GameManager'. The note that roster() needs its _udp() retargeted is outdated: the worktree lanparty.py already queries host_ip_of(t) when the title has host.box.
(syntax) 'PROCKILL Turok2MPEnglish.exe' is invalid because PROCKILL takes a PID. Use PROCLIST, then PROCKILL <pid>, as lanparty.py kill_games does.

NOT A DEFECT, verified unchanged against primary sources. Every launcher path exists in Games-Library/Turok2 (case-insensitive). FLEETRES.EXE has -ini (WritePrivateProfileStringA) and -setline. The bats are valid cmd: carets only inside quotes, no parentheses. The exe's parser splits lpCmdLine on single spaces and keeps quote marks, and +connect only writes gspylite.cfg. GetGameConfiguration and GetPermission parse ':port' with the port defaulting to 0. 12806 is RTIME's beacon port; 12888 is the GameManager query socket, and its dispatcher serves gm_configuration, gm_permission and status. Host a Game Max Players offers 2-16 and OK is its default button; the GameManager accepts 2-32. The NAME box overwrites +name from turok2.ini [Player] Names. UnrealGold.mp_summary:
Host server: unit unrealgold-server on 192.168.1.132. It runs the staged tree's own Unreal 226 System\UCC.exe under Wine in docker container 'ugsrv': join UDP 7807, GameSpy query 7808, LAN beacon 7775. Re-checked 2026-11-11 14:1x: 3/12 (3 bots, 0 humans), gamever 226, DMDeck16, timelimit 0 and fraglimit 0, so the map never changes mid-round. The server's System\*.u/*.dll/UCC.exe/Unreal.exe and Maps\DmDeck16.unr/Entry.unr are md5-identical to the library. Every applicable box's System packages and Maps\DmDeck16.unr (828303 B) match the library sizes. No client has joined this 226 server yet: server.log since 2026-09-28 has no Open or Join line.

Unreal 226 cannot join from the command line (retro-3dfx/FINDINGS.md 2026-08-31, item 2). .240's Unreal.log shows the pending connect to 192.168.1.132:7807 dropped when the intro map loads. So each round launcher writes three things into the box's own System\User.ini:
- Name=Fleet<octet>
- NetSpeed 20000 (the default 2600 is a modem rate)
- F9 = 'open <host>:7807?Name=Fleet<octet>'
It then starts the game through the title's own launcher (FLEETRES resolution; GlideDrv on .124 because GlideRender=1, D3DDrv elsewhere). The round presses UIKEY F9 once the intro is up. In 226's WindowConsole, F9 falls through to the key bindings both in the global state and in state UWindow ('case IK_F9: return Global.KeyEvent()'), so menu state does not matter. The intro never opens the menu by itself: the Intro class's HUDType is IntroNullHud, and the 7th-caption auto-ESC belongs to EndgameHud, the ending. The join is keyboard-only and automatable. The typed console 'open' is the measured fallback, and a User.ini 'open' binding pressed with UIKEY is what joined Deus Ex.

9 boxes apply:
- 7 XP boxes, .124 on Glide
- .243 through a COMMAND.COM Voodoo 2 variant, with User.ini patched by DOWNLOAD/UPLOAD
- .186 best effort on the software renderer: no 3D driver exists for its TU117 on 32-bit Win7, and Windows Firewall is ON there
.143 is excluded: Unreal.exe bugchecks that box (8 minidumps). 12 human slots against 9 boxes (11 if .145 and .197 come on); the 3 bots take no slots. No server change is needed.

launchers.bat:
@echo off
rem UnrealGold - fleet LAN round on the dev host's Unreal 226 server, port 7807.
rem 1 - this box's player name, net speed and the server join key go into its
rem     own System\User.ini.
rem 2 - the title's own launcher runs: FLEETRES resolution and render device
rem     for THIS box - GlideDrv on .124, D3DDrv elsewhere - Running.ini deleted,
rem     fullscreen, start, exit.
rem Unreal 226 cannot join from the command line: the intro map's load drops the
rem pending connection. The round presses F9 once the intro is up - F9 is the
rem one key 226's UWindow console hands to the key bindings even while its menu
rem is open. Without FLEETRES.EXE there is no join key, so do not start at all.
set UGR=C:\Games\UnrealGold
if not exist "%UGR%\System\Unreal.exe" exit
if not exist "%UGR%\FLEETRES.EXE" exit
"%UGR%\FLEETRES.EXE" -ini "%UGR%\System\User.ini" DefaultPlayer Name {name}
"%UGR%\FLEETRES.EXE" -ini "%UGR%\System\User.ini" Engine.PlayerPawn NetSpeed 20000
"%UGR%\FLEETRES.EXE" -ini "%UGR%\System\User.ini" Engine.Input F9 "open {host}:7807?Name={name}"
cd /d "%UGR%"
call "%UGR%\Play Unreal Gold.bat"
exit
launchers.notes:
Every file this calls was verified on every box at the library's size: 'Play Unreal Gold.bat' 3490 B, FLEETRES.EXE 33280 B (md5 equal to provisioning/fleetres/FLEETRES.EXE), FLEETRES.BAT 4917 B. FLEETRES.EXE -ini is WritePrivateProfileStringA(section, key, value, file) (fleetres.c main), and the open URL is one quoted argument. The staged Play bat ends with 'exit', so nothing may follow the call.

Result per box: the Play bat writes FR_UE1DEV into all three render-device keys.
- .124 (GlideRender=1, V5 6000 present) gets GlideDrv at the Glide 2 ladder mode, 1024x768, with RefreshRate from FR_HZ.
- Every other box gets D3DDrv at FR_W x FR_H. GAMERES today: .110 1600x1200; .123, .133, .171 1280x960; .184 1024x768; .240 1920x1080.

Changed from the draft: the game no longer starts when FLEETRES.EXE is missing. The draft started it with F9 still bound to Shot, a silent non-join.

Round steps:
1. MKDIR C:\fleetmp.
2. UPLOAD C:\fleetmp\UGOLD.BAT. Use this 8.3 name on every box: lanparty.py names the file after its key, and .243 needs 8.3.
3. LAUNCH "C:\fleetmp\UGOLD.BAT".
4. About 10 s later, DOWNLOAD C:\Games\UnrealGold\System\User.ini and confirm Name=Fleet<octet>, NetSpeed=20000 and F9=open 192.168.1.132:7807?Name=Fleet<octet> before any key is sent.
5. Wait until WINLIST shows foreground pid = Unreal.exe, then about 30-45 s more (60 s on .133 and .184). See first_run if the screensaver is still in the foreground.
6. UIKEY F9.

Cleanup: PROCKILL the Unreal.exe pid from PROCLIST. Then restore System\User.ini from the library copy (5528 B, md5 b532260a023c63d68eda60beb6887d8c, which all ten boxes hold today). Restoring is recommended, because the round's F9 no longer takes a screenshot.

launchers.bat:

rem the 4:3 mode FLEETRES picks under a 1024x768 cap. The title's own Play
rem launcher is not used because it writes D3DDrv, which has no hardware here.

"%UGR%\FLEETRES.EXE" -ini "%UGR%\System\Unreal.ini" Engine.Engine GameRenderDevice SoftDrv.SoftwareRenderDevice
"%UGR%\FLEETRES.EXE" -ini "%UGR%\System\Unreal.ini" Engine.Engine WindowedRenderDevice SoftDrv.SoftwareRenderDevice
"%UGR%\FLEETRES.EXE" -ini "%UGR%\System\Unreal.ini" Engine.Engine RenderDevice SoftDrv.SoftwareRenderDevice
"%UGR%\FLEETRES.EXE" -ini "%UGR%\System\Unreal.ini" WinDrv.WindowsClient FullscreenViewportX %FR_W43%

launchers.notes:
Best effort, untested in this hardware state. .186 is ADMIN-PC, 32-bit Win7 Pro RTM installed 2026-10-26, with a 1920x1080 desktop on 'Standard VGA Graphics Adapter'. The card is PCI 10DE:1F82 (TU117), which has no 32-bit Win7 driver. System\SoftDrv.dll (389120 B) is on the box. Upload as C:\fleetmp\UGOLD.BAT, like every box.

Resolution: with -cap 1024 768 on this panel, no 16:9 mode fits inside the cap, so FLEETRES makes the cap itself the target. FR_W43 x FR_H43 is then 1024x768, a mode in its driver's list (640x480, 800x600, 1024x768, 1280x1024, 1360x768, 1920x1080).

Firewall: Windows Firewall is ON. Standard, Public and Domain profiles all have EnableFirewall=1 with notifications on, and there is no rule for Unreal.exe (REGREAD 2026-11-11). UAC is off (EnableLUA=0). See first_run for the possible Security Alert.

On this same machine (then .246), Unreal Gold was verified 2026-08-31 at 1920x1080 and joined .143's server, but it had a real GPU driver then. If the box gets a working display driver before the round, use the XP-group launcher instead.

The SoftDrv and 1024x768 values are box-local. The staged Play launcher (render device) and the GAMERES startup pass (viewport) put D3DDrv and 1920x1080 back on their next run.

launchers.bat:
@echo off
rem UnrealGold - fleet LAN round, Windows 98 SE + 3dfx Voodoo 2. COMMAND.COM.
rem No percent-tilde paths, no cd /d, no start with a title, no blocks.
rem The round writes the player name, net speed and the F9 join key into
rem E:\GAMES\UnrealGold\System\User.ini through the agent - DOWNLOAD, edit,
rem UPLOAD - before it launches this; FLEETRES is cmd.exe syntax and is not
rem run on this box. The start is the staged Voodoo shortcut's: GlideDrv,
rem 640x480x16, from a fresh copy of Voodoo.tpl.
E:
cd \GAMES\UNREALGOLD
if not exist SYSTEM\UNREAL.EXE goto end
if exist SYSTEM\GLIDE2X.DLL del SYSTEM\GLIDE2X.DLL
cd SYSTEM
if exist RUNNING.INI del RUNNING.INI
copy /y VOODOO.TPL VOODOO.INI > nul
start /w UNREAL.EXE -INI=Voodoo.ini
cd ..
if exist DESKFIX9.EXE DESKFIX9.EXE
cls
:end
launchers.notes:
Write this as C:\FLEETMP\UGOLD.BAT. A 9x LAUNCH of a .bat goes through command.com /c in its own console (agent/shared/launchline.h). On .243 use only agent-internal commands: DOWNLOAD, UPLOAD, DIRLIST, REGREAD, UIKEY, WINLIST, PROCLIST, PROCKILL. No EXEC, and no FLEETRES.EXE.

Pre-check: REGREAD HKLM Software\RetroAgent. Require PciRescueBoot from THIS boot to say every installed PCI device is present. Today it reads 'agent 1.98.0, uptime 45s: all 6 installed PCI device(s) present'. Glide on a Voodoo 2 the BIOS left unconfigured maps the card over RAM and kills the box.

Before LAUNCH, patch User.ini:
1. DOWNLOAD E:\GAMES\UnrealGold\System\User.ini (today: library bytes, md5 b532260a023c63d68eda60beb6887d8c).
2. Replace exactly these three lines, keeping CRLF (each occurs once):
   - 'Name=Player' -> 'Name={name}'
   - 'F9=Shot' -> 'F9=open {host}:7807?Name={name}'
   - 'NetSpeed=2600' -> 'NetSpeed=20000'
3. UPLOAD it, then DOWNLOAD again to verify.

Win98's PROCLIST names processes by FULL upper-case path, e.g. E:\GAMES\UNREALGOLD\SYSTEM\UNREAL.EXE. Match Unreal.exe by basename, case-insensitively, for the foreground check and PROCKILL. Kill only UNREAL.EXE, never the DOS VM (WINOA386.MOD / COMMAND.COM). After the round, UPLOAD the original User.ini bytes back once Unreal is gone.

This launcher is the staged 'Play Unreal Gold - Voodoo.bat' minus its PAUSE branches. That launcher passed on metal 2026-10-03: Glide 2.56 opened, the intro ran, it closed by console quit. On the box: Voodoo.tpl 8771 B, DESKFIX9.EXE 4608 B, only glide2x.dll.nglide (no live wrapper), GamesDir E:\GAMES, Maps\DmDeck16.unr 828303 B.

Timing on this non-MMX P166: press F9 about 75 s after LAUNCH and check the roster about 120 s after F9.

first_run.symptom: WINLIST foreground is class WindowsScreenSaverClass (the 10-minute Starfield screensaver) after LAUNCH
first_run.keys: UIKEY SHIFT, wait 2 s, WINLIST again
first_run.notes: On 2026-11-11 the screensaver was the foreground window on all eight XP boxes in scout-DeusEx/winlist_fg.json. A key sent into it only closes it, so an F9 sent then is lost. Do not wake it before LAUNCH: on a box with no recent input the new Unreal window can take the foreground, and that closes the screensaver. A fresh keypress may start the 200 s ForegroundLockTimeout most boxes carry (0 on .133 and .240). Press F9 only when the foreground pid is Unreal.exe; on .243, match the PROCLIST basename.

first_run.symptom: Intro flyby on screen ('Press ESC to begin' at the top) and the box is not in the server's \players\ list. This is the normal state after launch.
first_run.keys: WINLIST first (foreground pid must be Unreal.exe), then UIKEY F9
first_run.notes: The launcher bound F9 to 'open <host>:7807?Name=Fleet<octet>' in this box's User.ini. WindowConsole returns False for F9 in its global state, so the binding runs. In state UWindow, F9 is handed to Global.KeyEvent, which also returns False (UWindow.u source). The intro does not open the menu by itself: UnrealI.Intro's HUDType is IntroNullHud (parsed from UnrealI.u class defaults), the 7th-caption auto-ESC is EndgameHud (the EndGame ending), and UPakIntroNullHud's ShowMenu call is commented out. Do NOT press ESC first. Timing after LAUNCH: XP about 30-45 s, 60 s on .133/.184, about 75 s on .243. A key pressed before the viewport opens is lost: press again if the box is missing from the roster about 60 s later. A repeat press while connecting only restarts the connect. The renderer-picker first-run dialog is suppressed: FirstRun=226 is in every box's Unreal.ini and in .243's Voodoo.ini.

first_run.symptom: Box joined (its name is on the server) but the UMenu menu bar or a menu window is drawn over the game
first_run.keys: UIKEY ESCAPE (once)
first_run.notes: This happens only if ESC or the console key reached the game, since the intro does not open the menu itself. Send ESC only after a screenshot shows the menu. In game with no menu, ESC OPENS it: User.ini has Escape=ShowMenu, and WindowConsole launches UWindow on IK_Escape.

first_run.symptom: F9 twice did nothing: no 'Open MyLevel ... 192.168.1.<octet>' line in server.log
first_run.keys: If a menu is visible, UIKEY ESCAPE first. Then UIKEY TILDE ; UIKEY TEXT:open 192.168.1.132:7807?Name=Fleet<octet> ; UIKEY RETURN
first_run.notes: The typed console 'open' is measured on 226: retro-3dfx/FINDINGS.md 2026-08-31 item 2, where .246 joined .143's UCC 226 server. .124 also reached 7807 on 2026-09-28, against 227k, which refused on package version. On .243, console 'quit' by keystroke worked 2026-10-03. With a menu up, Tilde opens the console only if Root.bAllowConsole is set, hence ESC first.

first_run.symptom: A Yes/No box asking whether to start Unreal in safe mode because it did not shut down properly
first_run.keys: UIKEY N
first_run.notes: Caused by a stale System\Running.ini, which every PROCKILL leaves behind. All three launchers delete it before start, and no box has one today, so this should only appear if Unreal.exe is started some other way.

first_run.symptom: An Unreal 'Critical Error' / General Protection Fault window
first_run.keys: UIKEY RETURN (dismiss), then relaunch the round launcher once
first_run.notes: The cause is at the end of <root>\System\Unreal.log. Read it with DOWNLOAD, which is mandatory on .243. This is the failure class that excludes .143.

first_run.symptom: .186 only: a 'Windows Security Alert' (Windows Firewall has blocked some features of this program) window, or WINLIST foreground leaves Unreal.exe right after F9
first_run.keys: UIKEY ESCAPE (= Cancel), then WINLIST
first_run.notes: Windows Firewall is ON on .186, with notifications on and no Unreal rule, so the alert may appear when Unreal opens its UDP socket. The client's own outbound flow to 7807 and its replies pass a stateful firewall whichever button is chosen; Cancel only adds an inbound block. 'Allow access' would add a rule. UAC is off (EnableLUA=0), so no consent prompt appears, but adding the rule is a change on the box and is the round's call. If Unreal is left minimized afterwards, record it; the server roster still witnesses the join.

first_run.symptom: .186 only: Unreal opens in a window, or exits right after start
first_run.keys: none - record the result
first_run.notes: DirectDraw on Win7's Standard VGA driver refused the mode, or SoftDrv failed. A windowed run is not a pass. Read System\Unreal.log with DOWNLOAD.

UnrealGold.in_game_proof:
Four witnesses, strongest first:

1. Server roster. Send UDP \players\ (or \status\) to 192.168.1.132:7808. Unreal 226 sends one datagram per HUMAN player, \player_N\Fleet<octet>\frags_N\..\ping_N\..\team_N\..\skin_N\..\mesh_N\.., and the last one carries \final\. IpServer.u's GetPlayer and SendPlayers walk PlayerPawns only, so bots never appear; with 0 humans the reply is just \final\. \info\ numplayers counts humans; \game_property\NumBots\ gives 3. Each box's name is unique to it, so the name proves the box.

2. Server log, /home/voidsstr/unrealgold-server/server.log. Per box, look for:
- 'Open MyLevel <MM/DD/YY HH:MM:SS> 192.168.1.<octet>:<port>' (the IP)
- 'Client netspeed is 20000' (2600 means the User.ini NetSpeed write did not take)
- 'Login request: Index.unr?Name=Fleet<octet>?...'
- 'Join request: Index.unr?Name=Fleet<octet>?Class=...'
- 'Login: Fleet<octet>'
- 'Join succeeded: Fleet<octet>'
The formats come from Engine.dll's strings and the 2026-08-31 UCC console capture (/home/voidsstr/lan-proof/unreal-rts/unrealgold-SERVER-143-console-join-succeeded.png). Count a box only when both its IP line and its name line are present.

3. Per box, in game with no menu open: UIKEY F1 (ShowScores, a toggle), a frame of the scoreboard listing the Fleet names beside the bots, then F1 again.

4. Optional: a tcpdump packet count per source IP to dst port 7807 (lanparty.py sniff).

A running Unreal.exe is not proof.
UnrealGold.screenshot_notes:
XP D3DDrv boxes (.110 .123 .133 .171 .184 .240): GDI SCREENSHOT 0 captures Unreal Gold fullscreen. The compat DB has 2026-08-31 frames from .123, .133, .171 and .240; .171's predates its swap to the GeForce FX 5500. The only black-frame record is .143, which is excluded.

.124 (GlideDrv on vcr-kmd): GDI hands back a stale frame. Use EXECW 60 C:\vcr\vcrctl.exe fbshot C:\fleetmp\ug124.bmp, then DOWNLOAD it (vcrctl.exe, 326480 B, is in C:\vcr). The server roster is the real witness.

.243 (Voodoo 2 pass-through): GDI sees only the Cirrus 2D desktop. Use the engine's own shot: UIKEY F11 (F11=Shot) writes System\ShotNNNN.bmp. Find the newest one with DIRLIST E:\GAMES\UnrealGold\System and fetch it with DOWNLOAD, never EXEC.

.186 (Win7, SoftDrv on DirectDraw emulation): GDI capture is uncertain, and dwm.exe is running there. Use F11 Shot plus DOWNLOAD.

F11 Shot works on every renderer, but only while the UWindow menu is closed: in menu state only F9 reaches the bindings. The F1 scoreboard frame is the per-box proof frame. No title here runs 8-bit, so there are no palette artefacts.
known_blockers: Unreal 226 cannot be joined from the command line (retro-3dfx/FINDINGS.md 2026-08-31, item 2). .240's Unreal.log shows 'Browse: 192.168.1.132:7807/Index.unr', then 'Game client on port 0, rate 2600', then the intro LoadMap and 'Unloading: Package IpDrv'. Every box therefore needs ONE keystroke after load (UIKEY F9). It is keyboard-only and automatable.
.143 cannot run Unreal Gold: 8 bugchecks naming Unreal.exe (2026-08-29..31), hard resets under GlideDrv and D3DDrv, and D3DDrv finds no fullscreen modes. Excluded.
.186 has no 3D and cannot get it: Turing TU117 on 32-bit Windows 7 has no driver. Software renderer (SoftDrv) only, untested in this state.
risks: No fleet client has ever joined the host's 226 server: server.log since 2026-09-28 has no 'Open MyLevel'/'Join' line, and the matrix doc says 'not yet re-tested'. This round is its first join. Queries and the beacon work, the packages are md5-identical to the library, ufw is disabled, and 7807/7808/7775 are bound by UCC.exe.

The F9-binding join has not been measured on Unreal Gold itself. It rests on 226's WindowConsole source and on the Deus Ex finding (FINDINGS 2026-08-31 item 3: an F5=open binding pressed with UIKEY joined in one shot). The typed console 'open' has been measured on 226 and is the fallback.
The intro does NOT open the menu by itself. That claim confused it with EndgameHud, the ending's HUD. So F9 normally lands with no menu up. Never send ESC before the join: it opens the menu.
Idle XP boxes show the Starfield screensaver as the foreground window. A key sent into it is swallowed. Check WINLIST before F9, and send SHIFT once if the screensaver is still up after load.

.124 runs on vcr-kmd, an experimental driver. Unreal Gold through GlideDrv there has only been seen on the intro (2026-09-28, 10-03). A level change under GlideDrv has not been observed for this title, although UT436 joined the UT99 server from .124 on 10-13. A 1280x1024 Glide re-open once hung there; the Glide 2 ladder keeps it at 1024x768. Reading its log: GlideDrv's 'grSstOpen Res=%i Ref=%i' appears to print the refresh code first. .124's 10-03 'Res=7 Ref=12' fits 85 Hz at 1024x768 in Glide 2 enums, and .243's 'Res=0 Ref=7' fits 60 Hz at 640x480.

.243 is a non-MMX Pentium 166 at 127 MB: expect very low fps and long loads, about 200 s from LAUNCH to in-game. It runs a single-threaded Win98 agent: agent-internal commands only, and close every connection gracefully (the Win98 RST crash). Its PROCLIST names are full upper-case paths, so a name-equality check reports Unreal as not running. Check PciRescueBoot first: Glide on an unconfigured Voodoo 2 kills the box.

.186 is untested. DirectDraw on the Win7 Standard VGA driver may refuse the 1024x768 mode, which would leave a windowed run (not a pass), or SoftDrv may fail. Its Windows Firewall is ON, so a Security Alert may pull the game out of focus at the join.

The launchers change each box's System\User.ini: Name=Fleet<octet>, NetSpeed=20000, and F9 bound to the join instead of Shot. The change persists until restored. Restore it by UPLOADing the library User.ini (5528 B, md5 b532260a023c63d68eda60beb6887d8c) after Unreal.exe is killed. GAMESYNC does not re-run on a provisioned box by itself.

Without NetSpeed raised, 226 clients connect at 2600 (the 2026-08-31 server log reads 'Client netspeed is 2600'), which makes play jerky with 12 pawns. The launcher sets 20000; the server's MaxClientRate is 20000. Confirm with the server's 'Client netspeed is 20000' line.

The 3 server bots are fixed (InitialBots=3, Hard). They take no player slots (DeathMatchGame.AddBot bumps NumBots, and PreLogin checks NumPlayers) and never leave. With 9 humans, DmDeck16 holds 12 pawns.
PROCKILL leaves System\Running.ini behind. All three round launchers delete it on the next start; an Unreal.exe started any other way would raise the safe-mode question.
The staged 'Host Unreal Gold LAN.bat' header is out of date: it still says no host-side 226 server is possible, and it misquotes 'Join succeeded!'. Do not run it in this round.
.110 and .123 have never run Unreal Gold since their re-image (no Unreal.log). D3DDrv on a GeForce 7800 GS at 1600x1200 and on a Radeon HD 3850 at 1280x960 is unmeasured on these boxes.

host_box.command: No box hosts. The dev host's unrealgold-server is already running and must not be restarted: docker container ugsrv (up since 16:02 UTC today) runs 'wine UCC.exe server "DmDeck16.unr?game=UnrealShare.DeathMatchGame?maxplayers=12" -ini=UnrealServer.ini -port=7807'. Pre-check: RETRO_GAMESERVER_HOST=127.0.0.1 python3 scripts/game-servers/gameservers.py | grep 'Unreal Gold'. Expected: 'OK Unreal Gold active 3/12 ... DMDeck16 [gamever 226]'.

server.unit: unrealgold-server
server.query_kind: GameSpy UE1 on UDP 7808. gameservers.py probe 'unreal226' sends \info\, requires gamever 226, and adds \game_property\NumBots\. The roster comes from \players\ or \status\. \status\ arrives as basic, info and rules datagrams, then one datagram per human.
server.roster_how: Send UDP \players\ (or \status\) to 192.168.1.132:7808 and collect datagrams until 0.7 s of silence. Names are the values of player_N. Only humans are listed: with 0 humans the reply is '\final\\queryid\N.0'. \info\ numplayers = humans, \game_property\NumBots\ = 3, maxplayers = 12, and \game_property\NumPlayers\ comes back empty on 226. Live at 14:1x today: 0 humans, 3 bots. lanparty.py's GameSpy \status\ parser reads this format as-is.
server.log_how:
The unit appends UCC's stdout to /home/voidsstr/unrealgold-server/server.log. journalctl --user -u unrealgold-server has only systemd lines, not the game output. Watch live with: tail -n0 -F /home/voidsstr/unrealgold-server/server.log | grep -a --line-buffered -E 'Open MyLevel|Client netspeed is|Join request|Join succeeded|Join failure|Login failed|Login: |Close TcpipConnection'. Afterwards, use the same grep with -n on the file. Lines have no category prefix in this log. Expected per box:
- 'Open MyLevel <MM/DD/YY HH:MM:SS> 192.168.1.<octet>:<port>'
- 'Client netspeed is 20000'
- 'Join request: Index.unr?Name=Fleet<octet>?Class=...'
- 'Login: Fleet<octet>'
- 'Join succeeded: Fleet<octet>'
'docker logs ugsrv 2>&1 | grep ...' shows the same lines, but only since the container's last start (16:02 UTC today).
server.bots_note: 3 bots on 'Hard' (bMultiPlayerBots=True, InitialBots=3, BotInfo.Difficulty=2), spawned at start. Per 226's DeathMatchGame and GameInfo source, they are NOT counted in NumPlayers: AddBot bumps NumBots, and the capacity check is NumPlayers>=MaxPlayers, humans only. So they hold no slots, and they never leave, because 226 has no MinPlayers backfill. They are absent from \players\ and from numplayers.
server.changes_needed: None required: 12 human slots against 9 applicable boxes (11 if .145 and .197 come on). Optional only, and not for this round: maxplayers 16 for headroom, via UG_MAXPLAYERS in ~/unrealgold-server/_run/run-ug-server.sh.

review_issues: WRONG: the recipe says the intro opens the UWindow menu by itself after its 7th caption, with IntroNullHud calling Console.KeyEvent(IK_Escape). DieByTheSword.mp_summary: Die by the Sword has real multiplayer: DirectPlay over IPX, TCP/IP, modem or serial, up to 4 players, with one player hosting. Sources: readme section D items 4-5, windie.exe's Arena/Multiplay strings, and its code references to DPSPGUID_IPX/TCPIP/MODEM/SERIAL. .243 has all four DirectPlay service providers. A whole-fleet round is impossible, for three reasons. (1) Only ONE fleet box can run it. requires.json sets max_os win9x on the title and on its only shortcut DBTS.BAT, and the shortcut also needs the glide capability. .243 (Win98 SE 4.10.2222 A, P166, Voodoo 2) is the only Win9x box. .124 was re-imaged and is no longer a Win98/XP dual-boot. So the title is deployed nowhere else: plan_args/inv/desk show no DieByTheSword folder or shortcut on any other box, and compat.py says '.123 OS too new for this title (have winxp, max win9x) [rule]'. A one-box match has no opponent. (2) The game has no dedicated server, and nothing on 192.168.1.132 serves it: no entry in gameservers.py SERVERS, no unit in ~/.config/systemd/user, no docker container. (3) Hosting and joining are menu-only: Main Menu > Arena > Multiplay > service provider (IPX / TCP/IP / Modem / Serial) > 'Host new game' + 'Name session to host', or 'Address of host / or hit return to search' > choose character > Enter Arena. windie.exe's switch table (3dfx, n3dfx, nocd, 16M, nogore, lowgore, fullgore, modex, cap<N>, master, slave, network, local, frname:, god, window, singlethread, killaudio, ...) has no host or connect switch. master/slave pass 5/4 to an undocumented developer mode setter, network only swaps in the developer's f:\die\data\ path, and local takes a data path. It cannot be lobby-launched either. It creates an IDirectPlayLobby2 only to build and parse addresses (CreateCompoundAddress, EnumAddress) and never calls GetConnectionSettings or Connect, and .243 has no DirectPlay\Applications registration. The menu cursor is game-drawn (mainmenu\arrow.bmp) from DirectInput, and the Voodoo 2 picture cannot be photographed, so any menu work would be blind. The round is therefore a single-player, fullscreen Glide liveness check on .243 only. It uses the staged DBTS.BAT through the route the 2026-10-03 metal pass proved (windie.exe up after 60 s, no dialogs), then PROCKILL windie.exe and GLRESET9. Unattended, the compat cell stays at 'runs', which was already hand-recorded. 'verified' needs a person at .243 to confirm the Voodoo 2 picture. Multiplayer stays untested because only one box can run the game, and no join is attempted. Confidence refers to this single-player launcher starting the game with nobody present.

launchers.bat:
@echo off
rem Die by the Sword - single-player Glide check, Win98 Voodoo 2 box only
E:
cd \GAMES\DIEBYT~1
call DBTS.BAT
launchers.notes: Write it with CRLF to C:\fleetmp\DieByTheSword.bat. Run MKDIR C:\fleetmp first: the folder does not exist on .243 (DIRLIST C:\FLEETMP* returned [] on 2026-11-11 14:10). lanparty.py's launch_bat already does the MKDIR. The 8.3 path E:\GAMES\DIEBYT~1 resolves to E:\GAMES\DieByTheSword: DIRLIST E:\GAMES\DIEBYT~1\WINDIE.* returned windie.exe (1,750,528 B), and DieByTheSword is the only E:\GAMES\DIE* entry. It is also the path the desktop .pif and metal243.py use. Launch it the way the 2026-10-03 metal pass did: LAUNCH C:\WINDOWS\COMMAND\START.EXE C:\fleetmp\DieByTheSword.bat. START.EXE (28,672 B, present) is an existing .exe, so agent 1.90.1+ starts it directly (agent/shared/launchline.h; .243 runs 1.98.0), and START opens the batch in its own DOS box. The metal pass gave START an 8.3 name (C:\RETRO_AGENT\RUNT.BAT). If START balks at the long name, pass the same file's short alias, C:\FLEETMP\DIEBYT~1.BAT (the folder is new, so the alias is ~1). lanparty.py's plain LAUNCH "C:\fleetmp\DieByTheSword.bat" becomes command.com /c "..." in a new console on 9x (agent/src/exec.c). Its tail is about 46 characters, under the 127-character limit, so it should also work, but it is unproven on this box. The title has no FLEETRES.BAT (none in the library tree) and needs none. Glide drives the Voodoo 2 fullscreen through its pass-through at the game's own mode (HKCU Video Mode = Normal Resolution), and the 2D desktop (800x600x16 on the Cirrus) is untouched. DBTS.BAT looks for GLIDE2X.DLL in %windir%\SYSTEM32, then %windir%\SYSTEM (C:\WINDOWS\SYSTEM\GLIDE2X.DLL, 226,304 B, present). It runs 'start /w WINDIE.EXE -3dfx -nocd', then DESKFIX9.EXE and cls, so the DOS box closes itself when the game ends. No player name or connect argument ({name}/{host} unused): this is single-player only.

DieByTheSword.in_game_proof: No server or roster exists, so the proof comes from .243 alone. In order: (1) 60 s after launch, PROCLIST shows windie.exe. .243's PROCLIST returns full paths (verified 2026-11-11: C:\WINDOWS\EXPLORER.EXE, C:\RETRO_AGENT\RETRO_AGENT.EXE), most likely E:\GAMES\DIEBYT~1\WINDIE.EXE here. Compare the lower-cased basename; lanparty.py's exact-name test will miss it. (2) WINLIST shows no #32770 dialog, and no DOS box stuck at one of DBTS.BAT's PAUSE branches ('No 3dfx Glide driver is installed' / 'tree is incomplete'). In the 2026-10-03 pass the foreground window was the batch's own box, titled 'START /w WINDIE.EXE -3dfx -nocd'; that is normal. (3) A person at .243 confirms the Voodoo 2 picture (logo/main menu or an arena). Without (3) the compat cell is 'runs', never 'verified'. After PROCKILL, GLRESET.TXT reading 'OK: Glide opened and closed on board 0 - the passthrough is back on the 2D card' shows only that the board was handed back, not that the game rendered.
known_blockers: Only one box in the fleet can run the title: max_os win9x on the title and on DBTS.BAT, plus the glide capability. .243 is the only Win9x box (.124's old Win98 dual-boot is gone after its re-image), so there is no second player and no multiplayer round at all.
No dedicated server exists for Die by the Sword, and none runs on 192.168.1.132: nothing in gameservers.py SERVERS, ~/.config/systemd/user or docker. A player hosts through DirectPlay.

Multiplayer host/join is menu-only: Arena > Multiplay > IPX / TCP/IP / Modem / Serial > 'Host new game' or 'Address of host'. The switch table has no command-line host or connect switch. The cursor is game-drawn from DirectInput and the Voodoo 2 output cannot be photographed, so it cannot be driven unattended.

A lobby launcher cannot auto-connect it. windie.exe creates an IDirectPlayLobby2 (CoCreateInstance, 0x4a07e6-0x4a07f9) but uses it only for CreateCompoundAddress (vtbl+0x38) and EnumAddress (vtbl+0x14). It never calls GetConnectionSettings or Connect, so it does not read lobby connection settings. REGREAD of HKLM\Software\Microsoft\DirectPlay\Applications on .243 fails ('Cannot open key'), and the staged install.reg adds no registration.

A real multi-box game would need a second Win9x + Glide machine, or a library/gate change that stages an XP variant (untested, out of scope here). The XP options are Glide 2 on .124's Voodoo 5 6000; the rld3d.dll D3D renderer, which the readme says works only on Riva 128 / Matrox; or the game's own software renderer ('Do Not Use 3D Hardware -- Use Software Rendering Only' in the detection dialog, or -n3dfx). The W98BUILD VMs cannot be the opponent: each sits behind its own SLiRP NAT, which DirectPlay IPX cannot cross and TCP/IP session search will not traverse.
risks: PROCKILL of windie.exe (a DirectSound game) on Win98 can leave the SB16 held until a restart. On 2026-10-03, TIE Fighter then failed with 'Error in Sound Config!'. Run Die by the Sword after .243's DOS and other sound titles in the session. Any restart afterwards goes through scripts/fleet/safe-reboot.py 192.168.1.243, never a bare REBOOT, and only with the operator's go-ahead.
Always run GLRESET9.EXE after the kill. Otherwise the last 3D frame stays on the monitor and later checks on .243 are misread.

lanparty.py's kill_games and shot_box compare full PROCLIST names to bare exe names. .243's PROCLIST returns full paths, so the tool would report windie.exe as not running and never kill it. Match on the lower-cased basename, as metal243.py does.

lanparty.py's DEFAULT_BOXES ([110,123,124,133,143,145,171,184,197,240]) omits .243. A title entry built from this recipe must carry a title-level boxes list [243], or the run must pass --boxes 243. Otherwise 'run' prints 'no launcher for: [110, ...]', launches nothing, and never mentions .243.

UIKEY goes to the focused window. In the 2026-10-03 pass that was the batch's DOS box, not the game, so keys probably never reach windie.exe's DirectInput. Never send ALT+TAB (it crashes the 3dfx build) or blind ALT+F4.

.243 is a single-threaded Win98 agent. Never use EXEC to read a file (use DOWNLOAD). Keep connections few and close them gracefully (Win98 RST crash). Do not hit it with many scouts or rounds in parallel. A wedged .243 needs a person at the keyboard.

If DBTS.BAT stops at one of its PAUSE branches (no Glide, incomplete tree), a DOS box sits waiting for a key. Close it with LAUNCH C:\RETRO_AGENT\WINKEY9X.EXE "<title substring>" CLOSE, then answer the terminate dialog with WINKEY9X "<title>" Y. Never answer RETURN: the default button is No.
This is a Pentium 166 with 127 MB, so loads are slow. Give it the full 60 s (as the metal pass did) before judging it dead.
DieByTheSword.screenshot_notes: SCREENSHOT on .243 photographs only the Cirrus 2D desktop. The Voodoo 2 drives the monitor through its pass-through, so GDI never sees a Glide frame (docs/evidence/2026-10-03-243-metal-pass/README.md; lanparty.py docstring). A capture taken mid-game shows the desktop and the DOS box and proves nothing about rendering, so a person at the box has to judge the picture. lanparty.py's shot_box (SCREENSHOT 1) returns that same desktop, so its frame and 'black' flag mean nothing for this title. Do not try ALT+RETURN or ALT+TAB to get a frame: ALT+TAB crashes the 3dfx build (readme E.6). The vcrctl fbshot route is .124-only. windie.exe has an undocumented debug switch cap<N> (switch table) and a CAPTURE%d.BMP format string. That is an untested lead only; do not use it unattended on .243.

AliensVsPredator.mp_summary: AvP is broken on every box today. Three primary sources now prove why. AvP Gold is DirectPlay peer-to-peer over TCP/IP or IPX. Both the retail readme ('eight player maximum limit') and the code at 0x48ac3b cap a session at 8 players. Rebellion shipped no dedicated server, and 192.168.1.132 has no AvP unit, container or gameservers.py entry. No box reaches the game's front end. All 7 boxes that ever launched it (.123 .124 .133 .143 .171 .184 .240) wrote the same LOGFILE.TXT: 49 CL_LoadImageOnce misses (98 log lines, 34 distinct Menus/Common .rim images), 0 'Loaded FastFile:' lines, all 136 sounds loaded 'by ExtractWavFile', then 'ASSERTION FAILED! Expression: pSurface File: ..\3dc\win95\alt_tab.cpp Line: 198'. The assert is hidden behind the exclusive 640x480x16 mode, which is the 'black screen / stall' every earlier note describes. CAUSE: the library tree is the disc's loose files, not an installed tree. Every one of the 470 files it shares with disc 1 is md5-identical, and 154 of them (139.7 MiB) are stored InstallShield-OBFUSCATED on the disc: all 63 avp_rifs\*.RIF, all 23 avp_huds\*.rif, fastfile\ffinfo.txt, fastfile\Tex1-58.FFL, and 9 FMVs (logos.bik, IntroSound.smk, Menubackground.bik and the six intro/outro .bik files). The disc's own data1.cab header sets FILE_OBFUSCATED (flags 0x6) on exactly 154 descriptors whose sizes match these files one for one; every other file is 0x4. So the retail setup decodes them while copying. avp.exe's fastfile loader (0x4de260) opens fastfile\ffinfo.txt in text mode, reads 512-byte lines with fgets and keeps only lines that start with A-Z/a-z. It does no decoding, so nothing usable is registered and the menu pack is never found (graphics\Menus;Tex37.FFL, which holds Menus\IntroFont.RIM). DECODE VERIFIED, FIX UNPROVEN IN GAME (read-only run, nothing applied): per file, b[i] = ror8(b[i] XOR 0xD5, 2) - (i mod 0x47), with i = 0 at the start of each file (unshield's algorithm). It makes ffinfo.txt 108 CRLF lines, makes all 58 Tex*.FFL valid RFFL packs whose sizes match exactly, makes the RIFs read REBCRIF1 and the videos BIK/SMK. The alternative, which the build-VM rule prefers, is to run the retail setup in the XP build VM and capture the tree. Then purge + GAMESYNC. Pass = LOGFILE.TXT shows 'Loaded FastFile:' and no ASSERTION. AFTER THAT FIX the round is peer_box_host: .110 hosts from its own menu (Multiplayer, TCP/IP, Host, max players 8), and the 7 other capable boxes run 'avp.exe -ip 192.168.1.110'. -ip only pre-fills the Join screen's IP field (the menu code at 0x48d725 copies the 15-char command-line buffer at 0x5850b1 into the field at 0x5850a1), so joining still needs menu work, and UIKEY delivery to those menus is unproven. In practice that is mp_not_automatable unless a DirectPlay lobby launcher is built (see known_blockers). A fleet-wide round on today's tree would only repeat the 7 identical logs. If a round must run, .110 alone is enough: it is the only capable box that has never launched AvP.

launchers.notes: With TODAY's library tree this reproduces the known failure: the screen goes to 640x480x16, nothing draws, and a hidden assert box blocks the game. Read LOGFILE.TXT, then taskkill. After the library fix, the host still has to work the menus by keyboard: Multiplayer, TCP/IP, Host game, max players 8 (the cap; 0x48ac3b clamps it to 1..8), start. MPConfig\Config1-7.cfg are saved host setups that ship with the game, and avp.exe loads MPConfig\*.cfg. The menu key sequence is unverified because no box has ever reached the menus. There is deliberately no {name}: AvP takes the player name from its user profile, its MP menu, or a DirectPlay lobby's DPNAME, never from the command line. '-n %s' fills the level-name buffer at 0x59ea34 (it starts as 'predbit6'), which a debug start path uses. It is not a player name, so do not use it.

{host} = 192.168.1.110. avp.exe parses -ip before the fastfile init: sscanf('-ip %s'), then strncpy of 15 chars into 0x5850b1. It is harmless today, and '-ip 192.168.1.110' contains no other switch avp.exe tests for (-l -server -client -debug -w -s -n). With today's tree every joiner shows the same assert as the host. After the fix, joining still needs menu work: Multiplayer, TCP/IP, Join, confirm the pre-filled IP, pick the session, choose species and name, join. That path is unverified. Do NOT use -server or -client: they are DirectPlay-LOBBY launches. With no lobby, GetConnectionSettings fails and avp.exe exits with code 0x6364 for either switch.

known_blockers: THE LIBRARY TREE IS THE DISC'S LOOSE FILES, NOT AN INSTALLED TREE (root cause, 2026-11-11). 154 files (139.7 MiB) are still InstallShield-obfuscated and md5-identical to disc 1; all 470 files the tree shares with the disc are md5-identical. The full list is in .claude/evidence-readiness-2026-11-11/scout-AliensVsPredator/obfuscated_files.txt: all 63 avp_rifs\*.RIF, all 23 avp_huds\*.rif, fastfile\ffinfo.txt + Tex1..Tex58.FFL, FMVs\logos.bik, IntroSound.smk, Menubackground.bik and the six intro/outro .bik files. The disc's data1.cab header flags exactly these 154 FILE_OBFUSCATED (0x6), and every other file is 0x4 (table: scout-AliensVsPredator/is_header_flags.txt), so the retail setup decodes them as it copies. The 50 Snd*.FFL, shape_rifs, MPConfig, English, the sound .dat files and avp.exe are plain. All 9 boxes carry the obfuscated ffinfo.txt (scout read of every box; .110 and .240 re-read in the fact-check). FIX, by either route. (a) The route the build-VM rule prefers: run the retail setup in the XP build VM (~/retro-vm/run-build.sh) and capture the 154 decoded files. (b) Decode them on the host with a FULL-file converter: b[i] = (ror8(b[i] ^ 0xD5, 2) - (i % 0x47)) & 0xFF, with i = 0 at the start of each file. isdeobf.py only previews 8 KB and writes nothing, so it is not that converter. Either way, write each file through scripts/fleet/libwrite.py, or sharewrite.py put with a read-back of each file through /mnt. stage-new-title.py will not work: it refuses an existing title. The sizes do not change, so purge C:\Games\AliensVsPredator on each box and GAMESYNC. Then check that the box's fastfile\ffinfo.txt starts 'Graphics\Common;Tex1.FFL' and that LOGFILE.TXT shows 'Loaded FastFile:' and no ASSERTION. This corrects three earlier conclusions. README-FLEET's 'byte-complete' is true against the disc, but the disc stores these files obfuscated. PER-TITLE-STATUS's 'graphics fastfile content absent from every distribution' is wrong: the content is present, obfuscated. The compat DB's 'runs (d3d 640x480 yes)' rows record only the mode switch before the assert.

No server for AvP exists on 192.168.1.132, and Rebellion shipped no dedicated server (docs/staged-title-server-matrix.md row 1; the disc carries no server binary). The DirectPlay session is hosted by a player's avp.exe.

No unattended join path exists today. -ip <addr> only pre-fills the Join screen, so joining needs work in menus that read input through DirectInput (avp.exe imports DINPUT.dll). docs/lan-multiplayer-status.md lists AvP under 'needs a person, once: drive its menus at the keyboard', while its line 484 says AvP's menus are 'driven by relative mouse deltas'. Both are unproven, because no box has ever reached the menus; the key sequence is unknown.

Fully unattended multiplayer needs a DirectPlay LOBBY launcher, and none exists yet (no RunApplication or IDirectPlayLobby code anywhere in the repo). avp.exe is lobby-aware. -server sets LobbiedGame=1 and -client sets 2. 0x48ae34 then creates IDirectPlayLobby3A and calls GetConnectionSettings. On -server it ORs the session flags with 0x44 (KEEPALIVE|MIGRATEHOST), sets dwUser1=100 and calls SetConnectionSettings. It copies DPLCONNECTION.lpPlayerName->lpszShortNameA (up to 12 chars) as the player name, then calls ConnectEx. With no lobby it exits 0x6364. RunApplication also needs the registration that setup.ins writes and install.reg lacks: HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\DirectPlay\Applications\Aliens versus Predator with Guid={379CCA80-8BDD-11d0-A078-004095E16EA5} (also embedded in avp.exe at file offset 0x8ad20), File=AvP.exe, Path and CurrentDirectory=C:\Games\AliensVsPredator\, and CommandLine=-server (a joiner would need -client). The launcher would call RunApplication with DPLCONNECTION_CREATESESSION on the host, and JOINSESSION carrying the same guidInstance on the clients, with guidSP=TCP/IP, a DPAID_INet address for the host, and lpszShortNameA=Fleet<octet>. Whether the host still has to start the match from its menu is unverified.
8-player session cap: the readme and 0x48ac3b both cap it, and that is exactly the 8 capable boxes. The host must set 8; .186 could never be a 9th.
Music is redbook audio on the audio-only disc 2, so the game has no music. That is expected, not a blocker.

review_issues: The verdict holds and is now stronger. broken_known, the root cause, the 8 applicable boxes, the two exclusions, exe avp.exe, no AvP server and the -ip pre-fill all check out against primary sources. One new source settles the cause: the disc's own data1.cab InstallShield header puts FILE_OBFUSCATED (flags 0x6) on exactly 154 descriptors, and their sizes match the recipe's 154 files one for one. Every other file is 0x4. The table is saved at .claude/evidence-readiness-2026-11-11/scout-AliensVsPredator/is_header_flags.txt. The problems below are errors in the details and in the fix procedure, not in the verdict.

mp_summary says '98 CL_LoadImageOnce misses'. That is wrong. Each of the 7 logs has 49 misses: 98 CL_LoadImageOnce lines, two per miss, over 34 distinct .rim images, with Menus\bonus.rim alone 15 times. The other counts are right: 0 'Loaded FastFile:', 136 of 136 sounds 'by ExtractWavFile', 1 ASSERTION each.

The .243 exclusion reason is partly false. It says 'Its Voodoo 2 is a 3D-only add-in card, and AvP is a DirectDraw/Direct3D title', but AvP Gold's own readme.txt lists Voodoo2 and Voodoo 1 as Direct3D graphics cards you can select. Its example: one Voodoo2 shows 1024x768, which needs two cards. The exclusion still stands on other grounds: CPUID family 5 model 2 with HWPROFILE features [fpu], so no MMX (the readme minimum is 'Pentium 200 MMX'); 165 MHz, under requires.json's 200 MHz floor; and the operator override, so there is no folder and no shortcut.

In risks, 'libwrite or stage-new-title.py is the safe route' is wrong for this title. scripts/fleet/stage-new-title.py lines 97-99 refuse any title that already exists ('this only creates NEW titles'). AliensVsPredator needs libwrite.py, or sharewrite.py put with a read-back of each file through /mnt.

known_blockers points to 'script: scout-AliensVsPredator/isdeobf.py' as the fix. That script decodes only the first 8 KB of each file, prints a preview and writes nothing. The fix needs a full-file converter, with i starting at 0 for each file and running over the whole file.

'VERIFIED FIX' overstates what was checked. I reproduced and confirmed the decode: ffinfo.txt becomes 108 CRLF lines; all 58 Tex*.FFL become RFFL packs where 20+headsize+datasize equals the file size and every entry starts 'LIST' (19 packs carry 2 bytes of alignment padding); Tex37 holds every Menus\*.RIM the logs miss; Tex1 holds Common\aa_font.RIM. But no box has run a decoded tree, so the fix is still unproven in the game.

The joiner notes say -server/-client exit 'with code 0x6364/0x6365'. In this build both exit 0x6364. The -client branch at 0x4aa216 jumps to 0x4aa078, the same lobby-init call, and its failure is 'mov eax,0x6364; call exit'. 0x6365 is the value in the released source code, not in this binary.

known_blockers says the lobby player name is 'max 11 chars'. At 0x48aee9 the code copies lpszShortNameA with strncpy(0x585070, ..., 12) and writes a NUL at byte 12, so names can be up to 12 characters.

The host notes say '-n %s writes into a general sprintf scratch buffer at 0x59ea34'. 0x59ea34 is the level-name buffer: it starts as 'predbit6' and has 49 code references, so -n chooses a level for the debug start path. The conclusion, do not use it as a player name, is right.

The check 'the log command really shows client joins' fails, because no log records joins. LOGFILE.TXT logs data and device loading only. The 'system message: DPSYS_CREATEPLAYERORGROUP' strings in avp.exe have no code reference. ConsoleLog.txt exists but is 0 bytes on .240. log_how did not say this; the corrected recipe does. Multiplayer proof stays netstat plus a host screenshot.

One doc conflict is not cited. docs/lan-multiplayer-status.md line 484 lists AvP among titles whose menus are 'driven by relative mouse deltas'. That claim is as unproven as the recipe's DirectInput note: all 7 logs assert before the menu, so no box has ever shown it.
Minor: 'the obfuscated index registers nothing' is slightly off. A few garbage fgets lines start with a letter and would be registered as junk entries. Nothing usable is registered.

The real engine is the encrypted SHOCK2.ICD (.text entropy 7.99). No patch is applied: READ-ME-FIRST says all 79 game files MD5-match the CD. launchers.bat:
@echo off
rem System Shock 2 - fleet readiness round: SINGLE-PLAYER fullscreen render check.
rem The staged build is the retail CD engine, window "System Shock 2 Final 1.15",
rem with no patch: its menu has no Multiplayer entry, so there is no server,
rem no host and no player name to set.
rem The tree ships no FLEETRES.BAT. The menu is fixed at 640x480x16 and the
rem in-game default is the same, so the guarded call below is a no-op today.
cd /d "C:\Games\SystemShock2"
if exist "C:\Games\SystemShock2\FLEETRES.BAT" call "C:\Games\SystemShock2\FLEETRES.BAT"
rem A frame left by an earlier title's fbshot must never be scored as this one.
if exist "C:\fleetmp\fb.bmp" del /f /q "C:\fleetmp\fb.bmp" >nul 2>&1
rem The screensaver was running on all 8 boxes at scout time; a game started
rem behind it may not get the foreground for its exclusive mode set.
taskkill /f /im ssstars.scr >nul 2>&1
rem The SafeDisc v1 loader exits silently when the secdrv driver is stopped.
rem install.reg makes it auto-start and it was RUNNING on all eight boxes, but the
rem template-v2 launcher does not start it, so do it here; harmless if running.
sc start secdrv >nul 2>&1
rem The staged launcher mounts the tree's own disc image on DAEMON Tools 3.47
rem device 0 unless a SYSTEMSHOCK2 volume is already in a drive, waits for the
rem drive letter, kills the disc autorun and starts shock2.exe fullscreen.
rem It ends with EXIT, so it must stay the last line.
call "C:\Games\SystemShock2\Play System Shock 2.bat"

Read-only checks on 2026-11-11: Play System Shock 2.bat (24,583 B) and the _disc image (.bin 669,536,784 B = 284,667 x 2352, ISO label SYSTEMSHOCK2 = the launcher's VOLID) are present on all 8, and each box's folder holds exactly the library's 75 names (.123 also has a stale mount-error.txt). DAEMON Tools 3.47 is at C:\Program Files\D-Tools\daemon.exe and running. secdrv is Start=2 and RUNNING. The AppHelp suppression value is set. Indeo VIDC.IV50 is registered. No AppCompat Layers shim names any SS2 path (.124, .143 and .240 read). No {name}/{host}: single player. DT drive contents (fsutil+vol): .110 E:=SamSE, .123 D:=SERIOUS_SAM_RC2, .124 D:=SYSTEMSHOCK2 (already mounted, so its launcher skips the mount), .133 E:=SamSE, .143 E:=BZONE and G:=STARCRAFT (four DT drives D-G per docs/lan-multiplayer-status.md), .171 E:=SamSE, .184 D:=SamSE, .240 F:=STARCRAFT. Deleting C:\fleetmp\fb.bmp only matters on .124 (fbshot) and is harmless elsewhere.

'GDI shows the old desktop' (lan_sweep docstring, lanparty VCR_BOXES) is a Glide/OpenGL fact on this driver. The 2026-08-31 .124 desktop frame is NOT evidence of a capture limit: it predates vcr-kmd, and the agent log inside it shows DISPLAYCFG 1024x768x32 just before the shot, so the game never had the screen. So on .124, take SCREENSHOT 0 first. Use vcrctl (C:\vcr\vcrctl.exe, 326,480 B, 2026-10-05, present) only if the GDI frame is the desktop, e.g. for the in-game 3D frame, and then strictly: DELETE C:\fleetmp\fb.bmp, run EXECW 30 C:\vcr\vcrctl.exe fbshot C:\fleetmp\fb.bmp, and reject the result if the output contains '[EXECW: timed out' or DIRLIST shows fb.bmp older than the shot. A timed-out fbshot leaves the previous title's fb.bmp to be downloaded and scored. If the default path parks (vcr-kmd README: a Direct3D game holding win32k's display lock parks it in the kernel), the README's route is 'vcrctl fbshot <path> --probe' after 'sc start vcrprobe'. The 2026-09-29 menu frame is a genuine fbshot (C:\vcr\systemshock2_dt.bmp, 921,654 B). The main menu is a 2D panel, so only the post-Start-Game frame proves 3D. known_blockers: No multiplayer in the staged build. The retail engine ('Final 1.15': a SafeDisc 1.11.000 loader plus the encrypted SHOCK2.ICD) shows a menu with no Multiplayer entry. Retail shipped without multiplayer; a free post-release patch added it. Its UI exists, unused, in intrface.crf (NETMAIN.STR / NETPLAY.STR). Only the official multiplayer patch (2.3 is the final cumulative build) or NewDark/SS2Tool enables it, and neither is on the share. Even then it is a 4-player peer co-op joined by typing the host IP, not a whole-fleet game. NewDark also needs D3D9, which is risky on .124 (vcr-kmd's DX7-class HAL), .184 (GeForce2) and .133 (GeForce4 Ti).

RogueSquadron.title_display: Star Wars: Rogue Squadron 3D (Factor 5/LucasArts, PC 1998; staged GOG build of v1.3) - 3dfx Voodoo
RogueSquadron.mp_summary:
SINGLE-PLAYER ONLY. The game has no multiplayer mode of any kind, so there is no host server, no join and no whole-fleet round.

EVIDENCE. 'Rogue Squadron.EXE' imports only KERNEL32, USER32, ADVAPI32, ole32, WINMM, IFORCE2, GDI32, DSOUND, DDRAW and DINPUT. Its single ole32 import is StringFromGUID2, with no CoCreateInstance. It contains no dplay/DirectPlayCreate, wsock, IPX, modem, lobby or connect string, and its LoadLibrary target is glide2x.dll. Both exes do carry DirectPlay GUIDs (CLSID_DirectPlay, IID_IDirectPlay4/4A, DPSPGUID_TCPIP/IPX). These are dxguid.lib residue, sitting beside an equally unused CLSID_DirectMusic, and the game has no way to instantiate DirectPlay. ROGUE.EXE is the LucasArts Launcher (Play / Documentation / Other Options / OnLine = Register + Lucasarts.com / Uninstall); its CoCreateInstance import serves IShellLink. The word 'multiplayer' appears only in LucasArts boilerplate: tech support in README.TXT line 635, and the EULA in License.txt line 23. None of the 27 servers in gameservers.py, and no systemd user unit, is for this game.

WHERE IT RUNS. The staged tree is Win9x + Glide only: requires.json sets max_os win9x on the title and on ROGUESQ.BAT, and the shortcut needs the glide capability. It is therefore deployed only on .243 (Win98 SE, P166, Voodoo 2), which has the single desktop shortcut. The XP boxes are excluded by this staging, not by their hardware.

THE ROUND (single-player fullscreen render check, .243 only):
1. Pre-flight the Voodoo 2: PciRescueBoot plus DRIVERS STATUS.
2. Launch C:\fleetmp\RogueSquadron.bat through START.EXE. It calls the staged ROGUESQ.BAT unchanged.
3. Confirm 'rogue squadron.exe' is alive at +60 s and again at +90 s, with no #32770 dialog.
4. The person at the box confirms the picture and presses F12 once for a kept Shot_NNN.bmp.
5. Quit through the front end's Quit button ('Exit the game to the desktop'). PROCKILL is only the fallback.
6. Delete the stale GLRESET.TXT, then run GLRESET9.

PRIOR RUN. The same ROGUESQ.BAT ran on .243's own hardware on 2026-10-03. It was alive at 60 s with no dialogs, was ended by PROCKILL (not a clean exit), left no windows, and GLRESET read OK. The same pass blames such kills for TIE Fighter's later 'Error in Sound Config!'.

launchers.notes:
WHAT DRIVES IT: a script modelled on one() in docs/evidence/2026-10-03-243-metal-pass/metal243.py, not lanparty.py. lanparty.py cannot run this round for three reasons:
- DEFAULT_BOXES leaves out 243.
- Its launch is hard-coded to LAUNCH "C:\fleetmp\<key>.bat" (command.com /c in a new console, never run on .243).
- kill_games and shot_box compare exact names, but Win9x PROCLIST returns full paths.

1. PRE-FLIGHT (read-only). PING. REGREAD HKLM Software\RetroAgent: PciRescueBoot must report every installed PCI device present. On 2026-11-11 it read 'agent 1.98.0, uptime 45s: all 6 installed PCI device(s) present - nothing to do'; re-read it if .243 has rebooted since. DRIVERS STATUS must list PCI\VEN_121A&DEV_0002 at problem 0. PROCLIST must show no Glide client. If any check fails, launch nothing that opens Glide (neither the game nor GLRESET9).

2. STAGE. MKDIR C:\fleetmp. UPLOAD C:\fleetmp\RogueSquadron.bat as ASCII with CRLF line ends, including after the last line. DOWNLOAD it back and compare the bytes.

3. LAUNCH. LAUNCH C:\WINDOWS\COMMAND\START.EXE C:\fleetmp\RogueSquadron.bat. This is the 2026-10-03 route; that pass used C:\RETRO_AGENT\RUNT.BAT. START.EXE is an existing .exe, so agent 1.98.0 starts it without command.com (launchline.h), and START opens the batch in its own DOS box.

4. WHAT THE WRAPPER DOES. It switches to E:\GAMES (GamesDir; inv.json dest=E:\GAMES) and calls the staged ROGUESQ.BAT unchanged: tree and Glide check, cd ROGUE, start /w "Rogue Squadron.EXE", cd .., DESKFIX9 repaint, cls. ROGUES~1 is the 8.3 alias the 2026-10-03 pass used. The full tree listing has no FLEETRES.BAT and GAMERES has no rule for this title, so the game keeps its own resolution. There is no {name} or {host}: the game is single player.

5. OBSERVE at +60 s and again at +90 s: PROCLIST basename, WINLIST, no #32770. The person at the box confirms the picture, presses F12 once on the real keyboard, then selects Quit in the front end. Afterwards, DIRLIST E:\GAMES\RogueSquadron\ROGUE\SHOT* and DOWNLOAD the BMP.

6. FALLBACK, with no person or a game that will not quit: PROCKILL <unsigned pid from PROCLIST>. Wait about 5 s; ROGUESQ.BAT then runs DESKFIX9 and cls, and the DOS box closes.

7. GLIDE RESET, only after 'rogue squadron.exe' is gone. DELETE C:\RETRO_AGENT\GLRESET.TXT first, because it still holds the 2026-10-03 OK. Then LAUNCH C:\RETRO_AGENT\GLRESET9.EXE and poll DOWNLOAD C:\RETRO_AGENT\GLRESET.TXT every 1.5 s for up to 30 s, until a line starts with OK or FAIL (the same loop as sweep.py glreset).

8. CLEANUP. Close any leftover tty or #32770 window with WINKEY9X, using its exact title. Answer Y to the 'terminate?' prompt; its default button is No.

RogueSquadron.in_game_proof:
Single player, so there is no server roster. Evidence, strongest first.

(1) THE PERSON AT .243 sees the game on the monitor, which the Voodoo 2 drives through its passthrough. Expect the intro or front end, then the Player Roster ('Create a new player'). Long black screens between front-end screens are normal on a P166 (README).

(2) A KEPT FRAME. The person presses F12 on the real keyboard at the roster or in flight. The README says the game saves snapshots as Shot_NNN.bmp in its install folder, E:\GAMES\RogueSquadron\ROGUE, with no problems under Glide; the exe has '%s%03d.bmp' and '/TXT_EXP_SNAPSHOT/'. Fetch it with DIRLIST E:\GAMES\RogueSquadron\ROGUE\SHOT*, then DOWNLOAD, and convert it to PNG. Together with (1), this is the evidence for compat runs=verified. An injected UIKEY F12 is not the route: DirectInput probably ignores it, and moving focus to the game is a task switch, which the README warns can lock the game up. If no new SHOT file appears, that proves nothing either way.

(3) LIVENESS (supports 'runs' only).

HiddenAndDangerous.mp_summary:
SERVER: none on any platform. H&D Deluxe is peer-hosted and co-op only, so the dev host .132 has nothing to run (staged-title-server-matrix row 16; no entry in gameservers.py, no unit in ~/.config/systemd/user, no container). It plays over TCP/IP natively through DirectPlay 8: inet2.dll carries the DirectPlay8 Peer, Address and TCP/IP SP GUIDs. A session holds at most 4 players, 1 host and 3 joiners (manual p.13: '2 - 4 players ... co-operative team'; p.15: 'maximum number of players is 4 (1 HOST 3 JOIN)'). The whole fleet therefore cannot be in one game, and the 8 applicable XP boxes would need two sessions of 4. No LAN join of this title has ever been observed on the fleet (compat_mp is needs_human on every box).

WHY MULTIPLAYER CANNOT RUN UNATTENDED TODAY
(1) Every launch stops at 'Select game profile / < create new >'.
- This was measured with the host launcher on .171 on 2026-08-31 (README-FLEET). The profile screen comes before any menu.
- No box has a profile: Savegame\ is absent on 8 of the 9 installed boxes and empty on .184 (DIRLIST 2026-11-11).
- 'profile <name>' sets the default profile. README-FLEET says it cannot create one, but that was not measured.
- The agent has never driven this screen. README-FLEET records ENTER doing nothing on .124, and clicks, ENTER, SPACE and arrows doing nothing on .171.
- Only half of the reason is known. Mouse buttons are sampled as a level: DirectInput8 GetDeviceState(c_dfDIMouse2) in immediate mode (igraph2.dll 0x10007b2a), plus a WM_LBUTTONDOWN/UP byte. So UICLICK's zero-length click is lost.
- The keyboard works differently. igraph2 installs a WH_KEYBOARD hook only while its window is active (from WM_ACTIVATE), and the hook latches each key-down. A UIKEY therefore reaches the game exactly when HDE.exe's IGraph_Window has the focus. UIKEY ALT+F4 has closed HDE.exe in four .124 sweeps.
- The 08-30/08-31 key tests never checked focus. The 11-08 00:48 sweep shows the game rendering while the agent console held the focus. So 'the screen ignores keys' is unproven.
(2) Past that screen, the HOST must choose 'Start the game', then the campaign, mission, soldiers and equipment (manual p.15). HDE.exe 1.50 has no command-line route for this:
- 'mission', 'net_num' and 'net_port' are parsed and never read. net_num has no code reference; mission and net_port are only released at exit.
- 'net_connect' and 'net_connection_provider' exist only in the out-of-date -help text.
(3) The profile screen has been passed once on fleet hardware. README-FLEET and requires.json record profile screen -> Mission selection -> a 3D mission map on 2026-08-30. That was on the PIII 850 / GeForce2 GTS then at .124, which is today's .184. Its Savegame\ folder dates from 2026-08-30 05:59:17 and is empty. How the screen was passed is not recorded.

THE UNATTENDED ROUND
It is a SINGLE-PLAYER fullscreen render check on the 8 boxes, using the staged Play launcher. A box passes when the 3D 'Select game profile' screen shows at its own FLEETRES mode. This screen has already been photographed:
- on .123, .133, .143 and .171 on 2026-08-31, along with the then-.124 box and .246;
- on .124 with vcr-kmd on 2026-11-08.

ATTENDED MULTIPLAYER (see host_box)
- A person is needed at every box until a profile is staged. After that, probably only at each host. With net_join, the code at 0x468dea looks like an automatic join of the first session found. This is untested.
- Session A: host .123, joiners .110, .240 and .133.
- Session B: host .171, joiners .143, .184 and .124. .143 is kept off the host role because of its nv4_disp 0xEA bugcheck history, and .124's experimental D3D stays out of session A.
- Start the host first and get it to 'Waiting for other players'. Then start the joiners with net_join net_address <host>.
- The host's lobby lists each player by its Fleet<octet> name. The host then picks 'Start the game', campaign 1 / mission 1, soldiers, and start.
- No CD key, disc or SafeDisc is involved.

TO MAKE IT AUTOMATABLE (all untested): see server.changes_needed. The keyboard with verified focus comes first, then a UIDRAG held click, then a staged profile.

OPTIONAL, HARMLESS EXPERIMENT: start the host and joiners unattended with net_log, then DOWNLOAD each box's Fleet<octet>.log. HDE.exe calls its host routine 0x467890 when the menu first starts (0x4672c8), so DirectPlay may host and connect behind the profile screen. At best this is network-level evidence, never proof of being in one game.

ATTENDED ONLY. Never use this in the unattended round.

SESSIONS (the cap is 4 players including the host):
- Session A: host .123 (Athlon 64 4000+, HD 3850, 2 GB), joiners .110, .240 and .133.
- Session B: the same host bat on .171 (P4 2.8 GHz, FX 5500, rendered H&D on 2026-08-31), joiners .143, .184 and .124.

JOIN bat for the other 3 boxes of each session: the same text, with the start line replaced by:
start "" "C:\Games\HiddenAndDangerous\Bin\HDE.exe" net_join net_address "{host}" net_player "{name}" net_log
The staged 'Join Hidden and Dangerous - LAN.bat' <ip> does the same, except it names the player %COMPUTERNAME% and does not log.

With net_join, HDE.exe pushes its join screen at menu start (0x4672e2). At 0x468dea it calls 0x469e60 on the first entry of the session list once the list fills. That is probably an automatic join of the host at net_address. Untested.

net_log is a no-argument flag. Each box writes C:\Games\HiddenAndDangerous\<net_player>.log (e.g. Fleet123.log) in its working directory. The file is fclose'd and reopened for every line, so it survives a PROCKILL.

ORDER: the person at the host passes the profile screen and sees 'Waiting for other players', then the joiners launch. HDE passes a 15000 ms value to inet2, probably the connect timeout. Before sending any key to any box, check that WINLIST's foreground is IGraph_Window.

Once a profile is staged, append profile "<name>" to both start lines.

Attended multiplayer: the host spawns Windows' dpnsvr.exe (the DirectPlay enumeration helper), which outlives the game briefly; do not count it as the game. Start the host first: joiners started before it is hosting will time out (HDE passes a 15000 ms value to inet2, probably that timeout). Two sessions can run side by side, because joiners target a host IP.

Staging a profile has costs. GAMESYNC never deletes, so a staged Savegame\<name>.bin comes back after a player deletes it (README-FLEET). GAMESYNC also recopies any file whose size or mtime differs, so it overwrites a profile the game has updated: every sync resets the host's campaign progress. In a network game the host's profile decides which missions are open (manual p.15). Whether 'profile <name>' then skips the screen is untested.
Every applicable box has a working wave-out device (AUDIOINFO 2026-11-11), so the 2026-09-28 InitSound crash type is unlikely now. There is no CD check, key or SafeDisc.
