review_issues: WRONG MECHANISM (affects first_run, known_blockers and the automation leads): the recipe says UIKEY presses and releases 'in the same instant, so the game never sees them'. That holds for mouse buttons only. igraph2.dll reads the KEYBOARD through a WH_KEYBOARD hook: SetWindowsHookExA(2, 0x10003a70) at 0x10004429, installed by 0x100043e0. The WM_ACTIVATE (0x10003c95), WM_SETFOCUS and WM_KILLFOCUS handlers call 0x100043e0, so the hook exists only while IGraph_Window is active. The hook stores each key-down VK at +0x1d, and the value survives the key-up, so a zero-length UIKEY is seen whenever the game has the focus. Proof it lands: UIKEY ALT+F4 closed HDE.exe in four .124 sweeps (lan_20260929 part2, gametune_1001 baseline, d3d32_step16, d3dtune 11-08 02:08), each time with IGraph_Window in the foreground. README-FLEET's 08-30/08-31 key tests record no focus check, and WINLIST's foreground field did not exist until agent 1.91.0. In the 11-08 00:48 sweep the game rendered fullscreen while ConsoleWindowClass held the focus. So 'the profile screen ignores keys' is unproven, not established.

OVERSTATED: 'HDE.exe ignores WM_CLOSE, so it must be force-killed with PROCKILL'. igraph2's WM_CLOSE handler (0x10003e04) only sets a flag. In every .124 sweep, taskkill without /f left the game running for the full 25 s grace. But UIKEY ALT+F4 sent with the game focused closed it, with no force, in 4 of 5 sweeps. Only the 11-08 00:48 run (console focused, keys withheld) needed taskkill /f. PROCKILL, which lanparty's kill uses, stays a valid fallback, and the desktop mode came back.

OMITTED PRIOR EVIDENCE: README-FLEET ('VERIFIED ON HARDWARE ... 2026-08-30') and requires.json record that the profile screen was passed through to Mission selection and a 3D mission map. That was on the PIII 850 / GeForce2 GTS then at .124, which is today's .184 (PIII 845 + GeForce2 GTS). .184's Savegame folder is dated 2026-08-30 05:59:17 and is empty. How the screen was passed is not recorded, and no .bin survived. Whoever creates the profile to stage must exit the game cleanly and confirm Savegame\<name>.bin exists before copying it.

.197 EXCLUSION REASON CONTRADICTED: the box last inventoried at .197 (ADMIN-PC, Windows 7, i5-2400, HD 5450; it was .246 until 2026-09-26) has compat .246 runs=verified. That row comes from a 2026-08-31 GDI SCREENSHOT 0 at 1920x1080 showing the profile screen (perbox/evidence/246_HiddenAndDangerous_*.png). So 'never been tested' and 'GDI frames come back black on Windows 7' are both false for this title on that box. Also, the share's ADMIN-PC.json now describes the E5300 at .186 (two boxes share the hostname), so .197's current hardware is unconfirmed. The exclusion still stands: the box is switched off.
UNMEASURED CLAIM STATED AS FACT: 'the profile <name> option only selects a profile that already exists'. README-FLEET asserts this with no recorded measurement. It is relabelled as unmeasured.

UNSUPPORTED JOINER CLAIM: 'after that, only at each host' was given without a basis, and no LAN join of this title has ever been observed on the fleet. The code makes it plausible but it is untested. With net_join, HDE.exe pushes its join screen at menu start (0x4672e2), and at 0x468dea it calls 0x469e60 on the first entry of the session list once the list is non-empty, which looks like an automatic join.

INEXACT DETAILS: 'mission' and 'net_port' do have code references, one each, both exit-time releases (0x4bd7d5, 0x4bd771). net_num has none. None of the three is ever read, so the conclusion stands. DeusEx.mp_summary:
host_server. The server is deusex-server on 192.168.1.132: the staged DEUSEX.EXE run with -server under Wine in docker container 'dxsrv' (--net=host), on DXMP_Cathedral, game DeusExMPGame.
- Re-queried 2026-11-11 ~14:30: \info\ on :7791 answered 0/16 players, gamever/minnetver 1100, gamemode openplaying.
- Twelve core files and all five DXMP maps are md5-identical to the library tree, so client and server are the same build.

The client cannot be pointed at the server from the command line. DeusEx.exe ignores any map or URL there: .133's log reads 'Command line: 00_Training.dx', then 'Browse: DX.dx'. README-FLEET records '<ip>:7790' and 'deusex://<ip>:7790' failing silently. The menus move their cursor by relative mouse deltas, so they cannot be automated.

The join route is a User.ini key binding whose value is the console command, pressed with UIKEY. It is proven with F5: .246 joined .143's box-hosted server on 2026-08-31.

Each box's launcher:
- writes [DefaultPlayer] Name=Fleet<octet> and [Engine.Input] PageUp=open {host}:7790?Name=Fleet<octet> into System\User.ini (PageUp is unbound in the staged User.ini);
- calls the staged 'Play Deus Ex.bat' (FLEETRES resolution, GlideDrv on .124, fullscreen, deletes Running.ini).

PageUp takes F5's code path. DeusExRootWindow.VirtualKeyPressed consumes only Escape, PrintScrn, Ctrl+F9 and keys bound to DataVault screens, and passes anything else to the bindings.

launchers.bat:
@echo off
rem Deus Ex 1.112fm - whole-fleet LAN round: join the fleet server {host}:7790 as {name}.
rem DeusEx.exe ignores any URL on its command line - it always loads entry.dx, then DX.dx -
rem so the join is a User.ini key binding whose value IS the console command. The round
rem presses it with UIKEY PAGEUP once the rotating DX logo is up and the game window has
rem the focus. PageUp is unbound in the staged User.ini; afterwards restore User.ini from
rem DefUser.ini - the two are byte-identical in the library.
cd /d "C:\Games\DeusEx"
if not exist "C:\Games\DeusEx\System\User.ini" copy /y "C:\Games\DeusEx\System\DefUser.ini" "C:\Games\DeusEx\System\User.ini" >nul
"C:\Games\DeusEx\FLEETRES.EXE" -ini "C:\Games\DeusEx\System\User.ini" DefaultPlayer Name {name}
"C:\Games\DeusEx\FLEETRES.EXE" -ini "C:\Games\DeusEx\System\User.ini" Engine.Input PageUp "open {host}:7790?Name={name}"
rem The staged launcher does the rest: FLEETRES.BAT for this box's own resolution, GlideDrv
rem where a 3dfx card drives the screen, StartupFullscreen True, deletes a stale
rem System\Running.ini so no Recovery Mode wizard, start DeusEx.exe, exit.
call "C:\Games\DeusEx\Play Deus Ex.bat"
launchers.notes:
Renderer: the staged D3DDrv. The per-box mode comes from FLEETRES (GameResBoot targets today: .110 1600x1200; .123, .133 and .171 1280x960; .184 1024x768; .240 1920x1080).

Sequence:
1. LAUNCH, with no UIKEY/UICLICK sent to the box in the previous 200 s. This is a precaution: games launched this way took the foreground on every box in the 2026-10-13 round.
2. DOWNLOAD C:\Games\DeusEx\System\User.ini. It must contain 'PageUp=open 192.168.1.132:7790?Name=Fleet<octet>' and, under [DefaultPlayer], 'Name=Fleet<octet>'. If either is missing, FLEETRES failed or is absent: fix that before pressing anything.
3. Readiness: System\DEUSEX.log is 4096 B with an mtime newer than the launch. It is truncated to 0 B first; .110 has no log yet. Then wait about 25 s.
4. WINLIST foreground must be title 'Deus Ex', class DEUSEXUnrealWWindowsViewportWindow.
5. UIKEY PAGEUP.
6. Roster at +60 s. If the box is absent, run lanparty sniff on 7790 before any retry (see first_run).

Hardware notes:
- .184 (GeForce2 GTS 32 MB on ForceWare 71.89, the same driver as .143) bound D3DDrv on 2026-08-31, but its 4 KB log stops before any fallback line, so judge the renderer from a frame.
- .110 (7800 GS), .171 (FX 5500) and .240 (X1950 Pro) have never run Deus Ex on their current cards.

Teardown:
- PROCLIST, then PROCKILL <pid of DEUSEX.EXE>. PROCKILL takes a PID only; EXEC taskkill /f /im DEUSEX.EXE also works.
- FILECOPY C:\Games\DeusEx\System\DefUser.ini|C:\Games\DeusEx\System\User.ini. This runs inside the agent, and CopyFileA keeps DefUser.ini's mtime, so GAMESYNC's size+mtime test sees the staged file again.

DeusEx.in_game_proof:
1. Server roster (the strongest proof). UDP '\status\' or '\players\' to 192.168.1.132:7791 should list one '\player_<i>\Fleet<octet>' per box, with numplayers equal to the boxes that joined. The reply spans several datagrams; lanparty roster reads them all. DX has no bots, so every entry is a client. The launcher puts ?Name=Fleet<octet> in the open URL and in [DefaultPlayer] Name; the 2026-08-31 proof showed the stock name 'Player'.
2. Per-IP packets. lanparty sniff (tcpdump, dst 192.168.1.132 udp port 7790) should show traffic from each 192.168.1.<octet>. This is also the liveness check for a box that is connected but still loading the map.
3. Server log: delayed, and not guaranteed. Once 4 KB has accumulated (0 B today), /home/voidsstr/deusex-server/System/DEUSEX.log shows 'NetComeGo: Open <level> <date time> 192.168.1.<octet>:<port>', 'DevNet: Login request: ...' and 'DevNet: Join succeeded: Fleet<octet>'.
4. Per-box frame. The DX multiplayer HUD on DXMP_Cathedral: the belt reads WEAPONS x3 / GRENADES x3 / LOCKPICK / MULTITOOL / MEDKIT / TOOLS, with aug icons top-right. Reference: ~/lan-proof/unreal-rts/deusex-CLIENT-246-ingame-dxmp-cathedral.png.

A running DeusEx.exe proves nothing: a failed join just sits at the rotating DX logo.

first_run.symptom: Before launch: WINLIST foreground is the Starfield screensaver (WindowsScreenSaverClass 'Screen Saver', not secure) on 8 of 9 boxes when read today. On .186 it is the Start button.
first_run.keys: NONE. Send no UIKEY or UICLICK to the box in the 200 s before LAUNCH.
first_run.notes:
ForegroundLockTimeout is 200000 ms on .110 .123 .124 .143 .171 .184 .186 (0 on .133 and .240). Under Windows' foreground-lock rule, a key that dismisses the saver can stop the game from taking the foreground.

This is a precaution, not an observed failure:
- Games launched through the agent took the foreground on all 10 boxes in the 2026-10-13 UT99 round.
- On .124, the 2026-10-03 focus probe saw Descent 3, Quake II and Unreal Gold hold the keyboard at 30 and 60 s.
- The .124 2026-10-02 'focus on the agent console' reading came from that sweep's own WM_CLOSE and was withdrawn (vcr-kmd/evidence/gametune_1001/README.md).

first_run.symptom: 30-60 s after launch (about 2 min on .124): the rotating DX logo on black with NO main menu. This is the ready state, not a hang; the menu appears only after a click. Readiness tell: System\DEUSEX.log is 4096 B with an mtime newer than the launch. The engine first truncates an existing log to 0 B, so an mtime change alone fires too early; .110 and .186 have no log yet. Then wait about 25 s.
first_run.keys: DOWNLOAD C:\Games\DeusEx\System\User.ini and confirm 'PageUp=open 192.168.1.132:7790?Name=Fleet<octet>' and '[DefaultPlayer] Name=Fleet<octet>'. Then check WINLIST: if the foreground title is 'Deus Ex' (class DEUSEXUnrealWWindowsViewportWindow, pid = DEUSEX.EXE), send UIKEY PAGEUP.
first_run.notes:
The binding route was proven with F5 on 2026-08-31 (.246 joining .143's box-hosted server). PageUp takes the same path: DeusExRootWindow.VirtualKeyPressed only consumes Escape, PrintScrn, Ctrl+F9 and keys bound to DataVault screens, and returns False for the rest. UIKEY sends VK_PRIOR with KEYEVENTF_EXTENDEDKEY, so NumLock cannot turn it into NumPad9.

Do not send ENTER, ESCAPE or a click first: Enter=ParseLeftClick|Fire and Escape=ShowMainMenu in User.ini, and a click opens the main menu.

F5 is the proven fallback if PageUp is ever swallowed (rebind and relaunch).

first_run.symptom: At join time the foreground is NOT the Deus Ex window: the agent console 'Retro Remote Agent Version 1.98.0', a retro_chat.exe console (.133/.143/.240), Progman/Start, or the screensaver still up.
first_run.keys:
Screensaver: UIKEY SHIFT.
Otherwise: UIKEY ALT+TAB, re-check WINLIST, at most twice.
Last resort:
1. UICLICK at the screen centre. It gives the focus AND opens the main menu.
2. Wait about 2 s.
3. UIKEY ESCAPE to close the menu.
4. Re-check WINLIST.
5. UIKEY PAGEUP.
first_run.notes:
MenuMain has no key handler of its own. It inherits MenuUIWindow.VirtualKeyPressed, where IK_Escape runs SaveSettings() and root.PopWindow(), so ESCAPE returns to the logo. Do not press PAGEUP with the menu up: inside UI screens DeusExRootWindow forwards only DataVault hot keys, so a plain binding very likely does not fire. The click+ESCAPE sequence is untested.

If the box never shows up, it needs a person: Multiplayer > Join, then type 192.168.1.132:7790. The menu cursor follows relative mouse deltas, so absolute clicks miss.

first_run.symptom: 'Deus Ex Recovery Mode' wizard (#32770: 'The previous time Deus Ex was run, it was not shut down properly'). A System\Running.ini from a killed run is present right now on .123 .124 .143 .171 .184 .240.
first_run.keys: This should not appear: the staged Play bat the launcher calls deletes Running.ini first, and so does the .186 bat. If it does appear: UIKEY RETURN (the preselected Run button), or PROCKILL <pid of DEUSEX.EXE from PROCLIST> and relaunch the launcher.
first_run.notes: The First-Time and Video Configuration wizards are suppressed by [FirstRun] FirstRun=1112, present in every box's DeusEx.ini (downloaded today).

first_run.symptom: No Fleet<octet> in the server roster 60 s after PAGEUP.
first_run.keys:
First run lanparty sniff on port 7790 for 8 s.
- If that box IS sending packets, it is connected and still loading the map: wait, up to 3 min on .124, .133, .143 and .186.
- Only if it sends nothing: re-check that WINLIST shows 'Deus Ex' in the foreground, then UIKEY PAGEUP again.
first_run.notes: A second 'open' cancels a stalled pending connection. InitialConnectTimeout=500 s, so a silent first attempt would otherwise wait about 8 minutes. But a key sent during a slow map load waits in the message queue and can fire after the load, which disconnects the box and starts it over.

first_run.symptom: .186 only: 'Windows Security Alert - Windows Firewall has blocked some features of this program' for DeusEx.exe. The firewall is ON for the Domain, Standard and Public profiles with notifications on (REGREAD 2026-11-11), against the fleet convention.
first_run.keys: Read the dialog with WINLIST/SCREENSHOT. Either click 'Allow access' (UAC is OFF on .186, EnableLUA=0, so no consent prompt follows) or press UIKEY ESCAPE (Cancel). Then UIKEY ALT+TAB back to Deus Ex.
first_run.notes: Either choice lets the join work: replies to the client's own outbound UDP pass the stateful firewall. Allow adds an Allow rule, which matches the fleet's firewall-off convention. On Windows 7, Cancel typically adds a persistent inbound Block rule for DeusEx.exe, which would stop .186 hosting later. The alert can also steal the focus or minimise the game.

first_run.symptom: .124 only: ending the game.
first_run.keys: PROCKILL <pid of DEUSEX.EXE> (PROCKILL takes a PID) or EXEC taskkill /f /im DEUSEX.EXE. No ALT+F4, no WM_CLOSE.
first_run.notes: Under GlideDrv, an outside WM_CLOSE raises 'Critical Error - Assertion failed: RenDev [WinViewport.cpp line 2187]' (2026-10-02). taskkill /F left the board healthy.

README-FLEET records '<ip>:7790' and 'deusex://<ip>:7790' failing silently ('spinning intro forever'). The join therefore depends on a keypress (UIKEY PAGEUP, bound in User.ini) landing in the FOCUSED game window while no UI screen is up.
The menus move their cursor by relative mouse deltas and cannot be automated. If the binding never fires on a box, a person must type 192.168.1.132:7790 into Multiplayer > Join.

No fleet box has ever joined deusex-server (Wine on .132): staged-title-server-matrix.md says 'Reached from a fleet box: not attempted'. The only proven Deus Ex join is .246 to .143's box-hosted dedicated server (2026-08-31). Prove .123 before launching the rest.

2. Re-render the bats with {host} = that box.
3. Roster-query <box>:7791.
4. Kill that box's own client by PID, never by image name.

Every client puts a CD token in its connect packet: 'connect 31 <qport> <challenge> <n> <token*pi as %4.2f> <userinfo>'. CDTOKEN() at 0x2006bcb0 calls GetModuleFileNameA(NULL), then CreateFileA('<exe dir>\FFC11.DLL'). If the file is absent, it returns 0 (0x2006be47). Otherwise it XOR-decodes a block (4<=L<=512, L%4==0) with a 400-byte key (0x20001fe0 returns 0x201a8b28) and closes any 'SJE_CdPlayerClass' windows. For each GetDriveTypeA==5 drive it opens MCI cdaudio, sets the time format to ms, and reads the track count and per-track lengths. It plays the last second, which must reach MCI_MODE_PLAY, and the total length must be 4,470,000-4,830,000 ms. The track count must equal L/4, and tracks 2..N-1 must match the file. On success it returns 1. On the server, SV_DirectConnect stores atof(arg5)*0.7407*4, and SV_New_f refuses any client below 4.95. A loopback client gets Com_Error(3, string 0x411): that is caught, calls SV_Shutdown and runs 'menu wonerror', so the listen server dies. A remote client gets SV_DropClient(0x411). Its svc_disconnect handler (0x2000f886) puts the reason into menu_dc_reason and calls Com_Error(2,'Server disconnected'), which runs 'menu disconnect', not the wonerror box. FFC11.DLL is missing from the staged tree and from all 8 boxes (checked case-insensitively, re-read live 2026-11-11). Only FFC10.dll is there, which is Immersion's 'Feel Foundation Classes' PE. So the token is always 0, which is why mounting a SOF-labelled image on .143/.246 changed nothing. All three CDTOKEN callers (0x2000af0c, 0x2000afc6, 0x2000b112) are client connect builders, so a server never needs the disc itself.

(2) The '%c:\' GetVolumeInformationA loop at 0x20055350 is the cl_violence/sv_violence (parental-lock) object's constructor, reading DRIVE_FIXED volume serials. It is not a CD check. (3) 'The disc is not what it wants' is half right: the disc IS required, but only once FFC11.DLL exists. (4) The provisioning/discmount/specs/SoldierOfFortune-Host/Join.json notes are also stale. They say 'single player runs with no disc at all' (false: no level loads), and 'SoF 1 has no dedicated server binary, so LAN here is box to box', but SoF.exe has a built-in dedicated mode (+set dedicated 1; 'dedicated server console', AllocConsole).

review_issues: Remote-client failure path is misdescribed in mp_summary and known_blockers. A joiner refused by a live server does NOT get the 'WON Error!'/'menu wonerror' box. Verified: the client's svc_disconnect handler (svc 8, jump table 0x200100ac -> 0x2000f886) reads the reason short, puts its string in menu_dc_reason and calls Com_Error(2,'Server disconnected'). That throws 0, and the catch at 0x20021381 does CL_Drop + 'menu disconnect'. 'menu wonerror' (0x20021317) is reached only from Com_Error(3), the LOOPBACK branch of SV_New_f. A joiner therefore shows the generic disconnect menu carrying the CD text, and its log says 'ERROR: Server disconnected'.

Wrong md5 for 'the staged SoF.exe'. 2f4db3771d51d8b585bbea695041e40c is the pre-patch retail 1.03 (provisioning/patches/idtech2/apply.py). The staged, mode-9-patched exe that was disassembled is b4ed42272887b16a8ecdb92c919a507d (md5sum of the library file; tests/python/test_patch_idtech2.py; the scout's own excerpt header). The patch touches only the mode table, so the conclusions stand.

.186 exclusion reason is partly wrong, though the exclusion stands. (a) The box has an NVIDIA GTX 1650 (PCI 10DE:1F82) with no driver bound. HWPROFILE classifies it as sm3.0 from the PCI id, so the gate did not 'fail open on an unclassifiable GPU'; it cannot see the missing driver. (b) 'Cannot render' is overstated: Windows' software GDI Generic OpenGL 1.1 is always there; it is just unplayable at FR_Q2WIDE 9 = 1920x1080. (c) The 'Win7 GDI returns black' rule is the DWM/WDDM case and does not clearly apply to the XDDM Standard VGA driver.

in_game_proof named expected modes for only 4 boxes and said 'the other boxes use the GAMESYNC-written value'. That is the wrong mechanism: the launcher recomputes FR_Q2WIDE at every launch and passes it on the command line. Expected from the 2026-11-11 GAMERES reads: mode 8 (1280 960) on .110 .123 .124 .133 .143 .171, mode 6 (1024 768) on .184, mode 9 (1920 1080) on .240.

SoF's log semantics are not stated, and they matter. SoF 1.03's Com_Printf opens '%s/sof.log' with mode 'a', and for logfile > 1.0 it reopens, appends and closes on every line (0x2001df56-0x2001dffe). The log is never truncated, so the launcher's delete is mandatory, and the check must require exactly one 'Cpu info' header. With developer 1 the log is also no longer 'about 4 KB'.

Risk note 'name, developer and deathmatch are command-line only' is wrong. 'name' is registered CVAR_ARCHIVE|USERINFO (flags 3) and 'maxclients' 0x15 (includes ARCHIVE), so both would be written to user\config.cfg on a clean exit. Only developer/logfile (flags 0) and deathmatch (0x10 latch) are unarchived. PROCKILL writes nothing, so the practical conclusion holds.

mp_summary overgeneralises 'a whole-fleet game cannot get past the host's own client': that is true only of a LISTEN host. SoF.exe has a built-in dedicated mode ('dedicated' cvar flags 8, 'dedicated server console', AllocConsole import; all three CDTOKEN callers are client connect builders, so a server never needs the disc). A dedicated host therefore has no own client, but every joiner is still dropped by the same SV_New_f check, so 'no shared game today' stands. The discmount spec notes ('no dedicated server binary ... box to box', 'single player runs with no disc') are stale too.

load_wait_sec 75 has no timing evidence for the slowest box (.133, P3-700/256 MB), where server init and the map load must finish before the check fires. Raised to 90, with polling of sof.log for the ERROR line.

The .124 capture command differs from the proven lanparty.py call. Aligned to 'EXECW 30 C:\vcr\vcrctl.exe fbshot C:\fleetmp\fb.bmp' (minor). Thief2.mp_summary:
Thief II is single-player only. This round is therefore a single-player render check, not a multiplayer game.

Why there is no multiplayer:
- Retail Thief II is single-player.
- cam.cfg carries `no_network`.
- docs/staged-title-server-matrix.md row 39 says "no multiplayer".
- None of the 27 entries in gameservers.py SERVERS is a Dark-engine server, and no Thief or Dark unit or container exists on the host.
- scripts/gameindex/README.md lists Thief as single-player.
- Thief2.exe still contains the dormant DirectPlay code the Dark engine shared with System Shock 2 (net_host, net_client, net_player_name, 'Could not initialize DirectPlay'), but no staged gamesys or menu uses it.
- The community T2MP co-op mod is not staged (searched case-insensitively).

So the whole fleet cannot be in one game. The round runs on all 8 XP boxes at the same time, which works because nothing is shared.

Steps:
1. Kill any leftover Thief2.exe first: PROCKILL <pid>, using the pid from PROCLIST (lanparty.py's kill_first does this). Otherwise the old Thief2.log cannot be deleted and a second instance starts.
2. UPLOAD C:\fleetmp\Thief2.bat. It calls the staged "Play Thief 2.bat", which:
   - runs FLEETRES and writes this box's mode into cam.cfg `game_screen_size`;
   - picks the D3D9 or DX6 display for vcr-kmd;
   - starts Thief2.exe, then exits.
3. LAUNCH it on all 8 boxes at once.
4. At T+45 s, prove the main menu on every box with four checks: PROCLIST, WINLIST, a fresh Thief2.log and a full-size SCREENSHOT 0. Re-check slow boxes (.133, .184) at 90 s before calling them failed.
5. Optional: three UICLICKs (New Game, Start Game, Continue) put each box into mission 1, "Running Interference", for a frame of the 3D world.
6. End the round:
   - From the main menu: UICLICK Quit.
   - From a mission: UIKEY ESCAPE, UICLICK Quit, then UICLICK Quit again on the main menu.
   - Otherwise: PROCKILL <pid>. PROCKILL takes a numeric PID only; `PROCKILL Thief2.exe` is answered 'Invalid PID' and kills nothing.
   The game ignores WM_CLOSE and ALT+F4.
7. Confirm every box is back on its desktop at its persisted mode, with DISPLAYCFG get or the size of a fresh SCREENSHOT 0.

Expected modes today, read from each box's cam.cfg (FLEETRES writes the same value again at launch):
- .110: 1600x1200
- .123, .124, .133, .143, .171: 1280x960
- .184: 1024x768
- .240: 1920x1080 (menus pillarboxed)

Other boxes:
- .145 and .197 are powered off. Thief2 is deployed on both and has never been tested.
- .139 is not a retro box.

excluded_boxes.reason:
No display driver, and none can be installed on this copy of Windows.
- OS: Windows 7 Professional RTM, 32-bit (Win32_OperatingSystem OSArchitecture=32-bit, Version 6.1.7600, no service pack, no hotfixes).
- Card: NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1650 (PCI\VEN_10DE&DEV_1F82, TU117), running on the 'Standard VGA Graphics Adapter' driver. DRIVERS STATUS calls it 'generic'.
- NewDark 1.26 removed the software renderer, so Thief II needs a Direct3D 9 HAL.
- NVIDIA never published a 32-bit driver for any Turing (GTX 16xx/RTX 20xx) GPU. Its 32-bit support ended with the R390 branch, which predates Turing. So no NVIDIA driver exists for this card on this install.
- What would make it a candidate: a 64-bit Windows 7 SP1 reinstall (the Pentium E5300 is x86-64 capable) plus the SHA-2 code-signing update, which recent NVIDIA Windows 7 x64 packages likely require, then an NVIDIA Win7 x64 driver (R418 or later). Alternatively, a card that has a 32-bit Windows 7 driver.
- The Thief2 tree and shortcut are already on the box (cam.cfg is 1920x1080).

Not deployed, and cannot run it.
- There is no Thief2 folder or shortcut in E:\GAMES. The gamegate operator override says 'not wanted on .243' (scripts/gamegate/overrides.txt, 2026-09-29; compat.py: gated).
- The NewDark Thief2.exe has PE subsystem 5.0 (measured from the header), which the Windows 98 loader refuses (requires.json min_os winxp).

launchers.notes:
How the launcher works:
- It reuses the staged launcher. Its md5, f38f3e8e4cef1a030389f868c86f8277, matched the library on all 9 boxes (scout probe, 2026-11-11).
- Each box's cam.cfg differs from the library only in `game_screen_size`. cam_ext.cfg, dark.bnd, cam_mod.ini, Thief2.exe and FLEETRES.* match the library by size.
- `call` must stay the LAST line: Play Thief 2.bat ends with `exit`, which closes the wrapper's cmd.

MaxPayne.mp_summary:
Max Payne 1 has no multiplayer of any kind. I re-checked the PE import tables on 2026-11-11. MaxPayne.exe (SafeDisc 2.51.020, entry point 0x8cc056 inside stxt371), rlmfc, e2mfc, sndmfc, grphmfc and e2driver\e2_d3d8_driver_mfc import no WS2_32, WSOCK32, DPLAY/DPLAYX, DPNET or WININET. None of them carries a networking string; the only 'dplay' hits are inside 'isSoundPlaying'. There is no server for it on 192.168.1.132: it is row 21 of the staged-title server matrix, has no unit, and is not in gameservers.py SERVERS. The 'whole fleet in one game' requirement therefore cannot apply.

The round is a per-box single-player fullscreen render check. Launch the seven unattended XP boxes (.110 .123 .133 .143 .171 .184 .240) together, each into its own instance. Run .124 only with a person at the box (docs/v56k-benchmark-plan.md); otherwise record it 'not run - attended-only'. The proof is the main-menu frame plus the live display mode.

Each box must pass two gates.

1. SafeDisc 2.51.020 must accept the DAEMON Tools 3.47 mount.
   - The game's own code has run before on six boxes:
     - .124: menu, 2026-09-29.
     - .133: in-game, 2026-08-31.
     - .143 and .171: startup-dialog frames, 2026-08-31 (.171 was then on its Intel 865G).
     - .184: full saved settings, Driver=GeForce2 GTS.
     - .123: only the game-created 'Customized Game' and 'Parental Lock' keys; no frame.
   - .110 has never launched it; DAEMON Tools went on 2026-09-29.
   - .240 tried twice on 2026-08-31 and failed before any game code ran: first a locked DT unit, then a failed mount that started the game against another disc.
   - Whether Emulation > SafeDisc must be ON is less settled than README-FLEET says. It was needed on the GeForce2 box on 2026-08-30. But .143 reached the dialog on 2026-08-31, and the fleetbook log for 2026-09-01 says its emulation was found OFF and only then set to 'All options ON'. The state cannot be read remotely, so treat .110 and .240 as unknown, not as expected refusals.

2. The startup dialog. -nodialog only clears the show-dialog flag. The game still opens 'Max Payne v1.05' when the saved video settings fail validation: no saved Driver, an adapter or mode index of -1, or a width, height or bpp of 0.
   - Verified in the unwrapped exe, read only: -nodialog clears 0x867afc (default 1) at 0x40cbc9, and 0x40a6a7 copies it to dialog+0xfe. 0x40b470 skips DoModal only when that flag is clear AND 0x407190 passes, and it continues only on IDOK.
   - Play's OnOK writes the settings (0x4078ae -> 0x406980, WriteProfileString/Int) before CDialog::OnOK. One press of Play therefore persists even if the game is PROCKILLed later.
   - Expect the dialog once on .110, .123, .143, .171 and .240, where no Driver is saved.
   - .124, .133 and .184 already hold a Driver that matches their current adapter, so they should go straight to the main menu.

excluded_boxes.reason: ADMIN-PC, Windows 7 RTM (6.1.7600). Its card is an NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1650 (PCI 10DE:1F82, SUBSYS 8D921462). It runs on Windows' generic 'Standard VGA Graphics Adapter' driver (display.inf; DRIVERS STATUS state=generic), which gives the game's Direct3D 8 renderer no hardware device. The box also reports disc_mount=false, with no DAEMON Tools or WinCDEmu, so the SafeDisc 2.51 image cannot be mounted. MaxPayne.in_game_proof:
Max Payne is single-player, so the proof is a fullscreen render on each box. Take the steps in order of strength.

1. SCREENSHOT 0 of the main menu: the MAX PAYNE logo plus the item list (Resume Game / Tutorial / New Game / Load / Save / Options / Credits / Quit). Take a second frame about 20 s later. A menu background with NO item list that is pixel-identical across frames is the .124 freeze signature from 2026-10-04, not a pass.
2. While MaxPayne.exe runs, DISPLAYCFG get (EnumDisplaySettings ENUM_CURRENT_SETTINGS, the live mode) must equal the box's GAMERES target: .110 1600x1200, .240 1920x1080, .184 1024x768, and 1280x960 on .123, .124, .133, .143 and .171.
3. WINLIST: the foreground pid is MaxPayne.exe's. No 'Max Payne v1.05' dialog, SafeDisc message box or DAEMON Tools modal is left.
4. DIRLIST C:\Games\MaxPayne shows no mount-error.txt. The launcher deletes it at start and writes it only on failure.
5. On boxes that showed the dialog: after Play, HKCU\Software\Remedy Entertainment\Max Payne\Video Settings has Driver set to this box's adapter. REGREAD the key and pick the value out. That value can only be written by the dialog's OnOK, so it proves SafeDisc passed and the startup gate cleared.

A running MaxPayne.exe alone is NOT proof: it sits alive and idle at the startup dialog, and a SafeDisc refusal box keeps it alive too.

first_run.symptom: The screensaver is in the foreground: the WINLIST foreground class is WindowsScreenSaverClass. This was true on all 8 boxes at 13:32 on 2026-11-11.
first_run.keys: UIKEY SHIFT, wait 3 s, then re-check WINLIST. Do this BEFORE the LAUNCH.
first_run.notes: This is the pattern scripts/benchmarks/d3_timetest.py uses. A game started under a screensaver can come up behind it, and then the startup dialog never gets the focus. The fleet screensaver is Starfield, and the agent does not make it password-protected.

first_run.symptom: The 'Max Payne v1.05' startup dialog appears despite -nodialog. It is a standard Win32 dialog owned by MaxPayne.exe, with Play / Options... / Parental Lock... / Quit and a Video Settings group (Display Adapter, Screen Mode, Acceleration). Expect it within about 30 s on .110, .123, .143, .171 and .240.
first_run.keys: First take SCREENSHOT 0, and check that Screen Mode shows the box's target. Then, if the WINLIST foreground pid is MaxPayne.exe's and the title is 'Max Payne v1.05', send UIKEY RETURN. Otherwise UICLICK <rect.left+472> <rect.top+53> using that window's WINLIST rect, which is the Play button. Confirm the dialog is gone and MaxPayne.exe is still alive.
first_run.notes:
Play is control id 1 (IDOK) in dialog resource 133 and carries BS_DEFPUSHBUTTON, so RETURN presses it. The second button's resource text is '&Advanced...', but it shows as 'Options...' at runtime.

The code path is at 0x40b470 / 0x407190, and the field evidence is the .124 frame from 2026-09-29 04:26.

Play's OnOK saves Driver, CPU Driver, HW Acceleration Level and the mode BEFORE the dialog closes, so later launches skip it even after a PROCKILL. Screen Mode defaults to the registry mode FLEETRES wrote. If it shows another mode, still press Play, and record the mismatch.

Never press Quit or ESC, and never close the dialog: any result other than IDOK makes the game exit.

first_run.symptom: SafeDisc refuses. A small OK-only box appears, such as 'There is a problem with your game installation. You may need to reinstall the game to fix it.' A launcher that fell back to another disc may show an insert-CD style prompt instead.
first_run.keys: Take SCREENSHOT 0 first. Send no keys. PROCKILL MaxPayne.exe, then ~f51e43.tmp if it is still alive. Then DOWNLOAD C:\Games\MaxPayne\mount-error.txt if it exists.
first_run.notes:
No keypress gets past this, and the box may be owned by the SafeDisc helper rather than MaxPayne.exe. Record the box as BLOCKED, not as a broken tree.

The remedy needs operator approval: in the DAEMON Tools tray menu, Emulation > 'All options ON'. That entry is a SET; the four single entries are toggles. If the launcher killed daemon.exe, start C:\Program Files\D-Tools\daemon.exe first. Verify that the d347bus\Cfg khjeh blob changed (the 2026-11-11 values are in scout-MaxPayne\box_*.json), then re-run.

Its outcome on .110 and .240 is unknown: .143 passed on 2026-08-31 while its emulation was apparently off.

first_run.symptom: A DAEMON Tools modal appears: 'Unable to mount image. Cue sheet: Unit is locked.' This was seen on .240 on 2026-08-31.
first_run.keys: If it is in the foreground, send UIKEY RETURN. The launcher already taskkills daemon.exe when no drive appears, which normally removes the modal.
first_run.notes: A locked unit lasts until a reboot, so the title cannot run on that box this boot. The launcher then writes mount-error.txt and may start the game against another disc. The boxes were freshly rebooted today, with about 90 min uptime at 12:31. Do not run another title's mount on the same box during this round.

first_run.symptom: The launcher console shows a 'Max Payne could not start' or 'THE MOUNT FAILED' banner.
first_run.keys: No keys. DOWNLOAD C:\Games\MaxPayne\mount-error.txt.

first_run.symptom: The main menu appears: the MAX PAYNE logo with Resume Game / Tutorial / New Game / Load / Save / Options / Credits / Quit. This is the end state of the round.

End with PROCKILL on MaxPayne.exe, then on ~f51e43.tmp if it is still alive. Never kill daemon.exe. Then DISPLAYCFG get should show the desktop back at its persisted mode.

known_blockers: SafeDisc 2.51.020 must accept a DAEMON Tools 3.47 mount on each box, and that is unknown on .110 (never launched) and .240 (never past the mount). README-FLEET says Emulation > SafeDisc must be ON: it was needed on the GeForce2 box on 2026-08-30, and with it off the game shows 'There is a problem with your game installation'. The fleet record is mixed, though. .143 reached the dialog on 2026-08-31, and on 2026-09-01 its emulation was found OFF and then set to 'All options ON'. The setting cannot be read remotely, because the khjeh blob is encrypted and differs on every box, and it cannot be set from the registry or the daemon.exe CLI. A refusal needs an operator-approved tray change.
.124 is attended-only for this title (docs/v56k-benchmark-plan.md). It froze on 2026-10-04 on the vcr-kmd D3D HAL, cause not established. Skip it unless a person is at the box.

.110, .123, .143, .171 and .240 stop at the 'Max Payne v1.05' startup dialog on their first launch despite -nodialog, because no Driver is saved yet. A launch-and-wait round would record an idle process unless Play is pressed once. It is a standard dialog and can be automated (see first_run). On 2026-08-31 a sweep recorded exactly this idle state on .133 as 'no GAME process after 90s'. The same row on .123 (no mounter then) and .240 (locked unit) had other causes.
There is no multiplayer at all, so the round cannot put the whole fleet in one game. Each box runs its own single-player instance.
risks: .124 (V5 6000, experimental vcr-kmd DX7-class D3D HAL, software T&L): Max Payne froze once on 2026-10-04. While it ran, everything at normal priority crawled: wmic took more than 40 s and a WM_CLOSE taskkill more than 60 s. Use long agent timeouts and end the game with PROCKILL (TerminateProcess).

rlmfc.dll's R_System::determineProcessorSpeed (0x10025546) raises the process to HIGH_PRIORITY_CLASS with a TIME_CRITICAL thread while it times the CPU, then restores both. It has a single caller and runs once at startup. A stall of a few seconds right after launch is normal on the single-core boxes. It does not explain a freeze at the menu.

These are first renders on several setups. Max Payne has never been seen rendering at 1920x1080 on a 16:9 LCD (.240): the compat DB's .246 'verified 1920x1080' row is a desktop-only frame. It has also never rendered at 1600x1200 (.110), or on the Radeon HD 3850 AGP (.123), GeForce 7800 GS (.110), FX 5500 (.171) or 6800 (.143). .171's only frame was on its old Intel 865G. The dialog lists every driver mode of at least 640x480 with no aspect filter, and the retail e2_d3d8 driver links every EnumAdapterModes mode, so the GAMERES modes should be accepted. The Fixes-pack DLLs do not change mode enumeration.

Mounting replaces whatever is on DAEMON Tools device 0. .240's HKLM Run entry StarCraftCD mounts C:\ISO\STARCRAFT.ISO there at logon, and .143's BZoneCD mounts BZONE.iso there. .143 also has StarCraftCD '-mount 3,...', but its DT has only Device0. A later StarCraft or Battlezone round on those boxes needs a re-mount or a re-logon.

Concurrent mounts on one box are the launcher's own leading explanation for a locked DT unit. A parked SafeDisc disc is a weaker one; the install-utility skill says not to leave one parked. Run nothing else that mounts on a box during its Max Payne round. If you unmount afterwards, use 'start "" /b daemon.exe -unmount 0', never a blocking EXEC: a locked unit answers with a modal that blocks daemon.exe forever.

On a failed mount the staged launcher taskkills daemon.exe, the tray app. It may then start the game against whatever disc is present, which leads to a SafeDisc refusal; mount-error.txt records this. After a mount it performs, it taskkills every Install.exe to stop the disc's autorun.

Send RETURN or ESC only when the WINLIST foreground pid is MaxPayne.exe's. RETURN on the desktop opens the selected shortcut and would launch another game. ESC, Quit or closing the startup dialog makes the game exit.

VOLID=MAX_PAYNE (the PVD label) never matches the Joliet label 'Max Payne' that Windows reports. The MARKER maxpayne.ico sits in the disc root, so :finddisc still finds a disc that is already mounted and skips the mount. A re-mount happens only when the disc is absent. This is harmless.
After a forced kill, DISPLAYCFG get must show the desktop back at its persisted mode, as it was on .124 after the 10-04 kill.

The SafeDisc helper ~f51e43.tmp runs beside MaxPayne.exe. It was seen only on .124, in the 09-29 sweep, and its name is specific to the SafeDisc version. Do not treat it as the game process. Kill it after MaxPayne.exe, by pid.

review_issues: MATERIAL - the launch plan contradicts itself. mp_summary says 'Launch all 8 applicable XP boxes together', and that set includes .124. But docs/v56k-benchmark-plan.md and the recipe's own .124 launcher notes restrict .124 to an attended run ('Max Payne kept for an attended run'; 'Run Max Payne on its own, with a person watching'). Corrected: launch the seven unattended boxes (.110 .123 .133 .143 .171 .184 .240) together, and run .124 only with a person at the box; otherwise record it 'not run - attended-only'.

MATERIAL - the recipe overstates the case that DAEMON Tools emulation must be ON. It cites '.143 ... all four options ON 2026-09-01' as support for .143's pass. The fleetbook change log for .143 on 2026-09-01 11:23 actually says 'DAEMON Tools emulation was OFF and was turned ON via the tray menu's All options ON'. Yet .143 had already reached the game's own startup dialog on 2026-08-31 10:43 (frame perbox/evidence/143_MaxPayne_Play_Max_Payne.png). So either this image does not always need emulation (CLAUDE.md measures it carrying 600 bad-EDC sectors), or the setting changed in between. The emulation state of .110 and .240 is unknown, so they are not 'most likely' refusals. Wording is softened throughout; the operator remedy is kept as conditional.

MATERIAL - a risks entry is factually wrong: 'the launcher simply re-mounts on every launch'. The first half is right. I read the image: PVD label MAX_PAYNE, Joliet label 'Max Payne', and the root holds maxpayne.ico / MAXPAYNE.ICO, so VOLID=MAX_PAYNE never matches. But :finddisc then checks the MARKER, which finds a disc that is already mounted, and the launcher prints 'disc already present - not mounting' and skips the mount. It re-mounts only when the disc is not mounted.

MATERIAL - the .186 exclusion misstates the hardware. ADMIN-PC has an NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1650 (PCI 10DE:1F82, SUBSYS 8D921462; HWPROFILE gpu.hardware_id), running on Windows 7's generic 'Standard VGA Graphics Adapter' (display.inf; DRIVERS STATUS state=generic). That is a missing display driver, not missing hardware. The shortcut suppression itself comes from requires_capabilities disc_mount, and the box reports disc_mount=false. The exclusion still stands, but the readiness report should list the GTX 1650 driver as a driver item, not as 'cannot run'.

F:', so MaxPayne.exe was started against another disc. HKCU still holds only Video Settings, so the game's code never ran. The conclusion is unchanged.

RedFaction.mp_summary: There is no Red Faction server on 192.168.1.132: nothing in gameservers.py, ~/.config/systemd/user, docker or ss uses RF or UDP 7755. One XP box has to host. .123 runs `rf.exe -dedicated teamdm -lanonly -port 7755`, which needs no disc (proven up on .171, 2026-08-31, with 'dm'). The other 7 applicable boxes play as clients, and .123 plays too: its client binds 7756 through HKCU ForcePort, which rf.exe reads only when -port is absent (0x4b1180-0x4b11b6, the -port switch object 0x7d9458). rf.exe has no command-line connect and no connect console command. Its switches are -dedicated -lanonly -level -mod -port -trackerip -startdir -startpos -timedemo -frameratetest -mip -voodoo -voodoo3, and its 22 console commands contain no connect. So every client joins through its menu: MULTI > JOIN GAME > server list > row > Join. Screenshot-guided UICLICK works there. The menu cursor is absolute, because rf.exe reads GetCursorPos then ScreenToClient (0x51d46f-0x51d482) and recentres only in mouselook mode. Every box renders RF at 640x480x16: rf.exe reads its mode from HKCU (default 640x480x16) and FLEETRES writes HKLM, so one set of coordinates serves all. How the LAN path works, read from the binary: with HKCU ListLAN=1 the Join screen opens with LAN Only ticked and immediately broadcasts the 3 bytes 00 00 00 to 255.255.255.255:7755 (hard-coded). It makes no automatic tracker query. With LAN Only ticked, the Get Servers button re-sends that LAN broadcast (0x44b943 -> 0x44aa60 -> 0x47b2b0); only with LAN Only off does it call the dead THQ tracker. Refresh All only re-queries rows already in the list. Add Server (a dotted IP, optionally :port) adds a row and queries it by unicast. MultiServerListBinDerDunDat=1 skips the first-visit help popup. A client on the server's own box must move off 7755, or its bind fails ('Invalidating TCP') and it can list nothing. Joining has never been proven on this fleet, and the compat DB has multiplayer at needs_human on every box. The 08-31 notes say Get Servers hit the tracker 'even in LAN Only mode', but the binary says that happens only with the box unticked, so that session probably never had the Join screen's LAN Only box ticked. Each client also writes gamestart.txt with 'name Fleet<octet>'. rf.exe runs that script after the local player exists, so the multiplayer name should be set and box identity can come from any client's console 'info'. If the menu join cannot be driven, the round still gives a fullscreen render check: each box ends at the RF main menu, launched through the staged Play Red Faction.bat.

host_box.command:
@echo off
rem Red Faction LAN round - DEDICATED SERVER on {host}. Needs no disc and no 3D.
rem HKCU UpdateRate must be non-zero or rf.exe prints "You have not properly selected
rem your network connection" and dies AFTER binding 7755 - install.reg seeds it, this re-asserts it.
rem Explicit -port 7755 so a leftover ForcePort can never move the server: clients find
rem LAN servers by a broadcast to UDP 7755, hard-coded in rf.exe.
rem teamdm = TeamDM, 16 players, 30-minute maps. Avoid dm: rf.exe clamps its $Max Time 1 up to
rem 5 minutes, so it changes level every 5 minutes and joins during a change are refused.
reg add "HKCU\Software\Volition\Red Faction" /v UpdateRate /t REG_DWORD /d 200000 /f >nul 2>&1
cd /d "C:\Games\RedFaction"
start "" /D "C:\Games\RedFaction" "C:\Games\RedFaction\rf.exe" -dedicated teamdm -lanonly -port 7755
host_box.notes: Start this about 30 s before the clients (lanparty's default host wait). Then confirm it from the dev host with the RF query: a UDP payload of 00 00 00 to 192.168.1.123:7755 must return a packet with d[0]==0x01 and d[3]==0x87 (see server.roster_how). A bound 7755 is NOT proof: a server missing UpdateRate binds 7755 and then dies at 'Hit a key to exit...'. Its window title is '%s Dedicated Server', i.e. 'Red Faction Dedicated Server'. The server name is '$ME's Dedicated TeamDM', where $ME is the Windows user .123's agent runs as. Why .123: Athlon 64 4000+, 2 GB RAM, one NIC, XP firewall off (EnableFirewall=0), HKCU UpdateRate=200000 present, D3D initialised there before (rfd3d.id, 2026-08-29). Alternate host: .110 (P4 2.8, 1.1 GB, firewall off; RF has never run there). .123 also plays, using the host-box client launcher with ForcePort=7756. That works because the server's explicit -port 7755 makes rf.exe ignore ForcePort (the only ForcePort read is at 0x4b1199). rf.exe's single-instance mutex is created and closed at once (CreateMutexA 0x523d33, CloseHandle 0x523d6b), so a second rf.exe on the box is not blocked. .123's client has NEVER run with a mounter: its 08-31 run died at 'NO DISC MOUNTER', and Daemon Tools 3.47 was installed there on 2026-09-28. Expect its first mounted launch to be slow, and treat a failure there as box-specific. The server console accepts typed commands ('info', 'say', 'quit') once its window has focus. After the round: PROCKILL rf.exe (clients first, .123 last; both of .123's processes are rf.exe), or type 'quit' in the server window. Then reset .123: reg add "HKCU\Software\Volition\Red Faction" /v ForcePort /t REG_DWORD /d 0 /f. Otherwise a later server there without -port binds 7756 and is invisible to LAN discovery.

server.unit: none on 192.168.1.132 - box-hosted: rf.exe -dedicated teamdm -lanonly -port 7755 on 192.168.1.123 (no systemd unit, no docker; RF is not in gameservers.py SERVERS; nothing on .132 listens on UDP 7755)
server.query_kind: rf_gameinfo. Request: the UDP payload 00 00 00 (type 0 game_info_request, u16 size 0), the same 3 bytes the client broadcasts (0x47b2b0) and unicasts (0x47b2e0). Reply, from the builder at 0x47af40: 01, then <u16 LE size = len-3>, then 87, then <server name>\0, then <gametype 0=DM 1=CTF 2=TeamDM (table at 0x5994f4)>, <numplayers>, <maxplayers>, then <level>\0, then <mod>\0, then <flags: 1=dedicated, 2=option bit 0x400, 4=password>. The builder answers only while its multi flag (0x64ec01) and server flag (0x64ec02) are set. Whether it answers during a level change is an inference, so retry on timeout. lanparty.py roster() has no 'rf' kind yet; one would be needed, aimed at the host box (roster() already uses host_ip_of(t) for host titles).
server.roster_how: The UDP reply carries the player COUNT only. From the dev host: s=socket(AF_INET,SOCK_DGRAM); s.settimeout(3); s.sendto(b'\x00\x00\x00',('192.168.1.123',7755)); d=s.recv(2048); require d[0]==1 and d[3]==0x87; i=d.index(b'\0',4); name=d[4:i]; gametype,players,maxp=d[i+1],d[i+2],d[i+3]; j=d.index(b'\0',i+4); level=d[i+4:j]. Names come from the console. On any NON-host client (for example .110 or .171), check WINLIST foreground (class Volition), then send UIKEY TILDE, UIKEY TEXT:info, UIKEY RETURN, SCREENSHOT 0, and UIKEY TILDE to close. The 'Clients (ping) ----------' block prints one '"<name>" (<ping>)' line per player. With gamestart.txt the names are Fleet<octet>; otherwise they read Default. IPs appear only in the dedicated server's own 'info' ('"%s" (%d) (%s)'). Reaching that window means taking .123's fullscreen client out of the way, because the agent has no window-activate command, so do it last, if at all.
server.log_how: There is no log file. rf.exe contains a 'Red Faction Multi Log' writer (0x47c520), but its enable check 0x47c840 is hard-wired to 'xor al,al; ret', so the file is never opened. Joins print only in the dedicated server window on .123 ('Player %s has joined' / '%s has joined'). That window is visible to SCREENSHOT 0 only when nothing fullscreen covers it, i.e. at the end of the round after .123's client is closed. The host box is a fleet box, so lanparty.py sniff (tcpdump on .132) cannot see client-to-host traffic.
server.bots_note: Red Faction has no multiplayer bots, so every slot is a human client. 8 boxes fit in teamdm's 16 slots.
server.changes_needed: None for this round. The stock 'teamdm' entry in the staged dedicated_server.txt is used as-is. Avoid 'dm': Max Time 1 is clamped to 5 minutes, so it changes level every 5 minutes. Later, optional, and NOT made: (a) run rf.exe -dedicated under Wine on 192.168.1.132 like shogo/descent3, so the server log and tcpdump are on the host and no box juggles ports; (b) Dash Faction, which adds an rf://host:port command-line join, needs exactly RF 1.20. Every frame of this tree reads 'Version 1.00', although the patch register and the 2001-09-03 link date say 1.20, so confirm the build before staging it. XP compatibility is unverified, and it is the user's decision.

launchers.bat:
@echo off
rem Red Faction LAN round - CLIENT {name} on the HOST box {host}. The dedicated server here
rem owns UDP 7755. rf.exe reads HKCU ForcePort only when -port is absent, so this client
rem binds 7756 while the server, started with an explicit -port 7755, keeps 7755.
rem rf.exe has NO command-line connect - the join is MULTI, JOIN GAME, the LAN list, Join.
rem ListLAN=1 ticks LAN Only: the list broadcasts on entry, and Get Servers re-broadcasts
rem on the LAN instead of calling the dead tracker. MultiServerListBinDerDunDat=1 skips the help popup.
rem gamestart.txt runs after the local player exists, so its name line sets the MP name.
reg add "HKCU\Software\Volition\Red Faction" /v UpdateRate /t REG_DWORD /d 200000 /f >nul 2>&1
reg add "HKCU\Software\Volition\Red Faction" /v ForcePort /t REG_DWORD /d 7756 /f >nul 2>&1
reg add "HKCU\Software\Volition\Red Faction" /v ListLAN /t REG_DWORD /d 1 /f >nul 2>&1
reg add "HKCU\Software\Volition\Red Faction" /v MultiServerListBinDerDunDat /t REG_DWORD /d 1 /f >nul 2>&1
cd /d "C:\Games\RedFaction"
> "C:\Games\RedFaction\gamestart.txt" echo name {name}
call "C:\Games\RedFaction\Play Red Faction.bat"
launchers.notes: Launch only after the host server answers the RF query (lanparty already skips kill_first on the host box, so the server survives). The staged Play Red Faction.bat (checked in the library) calls FLEETRES.BAT, cd /d's into the tree, deletes any stale mount-error.txt, mounts _disc\RedFaction_Disc2.cue with Daemon Tools 3.47 (-mount 0,...; WinCDEmu fallback), waits for volume RF_2, suppresses AutoPlay, starts rf.exe, and runs 'exit'. That is why the call is the last line. gamestart.txt: rf.exe strips its extension, appends .txt and runs it as a console script during startup (0x4b226d -> 0x50af80). The local player already exists by then (0x4b1fbf -> 0x4a22a0), so 'name Fleet123' should apply. On the dedicated server the same line is a NULL-guarded no-op. This box's client has never run with a mounter (Daemon Tools arrived 2026-09-28), so a failure here is box-specific. After the round, set ForcePort back to 0 on this box.

first_run.symptom: The box is in the Starfield screensaver. All 9 XP boxes were in ssstars.scr during the scout, and a game started under it may not get the foreground for exclusive D3D mode.
first_run.keys: UIKEY SHIFT just before LAUNCH
first_run.notes: Harmless key; the agent's uiguard does not refuse it.

first_run.symptom: Intro Bink movies (THQ logo, then the intro) play before the main menu. The 30 s frame on .171 (08-31) was the THQ logo; the menu was up with no keys at 60 s on .124 (11-08) and at 90 s on .133 (08-31).
first_run.keys: None by default: wait load_wait_sec, then SCREENSHOT. Only if a movie frame is still showing, send UIKEY ESCAPE once and re-check.
first_run.notes: Never send ESC or RETURN blind. rf.exe has 'Are you sure you want to quit Red Faction?', which ESC on the main menu probably raises; an odd number of ESCs can leave it up, and RETURN would quit. If it shows, click No (position from the frame). Send keys only when WINLIST foreground is class 'Volition', title 'Red Faction'. RF does not exit on WM_CLOSE, so close it with PROCKILL.

first_run.symptom: RF main menu at 640x480: left column NEW / LOAD / MULTI / OPTIONS / EXTRAS / QUIT, with NEW highlighted.
first_run.keys: UICLICK 115 210 (MULTI). Button bands measured on the 08-31 .133 frame: NEW y66-110, LOAD y127-171, MULTI y188-232, OPTIONS y249-293, EXTRAS y310-354, QUIT y371-415, x about 50-180.
first_run.notes: UICLICK lands where aimed: in menus rf.exe takes the cursor position from GetCursorPos then ScreenToClient (0x51d46f-0x51d482) and recentres only in mouselook. Keyboard navigation is unverified.

first_run.symptom: 'No Internet Connection Detected' with a 'Continue Anyway' button after MULTI (the RAS check in rf.exe; not reported on 08-31).
first_run.keys: UICLICK 'Continue Anyway' (read its position from SCREENSHOT)
first_run.notes: Only if it appears.

first_run.symptom: Multiplayer screen: buttons PLAYER / JOIN GAME / CREATE GAME / BACK, and a player panel with a 'Player name' field and a 'Character Model' selector.
first_run.keys: UICLICK JOIN GAME (position not recorded: take one SCREENSHOT; every box runs 640x480, so one box's coordinates serve all)
first_run.notes: The Player name field should already read Fleet<octet> from gamestart.txt. If it reads Default, the name can be set here (click the field, UIKEY TEXT:Fleet<octet>, RETURN; not tested) or in-level with the console.

first_run.symptom: Server list. With ListLAN=1, LAN Only is ticked on entry, the LAN broadcast has already gone out, and no tracker query is made. The row "<user>'s Dedicated TeamDM" from 192.168.1.123 should appear within about 5 s.
first_run.keys: Wait 5 s. If the list is empty, confirm LAN Only is ticked (never untick it) and UICLICK 'Get Servers'; with LAN Only ticked that re-sends the LAN broadcast. Then UICLICK the server row, then UICLICK 'Join'.
first_run.notes: 'Refresh All' only re-queries rows already listed, so it cannot find an unlisted server. Fallback: 'Add Server', UIKEY TEXT:192.168.1.123:7755, OK; it adds the row and queries it by unicast (dotted IP only; the port defaults to 7755). If 'Could not connect to Game Tracker, check your internet connection.' appears, LAN Only was off: dismiss it with RETURN and tick LAN Only (that click itself broadcasts). There is also a 'Filter' cycle control; make sure it reads All. Without MultiServerListBinDerDunDat=1 a first-visit help popup appears; dismiss it with OK.

first_run.symptom: 'The game is between levels, try joining again in a minute or so.'
first_run.keys: UIKEY RETURN, wait 30 s, UICLICK Join again
first_run.notes: Should not happen with teamdm (30-minute maps). With dm it happens every 5 minutes, because Max Time is clamped to 5-60.

first_run.symptom: Daemon Tools modal 'Unable to mount image. Cue sheet: Unit is locked.' (seen on .240 and .124, 2026-08-31), or the in-engine 'Insert Red Faction CD #2 (ESC exits game)'.
first_run.keys: UIKEY RETURN on the Daemon Tools modal; ESCAPE exits the CD prompt
first_run.notes: Keys cannot fix this. The Daemon Tools unit lock clears only on a reboot (safe-reboot.py, after the activation check). Mark the box failed and read C:\Games\RedFaction\mount-error.txt with DOWNLOAD.

first_run.symptom: Joined, but no HUD or weapon is visible: teamdm has Force Respawn false, so the player may wait unspawned.
first_run.keys: UICLICK once mid-screen (fire) to spawn
first_run.notes: The server already counts the player, so this is only for the in-level frame.

first_run.symptom: Optional, once in the level: the box shows as Default (gamestart.txt did not apply).

first_run.notes: The console 'name' command is registered ('Set player name').

RedFaction.in_game_proof: Strongest first. (1) Count: from the dev host, send UDP 00 00 00 to 192.168.1.123:7755. The reply must have d[0]==1 and d[3]==0x87. After the server name come gametype=2 (TeamDM), then numplayers, which must equal the number of boxes that joined, then maxplayers=16; the level is a dm*.rfl. (2) Per-box identity without touching .123: on one non-host client (for example .110 or .171), with the foreground checked, send UIKEY TILDE, UIKEY TEXT:info, UIKEY RETURN, SCREENSHOT 0, UIKEY TILDE. The 'Clients (ping)' block must list one "Fleet<octet>" (<ping>) line per box. (3) Each box's own frame shows the in-level view with HUD, not the menu or the server list (.124 via vcrctl fbshot). (4) Optional and last: the dedicated server's own 'info' on .123 adds IPs ("<name>" (<ping>) (<ip>)), but its window sits under .123's fullscreen client and the agent cannot activate it, so it costs that client. A running rf.exe is NOT proof, and .123 runs two of them.
RedFaction.screenshot_notes: XP GDI 'SCREENSHOT 0' captures RF's fullscreen D3D8 frame: the 640x480 main menu was captured that way on .133 and .246 (08-31). The perbox frame named 143_RedFaction is actually the 1024x768 desktop with no RF window, and 171's is the THQ intro, so neither shows the menu. Expect 640x480 on every box: rf.exe reads Resolution Width/Height/Bit Depth from HKCU (defaults 640/480/16), while the launcher writes HKLM. On .124 (Voodoo 5 6000 on vcr-kmd) use EXECW 30 C:\vcr\vcrctl.exe fbshot <bmp> then DOWNLOAD (lanparty's VCR_BOXES path). A GDI frame there is the old desktop. Its 11-08 fbshots show the menu at 60 s, after a black frame on 09-29. RF runs at 16 bit, so the 8-bit palette caveat does not apply. .186 (Win7) is not used.
known_blockers: No unattended join exists in stock rf.exe (md5 0ba3b15d64a702333a4d9a0815f782b7, build.ver 177). It has no connect switch, and none of its 22 console commands is a connect, so every client must click through MULTI > JOIN GAME > server list > Join.

Joining has NEVER been proven on this fleet (compat DB multiplayer=needs_human on all boxes; staged-title-server-matrix row 27 'needs a decision'). The 08-31 notes say Get Servers went to the dead tracker 'even in LAN Only mode', but rf.exe's Get Servers sends the LAN broadcast whenever the Join screen's LAN Only box is ticked. So that run most likely never had it ticked, and the LAN path (forced on here with ListLAN=1) is untested on hardware.

Per-box resolution does not reach RF. Play Red Faction.bat writes Resolution Width/Height/Bit Depth to HKLM, but rf.exe reads HKCU (root 0x80000001 in 0x52b2a0), so every box runs RF at its default 640x480x16. A library fix would have to write HKCU and use only HUD-supported widths (640/800/1024/1280). It is not made here, because uniform 640x480 is what keeps the click coordinates the same on every box.
The client needs disc 2 (volume RF_2, marker MUSIC.VPP) mounted by Daemon Tools 3.47 or WinCDEmu. RF has no CD key and no SafeDisc (a plain volume check). The dedicated server needs no disc.
risks: .124: RF through the experimental vcr-kmd D3D HAL has rendered only its MENU (11-08); it was a black frame on 09-29. A level is a new D3D workload, and the HAL has stalled games before. Watch it, and PROCKILL rf.exe if its fbshot is black at 60 s.

Several clients are untested on RF: .110 never ran it, and .123's client has never run with a mounter (Daemon Tools installed 2026-09-28; its mount-error.txt is the stale 08-31 'NO DISC MOUNTER'). The .143 and .184 menus were never photographed. Expect some boxes to fail for box-specific reasons unrelated to the join.

Daemon Tools unit lock ('Unit is locked', .240 and .124 on 2026-08-31) can only be cleared by a reboot. Two launchers racing on one box reproduce it, so start one RF launcher per box (the host bat does not mount).

Blind ESC or RETURN can open, then confirm, 'Are you sure you want to quit Red Faction?'. Screenshot before every key, and check that WINLIST foreground is class 'Volition', title 'Red Faction'. RF held the foreground during play in the 11-08 sweeps, but retro_chat (.133/.143/.240) and agentwd (.124) consoles exist and took the focus after a WM_CLOSE.

Getting the dedicated server window on .123 in front (for 'info' or its join lines) takes .123's own fullscreen D3D8 client out of exclusive mode or requires killing it. Do it last, or rely on the UDP count plus a non-host client's 'info'.

If ForcePort=7756 is left on .123 after the round, a later dedicated server there without -port binds 7756 and is invisible to LAN discovery, which is hard-wired to 7755. Reset it to 0 in cleanup (a GAMESYNC re-merge of install.reg also restores 0). ListLAN=1 and MultiServerListBinDerDunDat=1 left behind are harmless, arguably useful.

gamestart.txt is written into C:\Games\RedFaction on each box. It is not in the library, and GAMESYNC never deletes it. It only sets the name and is a no-op on the dedicated server; delete it in cleanup if the tree must stay pristine.

RF does not exit on WM_CLOSE (the 11-08 sweeps force-closed it; the desktop was restored), so cleanup must PROCKILL rf.exe or type 'quit' in the server console. Killing rf.exe on .123 also kills the server.
Low RAM: .124 and .133 have 255 MB; requires.json floor is 128 MB.
.123's own client is assumed to see the local server through Windows broadcast loopback. If it does not appear, use Add Server 192.168.1.123:7755 on that box.
Version label is uncertain: the menu says 'Version 1.00' while the patch register says 1.20. Every box has the same md5, so it does not matter here. It matters before staging any community patch.

review_issues: SERVER-LIST STEP IS BACKWARDS ON 'Get Servers'. With HKCU ListLAN=1, the Join screen's LAN Only checkbox starts ticked: 0x44c5ec-0x44c611 copies ListLAN into the checkbox byte 0x63ea08. The Get Servers handler 0x44b920 (wired to its button at 0x44cc41) tests that byte at 0x44b943 and calls the LAN search 0x44aa60, which sends the broadcast from 0x47b2b0. It reaches the tracker (0x482970) only when LAN Only is unticked. So 'NEVER click Get Servers' forbids the one LAN rescan button.

'if empty, UICLICK Refresh All' cannot work. Refresh All (0x44cde0) only re-flags rows already in the list (it loops over count 0x63edb4), so on an empty list it does nothing. The fallback that does find a server is Add Server. Its callback 0x44cf20 takes a dotted IP only (inet_addr), splits on ': ', defaults the port to 7755, adds a row and queries that row.

The recipe repeats the 08-31 note 'Get Servers contacts the tracker even in LAN-Only mode' (README-FLEET.txt, FINDINGS.md). The binary contradicts it. With LAN Only off, simply opening the Join screen runs the tracker query by itself (0x44c4cc calls 0x44b920). The 08-31 session most likely never had the Join screen's LAN Only box ticked; the Create Game screen has its own LAN-only option, and -lanonly only affects dedicated servers. The recipe is right that the LAN broadcast path is untested. It is wrong about why 08-31 failed.

dm's '$Max Time 1' is not a 1-minute map. rf.exe clamps Max Time to 5..60 minutes (clamp call at 0x46dd79-0x46dd92 with 5.0f/60.0f), so dm changes level every 5 minutes. The host-bat comment and the first_run 'between levels' note were wrong. teamdm (30 min) is still the right choice.

Three blind ESC presses can strand the box. rf.exe contains 'Are you sure you want to quit Red Faction?', and ESC on the main menu probably raises it (not tested). An odd number of ESCs after the intro has ended can leave that dialog up, and a later RETURN would quit. No keys are needed: the .124 sweeps on 2026-11-08 reached the main menu at 60 s, and .133 on 08-31 was at the menu at 90 s.

The gamestart.txt name hedge is too pessimistic. The local player is created during startup (0x4b1fbf calls 0x4a22a0, which stores 0x7c751c via 0x4a3190), before gamestart.txt runs at 0x4b226d. So 'name Fleet<octet>' should take effect on every client. It is a safe no-op on the dedicated server, where 0x4a22a0 sets the local player to NULL. Box names are therefore available for identity proof, though not yet tested on hardware.

The identity proof through the server window on .123 is impractical. The agent has no window-activate command, and that window sits under .123's own fullscreen client. Getting to it costs that client: ALT+TAB risks a lost D3D device, and killing the client drops it from the list first. A console 'info' on any non-host client lists every player name, using the strings 'Clients (ping) ----------' and '"%s" (%d)'.

The Multiplayer screen layout is wrong. It has PLAYER / JOIN GAME / CREATE GAME / BACK plus a player panel with a 'Player name' field and a 'Character Model' selector (rf.exe .rdata 0x199b48-0x199c8c), not JOIN GAME / CREATE GAME / BACK.

Bad evidence citations. perbox/evidence/143_RedFaction_Play_Red_Faction.png is the 1024x768 DESKTOP with the agent console and no RF window, and 171's frame is the THQ intro; only 133's and 246's show the 640x480 menu. The compat DB's '.143 verified 1024x768' RF row rests on that desktop frame, so RF on .143 is not proven by it.

Untested client boxes are not flagged. .123's client has never run with a disc mounter: its mount-error.txt, downloaded today, still reads 'NO DISC MOUNTER IS INSTALLED' from 2026-08-31, and Daemon Tools 3.47 was installed there on 2026-09-28. .110 has never run RF (no rfd3d.id). .240's last attempt left 'MOUNT FAILED - started against an unrelated disc' (F:). .184's and .143's menus were never photographed. Only .133, .124 and .246 (now off) have menu frames.

The version label is uncertain. The recipe says 'stock rf.exe 1.20'. The patch register (_patches/README.txt:49) and rf.exe's link date (2001-09-03) agree, but every RF frame shows 'Version 1.00' (the minor-version global 0x7d9738 is never written) and README.TXT is the v1.00 readme. This does not matter for this round, because every box has the same md5. It does matter for the Dash Faction suggestion, which needs RF 1.20.

The .243 reasoning is partly wrong. A Voodoo 2 is not Glide-only: it has Win9x Direct3D drivers, and rf.exe even has -voodoo for such cards. The real exclusions are the operator override plus the P166 sitting below RF's 300 MHz floor (and 127 MB below its 128 MB floor).

Focus theft is overstated. Both 11-08 sweeps were on .124 only, and in both RF held the foreground (class Volition) at 30 s and 60 s. The console took the focus only after the sweep's own WM_CLOSE. Check WINLIST before every key anyway.

Minor: 'clients find servers ONLY by broadcast' ignores the unicast Add Server path (frame update 0x44d0e0 sends via 0x47b2e0). The switch list also includes -voodoo3. With ListLAN=1, opening the screen also skips the automatic dead-tracker query, which is one more reason to set ListLAN.

Could not be run live: no RF server exists anywhere yet. A UDP 00 00 00 to 192.168.1.123:7755 and to .132:7755 timed out, and nothing on .132 uses 7755 (gameservers.py, user units, docker, ss). So neither the query nor any join log could be exercised. 'No log file' is confirmed in the binary: the 'Red Faction Multi Log' writer at 0x47c520 is gated by 0x47c840, which is 'xor al,al; ret', so the log never opens.

SeriousSamFirstEncounter.title_display: Serious Sam: The First Encounter (Croteam 2001, retail v1.00, Serious Engine 1)
SeriousSamFirstEncounter.mp_summary: host_server. The TFE v1.00 dedicated server, ssam-tfe-server on 192.168.1.132, takes joins on UDP 25600 and answers a GameSpy \status\ query on 25601. It has 16 slots and no bots. Re-queried 2026-11-11 around 14:30: 0/16, Desert Temple, Fragmatch, fraglimit 20, gamemode paused. Eight XP boxes join through the staged 'Join Serious Sam TFE - LAN.bat' with the argument {host}:25600. That launcher calls FLEETRES and rewrites Scripts\Game_startup.ini: sam_bFullScreen=1, the box's own WxH and gfx_iRefreshRate, and ogl_bExclusive=1 where FR_UE1DEV is Glide (only .124; its current file carries it). It mounts _disc\SeriousSamTFE.iso (501,800,960 B, present on all 8) with DAEMON Tools 3.47 from C:\Program Files\D-Tools (all 8). If DT yields no drive it falls back to WinCDEmu, which only .124 has. It then starts 'Bin\SeriousSam.exe +connect host:25600'. TFE 1.00 has no +quickjoin. Verified in the disassembly: +connect calls StartMenus("join") (0x421c46/0x421c4d). That path always shows CONNECTION SETTINGS (0x40a295 calls 0x40b080 with no condition), then SELECT PLAYERS with START as the default gadget (0x40d452), whose action is JoinNetworkGame (0x409d80). So after the window is up, every box needs UIKEY RETURN to load LAN gaming and UIKEY RETURN on START. The fleetmp wrapper appends sam_bFirstStarted=0 and the LAN sam_strNetworkSettings to the box's own Scripts\PersistentSymbols.ini when they are missing. Today that means .124, .133, .143 and .171. The intent is that every box gets the same RETURN, RETURN: no Information box, LAN pre-selected. This pre-seed has NEVER run on hardware: the pre-selection is read from the code. Confirm with a frame on first use. Prior evidence: on 2026-10-13, 10 of 10 boxes joined at once through the same staged Join launcher. That count included .145 and .197, both off now. That run used per-box keys and no pre-seed: RETURN on Information, DOWN x4 + RETURN, then RETURN on START. .124 and .133, the two 255 MB boxes, timed out after repeated 'CRC check OK' lines. .133 got in by retrying in the same process; .124 was relaunched. A failed join leaves SELECT PLAYERS up with START focused, so the first retry is one more RETURN. Player names cannot be set per box: they live only in the binary Players\Player0.plr. Identify boxes by IP in the server's engine log.

excluded_boxes.reason: Cannot render the game and has no Join shortcut. Windows 7 Professional 32-bit (6.1.7600, no SP). Its NVIDIA 10DE:1F82 (TU117, GeForce GTX 1650) runs on Microsoft's Standard VGA driver with no NVIDIA driver installed. Serious Engine 1 needs an accelerated OpenGL ICD and has no software renderer. NVIDIA's 32-bit drivers ended with R390, before this card shipped, so a 64-bit OS or another card is probably needed. disc_mount=false as well, so requires.json's per-shortcut disc_mount gate suppressed Play and Join and left only the Host LAN shortcut (DedicatedServer.exe). Never run that shortcut in this round: it would bind 25600/25601 on the box.

Title not installed and no shortcut (plan_args installed=false). compat.py shows it gated by an operator override, 'not wanted on .243'. Its Pentium 166 is also below requires.json's 233 MHz floor, and with disc_mount=false SeriousSam.exe's CD check would fail.
